summary: PsiLogic adds a dual-EMA detector of normalized gradient-norm instability to Adam, dynamically damping chaotic phases and fading to zero as training stabilizes, which also acts as an implicit warmup. Three-seed H100 tests report NLP perplexity 7.79 versus AdamW's 8.17 and ViT accuracy 0.244 versus 0.223, while diffusion is tied. Transformer-heavy arenas run 1.2-1.8x slower and three seeds leave several comparisons statistically fragile.
source_title: PsiLogic: Chaos-Aware Active Cancellation for Adam with a Fair Cross-Domain Benchmark

summary: SpecGradFilter suppresses a small low-frequency portion of selected layer gradients during federated local updates, using an FFT projection or spatial detrending approximation. The motivating spectral disagreement is measured under structured parameter layouts, not asserted as a universal frequency semantics. With 100 clients and 10% participation, ResNet-20 CIFAR-10 accuracy at severe Dirichlet heterogeneity improves from FedAvg's 58.40% to 78.05% over three runs. Communication payload is unchanged, but local FFT computation and temporary buffers are added. Convergence requires sufficient retained global descent signal and bounded filtered heterogeneity; filter ratios are fixed and large-language-model scaling remains open.
source_title: SpecGradFilter: A Spectral Gradient Filtering Framework for Taming Federated Heterogeneity

summary: This work uses Armijo backtracking along Adam's first-step direction as a curvature probe, capping the requested learning rate at twice the smallest accepted step. For language models, up to nine additional probes during the first fifty updates handle rapid early sharpening. The deployed protocol reports approximately 1% overhead and restores parameters, buffers, and random states so a nonbinding cap changes nothing. Classifier and GPT-2 experiments show divergence prevention across aggressive learning-rate grids. It is a safety wrapper, not an accuracy guarantee: stable runs can remain poor, initialization-only caps fail at GPT-2 scale, and periodic rate-growth controllers can hurt.
source_title: Directional Curvature from Armijo Backtracking: A Low-Cost Sharpness Probe and a Calibration-Free Learning-Rate Safeguard for Adam

summary: FedACT forms a globally corrected AdamW direction and reallocates coordinate magnitudes using local-global agreement, preserving smaller nonzero steps where trust is weak. Federated vision Transformers, CNNs, LLM pretraining, and LLM fine-tuning consistently improve over strong adaptive baselines, with the largest gains under stronger heterogeneity. The abstract provides no common numerical effect and the promised implementation has not yet been released.
source_title: FedACT: Federated Adaptive Coordinate Trust Modulation for Robust Transformer Training under Data Heterogeneity

summary: DSGNAR trains physics-informed neural networks using a doubly sketched Gauss–Newton model: CountSketch compresses residuals, a randomized cosine embedding compresses parameters, and one small SVD supplies multiple regularized candidate steps. A target actual-to-model decrease ratio jointly controls regularization and step length, first seeking favorable conditioning and then aggressive descent. Experiments span Burgers, chaotic dynamics, high-dimensional Poisson, and Navier–Stokes with several architectures and precisions. Reported single-precision Burgers error reaches 4.75e-7 in 9.8 seconds on the stated setup. Evidence concerns comparatively small PINNs, not LLM pretraining; sketch size explicitly trades accuracy against runtime and candidate probing adds objective evaluations.
source_title: An Optimisation Framework for the Well-Conditioned Training of Physics-Informed Neural Networks

summary: Develops compressed decentralized stochastic subgradient methods for nonsmooth nonconvex training, including heavy-ball/Nesterov, sign-regularized, and momentum-tracking variants. Unbiased and contractive compressors use different error compensation and time-scale choices; convergence concerns critical cluster points under boundedness, definability, and diminishing-step assumptions. Eight-agent ResNet-20/CIFAR-10 experiments compare quantization and ten-percent sparsification over ring and random graphs, with five seeds. New variants improve selected accuracy/communication tradeoffs, but CHOCO-based extensions can lead at the smallest communication budgets, so no uniform dominance is established. The contribution includes genuinely new update variants alongside a framework reanalyzing established methods, rather than treating every included baseline as newly invented.
source_title: Decentralized Stochastic Subgradient-type Methods with Communication Compression for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization

summary: SNG implements natural-gradient and Sobolev mirror-descent steps by Fourier transforming the gradient, dividing by a positive metric symbol plus damping, and transforming back. Known translation-invariant Fisher or Hessian operators admit exact updates without constructing dense matrices; other symbols instead define structured preconditioners. A periodic one-dimensional quadratic convolution experiment reproduces dense natural-gradient trajectories to double-precision accuracy and illustrates FFT scaling across dimensions 128–8192. This is a specialized geometric implementation rather than evidence of a universal neural-network optimizer: exactness requires Fourier-diagonalizable geometry, and general nonperiodic bounded domains lie outside the stated setting. No large-model training comparison is provided.
source_title: Fourier-Diagonalized Natural Gradients and Sobolev Mirror Descent

summary: SCAPE derives a one-step-delayed sparse communication mask from AdamS first-moment statistics and reconstructs second-moment quantities from one synchronized sparse buffer. GPT-345M and Llama-500M retain dense quality at 90-99% sparsity; the 500M run saves up to 43.3% wall time and a 1.8B test reaches 3.26x step speedup. Evidence stops at 1.8B on 32 GH200 GPUs and tightly couples optimizer logic to the distributed system.
source_title: SCAPE: Accurate and Efficient LLM Training with Extreme Sparse Communication

summary: FedCGNM groups classes by within-group variance, maintains and unit-normalizes a momentum for each group, then sums them as the client update; FedHOO parallelizes exploration of resampling rates. It consistently beats baselines on four public long-tail datasets and a proprietary chip-defect dataset, with a convergence analysis that allows time-varying sampling. The optimizer is specialized to federated class imbalance and the public repository is only a placeholder.
source_title: Class-Grouped Normalized Momentum and Faster Hyperparameter Exploration to Tackle Class Imbalance in Federated Learning

summary: The paper offers a mechanistic, not architectural, analogy between Muon's orthogonalized update and a residual connection: weaker immediate gradient alignment can preserve representations that downstream layers can use more easily. In controlled two-layer linear models, SGD fitted the local factor faster, but Muon completed end-to-end learning in fewer total steps under every tested joint or alternating schedule because the downstream factor adapted faster; the evidence remains limited to linear settings.
source_title: Muon as a Residual Connection

summary: Ember gives embedding and language-head tables a row-by-column factored second moment without a first-moment state, while hidden weights can continue to use AdamW or Muon. State falls from O(2VD) to O(V+D), about 1500x for a 50k-by-768 table, and a 30-run modded-nanogpt study reports mean validation loss 3.2788. The design is intentionally limited to token-interface matrices rather than a replacement for the whole optimizer.
source_title: Token Geometry

summary: ZO-Act builds a low-rank activation basis once from a calibration batch, freezes it, and optimizes lightweight coefficient matrices using forward-only loss queries and Adam. This reduces perturbation dimension and permits adaptation of frozen INT4 backbones. On Llama-3-8B, RTE accuracy improves from ZO-Muon's 81.2% to 87.0%, and eight-task commonsense accuracy reaches 70.8%. Under 4,500 matched forward queries, RTE runtime is 42.0 minutes at 16.1 GB; INT4 memory falls to 5.8 GB. Fixed-subspace bias remains, most baseline scores are imported from prior work, and first-order fine-tuning still offers stronger accuracy and runtime when feasible.
source_title: ZO-Act: Efficient Zeroth-Order Fine-Tuning via One-Shot Activation-Informed Low-Rank Subspaces

summary: DMD separates the direction and magnitude of low-rank factors, with an overparameterized form and a cheaper recursive variant designed to accelerate motion between saddles. For matrix factorization it proves exponentially faster convergence than Burer-Monteiro gradient descent, with numerical support on sensing and completion. The method targets low-rank matrix problems rather than general neural-network training, and no public implementation is linked.
source_title: Direction-Magnitude Decomposition for Low-Rank Matrix Optimization: Faster Convergence and Saddle-to-saddle Dynamics

summary: CWGD-Cosine modulates a cosine learning rate using minibatch gradient diversity weighted by a diagonal Hessian proxy. Hutchinson probes initialize curvature estimates, while per-coordinate minibatch variances drive the scheduler. On small strongly convex quadratics, twenty-seed tests report approximately twenty-percent lower terminal error, including a comparison charging twenty extra initialization probes. Guarantees assume diagonal quadratic curvature and isotropic noise; the paper reports failures under extreme-condition-number transients and Rosenbrock nonconvexity, plus degradation on nonconvex classification models. Static curvature becomes stale, and periodic-refresh cost differs from the one-time quadratic accounting. This is a narrow scheduler proposal, not validated general neural-network optimization; its advertised repository was unavailable.
source_title: Curvature-Weighted Gradient Diversity: A Noise Measure for Geometry-Adaptive SGD Schedules

summary: ARp-LS modifies adaptive tensor regularization for objectives whose highest modeled derivative is only locally Lipschitz, with its growth controlled by the gradient norm. It multiplies the Taylor-model regularizer by a clipped gradient magnitude and adds gradient-based acceptance checks alongside the usual reduction ratio. Under stated regularity assumptions, nonconvex stationarity and convex objective-gap complexity match classical tensor rates up to logarithmic factors. The second-order AR2-LS variant beats classical cubic regularization on three synthetic regression benchmarks but generally trails AN2CLS. Experiments count iterations and solve cubic subproblems exactly; they do not establish large-scale neural-training speedups or inexpensive higher-order implementation.
source_title: Fast Adaptive Tensor Methods Under Local Smoothness

summary: For exact-polar, momentum-free Muon on matrix factorization, the analysis shows that early alignment is followed by nearly uniform additive growth of singular values, so smaller target modes finish first instead of traversing gradient descent's condition-number-limited saddle staircase. It identifies a Muon-specific conserved square-root Gram imbalance, proves balanced solutions from vanishing initialization, and validates alignment scaling and a two-stage learning-rate schedule, while noting that large fixed steps oscillate near the optimum.
source_title: Muon learns balanced solutions in matrix factorization without slow saddle-to-saddle dynamics

summary: MuonSSM moves Muon's orthogonalization idea from parameter optimization into recurrent memory, combining a momentum state with one-step Newton-Schulz-normalized low-rank writes while retaining a block-affine recurrence that supports associative scans. Theory supplies an additional gradient path, bounded singular amplification, and rank enrichment, and controlled 170M-token-model, vision, and time-series comparisons report stronger long-context retrieval and robustness; ablations attribute higher momentum rank and validation accuracy to Newton-Schulz rather than simple Frobenius normalization.
source_title: MuonSSM: Orthogonalizing State Space Models for Sequence Modeling

summary: Dead-Direction Conditioners precondition only the horizontal, function-changing component of an update while reducing each vertical gauge-orbit direction to a scalar, covering common shift, rescaling, normalization, and attention-rotation symmetries. The construction is exactly gauge-equivariant for Adam and composes with a compatible Muon orthogonalizer; experiments found DDCMuon grokked 10 of 11 deep-model seeds where plain Muon grokked none, with additional language-model and vision gains.
source_title: Dead-Direction Conditioners: Gauge-Equivariant Preconditioning for Deep Networks

summary: PCD constructs a scale-normalized multi-objective direction that stays close to primary descent while enforcing controlled secondary progress. A single tolerance governs the distortion, with closed-form solutions for two or three objectives. Compression experiments report strong accuracy-sparsity frontiers across CNNs; DenseNet-121/CIFAR-10 retains 94.0% accuracy at 90% parameter reduction in the main comparison. The two-objective deployment adds under 2% runtime in the reported setup, while three-objective runs are substantially costlier. Guarantees apply to the constructed direction, not automatically to Adam's realized step; the paper explicitly measures that optimizer gap, and operating-point selection uses test accuracy without held-out validation.
source_title: Not All Objectives Are Born Equal: Priority-Constrained Descent for Hierarchical Multi-Objective Optimization

summary: This optimizer wrapper chooses a correction that reduces losses harmed by minibatch averaging and historical momentum. It transforms a parameter-sized constrained problem into batch space, approximates full-network gradient interactions using the last linear layer, and solves a GPU-friendly surrogate without materializing per-sample gradients. Integrations with momentum SGD and AdamW improve CIFAR, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet-100 classification. ViT CIFAR-100 at batch 1024 rises from 58.82% to 61.06% with 4% runtime overhead. Costs scale quadratically with batch size; ill-conditioned last-layer Gram matrices and BatchNorm dependence can reduce benefits. The method is not uniformly positive across all architecture-batch combinations.
source_title: Reducing Per-Sample Interference in Stochastic Optimization

summary: Aurora traces neuron death in tall MLP matrices to persistently unequal row leverage in Muon's polar update, then replaces post-hoc row normalization with an iterative projection toward both semi-orthogonality and equal row norms. Across 340M and 1.1B models trained for 100B tokens, it prevented the diagnosed dead-neuron feedback and improved aggregate benchmarks over Muon, including a reported 9.1-point MMLU gain at 1.1B, with modest distributed overhead.
source_title: Aurora: A Leverage-Aware Spectral Optimizer

summary: DMuon preserves exact Muon while assigning each matrix and its optimizer state to one rank, computing Newton-Schulz once, and hiding hierarchical reduction and publication behind training through lookahead overlap. Batched Gram-form orthogonalization, symmetry-aware kernels, autotuning, and measured-cost owner placement produced 1.48-3.01x end-to-end and 6.85-163x optimizer-step speedups on language and embodied-foundation workloads, bringing average end-to-end overhead to within 2% of AdamW without framework changes.
source_title: DMuon: Efficient Distributed Muon Training with Near-Adam Overhead

summary: Hierarchical Muon applies the finite Newton-Schulz map independently to fixed-size matrix tiles, yielding a distinct locally coupled optimizer rather than an approximation that converges to full Muon as iterations increase. Its cost scales with tile size instead of the smaller full matrix dimension and exposes small batched GEMMs; diagnostics show larger tiles retain more global behavior, while single-seed Qwen3 experiments kept loss close to full Muon with lower optimizer and wall-clock time.
source_title: Hierarchical Muon: Tiled Newton-Schulz Updates for Efficient Muon Optimization

summary: This method treats a dataset as a finite population and uses an auxiliary gradient-prediction model to design lower-variance survey samples for any stochastic optimizer. Across synthetic and six benchmark studies, 71-86% of experiments improve and AdamW reaches better generalization in roughly half as many epochs in selected settings. It must train or maintain the auxiliary sampler, and the largest benefits appear at moderate input dimension.
source_title: Stochastic Gradient Optimization with Model-Assisted Sampling

summary: Tensorion generalizes Muon's matrix spectral steepest-descent view to higher-order tensors by introducing a tractable dual norm that upper-bounds the NP-hard tensor spectral norm; its linear minimization oracle selects an unfolding by nuclear norm and applies a matrix polar update, exactly recovering Muon at order two. An offline unfolding heuristic avoids repeated selection, and ResNet, Swin, and ViT experiments improved accuracy over SGD and Adam, though evaluation is confined to modest vision benchmarks.
source_title: Tensorion: A Tensor-Aware Generalization of the Muon Optimizer

summary: PACE formulates training for an EMA-returned model as optimal control and wraps AdamW with a clipped coordinate-wise force that pulls live weights toward their running average. It improves over AdamW and EMA-evaluated AdamW across 1-2B language-model fine-tuning and GPT-2 FineWeb pretraining under broad learning-rate and schedule sweeps. Guarantees rely on continuous-time quadratic and stylized convex models, and the paper reports no single uniform empirical gain.
source_title: Training for the Model You Return: Improving Optimization for Iterate-Averaged Language Models

summary: The analysis interprets Muown as Riemannian descent on a row-oblique manifold: growth of the unused ambient row norm acts as a gauge variable that implicitly decays angular steps at roughly inverse square-root time. AngularMuown instead fixes unit directions and explicitly schedules a width-transferable angular multiplier independently of Adam's radial scale; FineWeb-Edu dense and mixture-of-experts experiments lowered loss and showed more transferable learning rates, alongside a nonconvex stationarity guarantee.
source_title: Muown Implicitly Performs Angular Step-size Decay

summary: This work unifies normalized SGD, SignSGD or Lion, and Muon as momentum trust-region methods over operator subspaces and norms, analyzing them with structured smoothness and noise matrices rather than generic Euclidean conversions. The resulting theory explains when Muon benefits from high-rank solutions but low-rank curvature or noise, and shows extrapolation and momentum variance reduction can match one-sided Shampoo or AdaGrad rates in convex settings; it is a theoretical contribution without empirical validation.
source_title: Non-Euclidean SGD for Structured Optimization: Unified Analysis and Improved Rates

summary: EVON runs IVON in the eigenspace of SOAP's Kronecker preconditioner, then maps diagonal variance back into a structured non-diagonal posterior. It recovers exact Gaussian covariance in logistic regression and improves over diagonal IVON on NanoGPT or LLaMA-134M pretraining and eight CLIP classification datasets at SOAP-like optimizer cost. Language-model tests stop at 134M and posterior sampling adds inference cost because the primary goal is Bayesian uncertainty.
source_title: SOAP-Bubbles: Structured Weight Uncertainty for Neural Networks

summary: This work formulates root-finding bilevel optimization and uses two-timescale stochastic approximation: fast lower-level gradient updates are paired with slow upper-level residual updates, bypassing implicit Jacobian or inverse-Hessian estimation. A robust variant clips residual estimates and projects iterates onto feasible sets. Reported experiments cover contrastive-learning temperature tuning, entropy control, generative modeling, and nonlinear control, including a 2.6-point SimCLR accuracy improvement and 17x faster control convergence against the selected baselines. Its guarantees concern structured equilibrium tracking under regularity, bounded-noise, compact-domain, and timescale conditions. It is not a general guarantee that residual descent solves arbitrary nonmonotone bilevel problems.
source_title: Escaping the Variance Trap: Jacobian-Free Dynamics for Root-Finding Bilevel Optimization

summary: VRA-FedSGD addresses heavy-tailed stochastic gradients and noisy uplink/downlink communication with coupled variance-reduction mechanisms. Clients track corrected server broadcasts, compute paired gradient estimates, and apply a nonlinear robust mapping; the server uses variance-reduced aggregation to suppress channel noise. The paper establishes mean convergence rates for nonconvex objectives and almost-sure rates for strongly convex objectives, explicitly depending on the finite-moment tail index. Real-data logistic-regression simulations verify robustness under the modeled noise. The algorithm needs additional estimator state, paired local gradient evaluations, and calibrated schedules. Evidence concerns wireless-style noisy federated optimization, not broad deep-network or language-model pretraining.
source_title: Federated learning with heavy-tailed gradient noise and communication noise: a variance-reduction based algorithm

summary: The paper removes a fragile assumption in prior inexact-linear-oracle analyses of Muon-type methods: the smallest positive singular value of the rescaled momentum need not remain bounded away from zero. By replacing proximity to a nonunique polar factor with objective-alignment and update-size conditions, and treating low-momentum layers separately, it derives stochastic nonconvex, deterministic PL, and star-convex weight-decay convergence under layer-wise generalized smoothness, with explicit dependence on solver thresholds, precision, and iteration count.
source_title: Convergence Analysis of Muon-type Methods with Inexact LMO in the Degenerate Case

summary: These restart wrappers calibrate proximal stochastic-subgradient stage lengths and piecewise-constant step sizes to weak convexity and Kurdyka–Lojasiewicz geometry. Gap-based and deterministic schedules obtain exponent-dependent rates, with robustness bounds for misspecified restart and learning-rate constants. Five-run nanoGPT/Shakespeare and ResNet-18/CIFAR-10 experiments examine restart sensitivity, alongside controlled toy objectives. This is a theory-guided scheduling extension, not a new base gradient formula or fully parameter-free optimizer. The theory can require Moreau-envelope gaps and regularity constants; neural experiments instead substitute raw loss, a zero optimum estimate, and a tuned scaling factor. Robustness to misspecification does not remove those calibration choices.
source_title: Restart and Adaptive Acceleration in Stochastic Gradient Methods

summary: In a mixed-spiked matrix-sensing model, the paper casts optimization as following an informative river through nuisance curvature and shows why Muon's scale-free spectral step travels quickly early but overshoots and oscillates near the river bottom after discarding residual magnitude. Extensions to nonconvex spectral rivers plus MNIST and controlled 250M-token language-model runs support switching from Muon to AdamW or gradient descent for late refinement, which improves stability and final loss without claiming universal superiority.
source_title: Towards Understanding the Power and Limits of the Muon Optimizer: A River-Valley Perspective

summary: MGUP ranks coordinates by update-gradient alignment, amplifies a fixed top fraction, and gives the remainder a smaller nonzero step, unlike cautious masking schemes that discard misaligned coordinates; the rule plugs into AdamW, Lion, and Muon. It improves the underlying optimizers across masked-autoencoder training, language-model pretraining, and GLUE or GSM8K fine-tuning, while its near-optimal stochastic nonconvex convergence proof currently covers only AdamW without weight decay, leaving Lion and Muon theory open.
source_title: MGUP: A Momentum-Gradient Alignment Update Policy for Stochastic Optimization

summary: Turns Hamiltonian trajectories into deterministic accelerated optimization by averaging intermediate positions rather than requiring endpoint contraction. Its explicit extragradient discretization uses two gradient evaluations per integration step, resets velocity at outer cycles, and mixes a weighted trajectory average with the endpoint. Smooth convex and strongly convex results achieve accelerated first-order complexity with deterministic integration lengths. Synthetic linear and logistic regression experiments confirm acceleration over ordinary gradient descent, while tuned Nesterov acceleration is faster in most reported settings. This is an optimization algorithm rather than a sampler; theoretical acceleration does not establish stochastic nonconvex training gains, and integration, averaging, and parameter choices affect observed performance.
source_title: Accelerated Convex Optimization via Hamiltonian Dynamics with Deterministic Integration Time

summary: Adapts an unknown weak-convexity scale through one proximal candidate, a noisy function-difference test, and multiplicative bidirectional proximal-parameter updates. Successful trials accept the candidate and reduce regularization; failures retain the point and increase regularization. High-probability O(epsilon^-2) iteration guarantees allow biased heavy-tailed difference errors and candidates reliable only in a safe parameter regime; extensions cover prox-linear and proximal-gradient models. Robust phase-retrieval illustrations compare forty stochastic runs against fixed safe parameters. Iteration counts hide oracle work: the analyzed raw minibatch difference estimator can require O(epsilon^-6) total paired samples, and candidate solves add inner subgradient steps. This is not an empirically established large-model optimizer.
source_title: An Adaptive Proximal Framework for Stochastic Weakly Convex Optimization

summary: CacheMuon reuses the left preconditioner obtained from a stabilized Gram-form Newton-Schulz solve on recent momentum, applying it cheaply to the current matrix until an orthogonality residual triggers refresh. Its inexact-Muon analysis separates fresh-solver error from Lipschitz-controlled Gram staleness and gives convergence when their aggregate remains below one; GPT-2 and ResNet experiments show conservative thresholds match fresh Muon while cutting orthogonalization FLOPs, with aggressive caching exposing a clear savings-quality tradeoff.
source_title: CacheMuon: Using Temporal Preconditioning To Approximate Polar Factor

summary: Hyperball optimization fixes every Transformer matrix at its initialization Frobenius radius, normalizes the base optimizer's proposed direction, and projects each step back to the sphere, directly controlling angular learning instead of relying on weight-decay equilibrium. In Qwen3-style models up to 1.2B parameters, MuonH delivered a reported 20-30% token-equivalent gain over weight-decayed Muon and substantially reduced optimal-learning-rate drift across scale; scale-absorbing normalization layers motivate its expressivity argument.
source_title: Fantastic Pretraining Optimizers and Where to Find Them II: Hyperball Optimization

summary: Optimizes functions directly while adapting the finite representation used to approximate each functional-gradient step. A computable relative-error criterion triggers refinement instead of committing to a fixed neural architecture or grid resolution. The framework gives stationarity guarantees under smoothness and stronger convergence with additional Polyak-Lojasiewicz structure. Experiments cover kernel regression, wave-equation problems, and radiance-field reconstruction using task-specific representations. Adaptive resolution can improve approximation quality and practical efficiency, but refinement and full-batch gradient costs prevent a universal runtime advantage. This is a function-space learning and numerical-optimization framework, not an interchangeable parameter-space optimizer for arbitrary transformers; representation and learning-rate choices remain problem dependent.
source_title: Functional Gradient Descent with Adaptive Representations

summary: GENIE measures each parameter's one-step loss-reduction-to-gradient-alignment ratio and uses it as a preconditioner to equalize contributions across parameters. Across five domain-generalization benchmarks it improves over Adam, SGD, and SAM by 5.69, 6.36, and 4.37 points respectively while training about 1.3x faster than SAM. The method is domain-generalization-specific and its equal-ratio motivation remains partly conjectural.
source_title: One-Step Generalization Ratio Guided Optimization for Domain Generalization

summary: SILAGE exploits a nested finite-sum objective containing n sample groups of size m to obtain variance reduction without global full-gradient refreshes or per-sample control-variate storage. It stores group-level state, requiring O(n) vectors rather than O(nm), and evaluates at most one local group gradient per iteration. Complexity adapts to separately measured between-group and within-group functional similarity instead of a single worst-case smoothness constant. Controlled nonconvex-regularized logistic-regression experiments examine eight heterogeneity regimes. This is a centralized nested-data algorithm, not federated aggregation or a turnkey LLM optimizer; gains depend on group structure and must include the cost of local group-gradient evaluations.
source_title: SILAGE: Memory-Efficient, Full-Gradient-Free Nonconvex Optimization for Nested Finite Sums

summary: This paper analyzes Muon under genuinely heavy-tailed gradient noise with only a finite p-th moment, using martingale inequalities in the optimizer's native Banach geometry instead of dimension-costly Euclidean norm conversions. It proves optimal normalized steepest-descent rates for uniformly smooth duals and matching lower bounds, with improved dimension dependence for nuclear-norm Muon; Pythia-70M measurements find native noise ratios milder than worst case and gains from Schatten geometry up to an intermediate order before plateauing.
source_title: Free Heavy-Tailed Lunch for Muon: A Theoretical Justification of Empirical Success

summary: Gefen infers parameter blocks from initial squared gradients, shares second moments within them, and quantizes first moments with a learned histogram codebook; its GefenMuon extension quantizes Muon momentum. The AdamW-like method cuts state memory about 8x, saving 6.5 GiB per billion parameters at matched performance, while GefenMuon reports 4x less persistent state and about 38% lower peak memory on GPT-2 pretraining and Qwen3-1.7B fine-tuning. Partitions are inferred early and the Muon evidence is narrower than the main Gefen study.
source_title: Gefen: Optimized Stochastic Optimizer

summary: LoRA-Muon solves a spectral linear minimization problem on the tangent space of the fixed-rank matrix manifold rather than optimizing LoRA factors independently, using Gram-whitened factor gradients and matrix-sign updates with a split trust region. The induced composed-matrix update is invariant to arbitrary invertible LoRA reparameterizations; compute-matched six-seed TinyShakespeare tests show rank-2 behavior near dense training and lower mean validation loss at rank 32, but evidence remains deliberately small-scale.
source_title: LoRA-Muon: Spectral Steepest Descent on the Low-Rank Manifold

summary: Muon^p interpolates between Muon and gradient descent by replacing each singular value with its fractional power and identifies the update as steepest descent under a corresponding Schatten norm. After proving fixed univariate polynomial iterations cannot realize noninteger powers, it derives SVD-free odd bivariate matrix recurrences; Llama 1B and 3B fine-tuning experiments outperform Muon on math and code tasks at competitive runtime, while mixed pretraining results suggest the best power is regime dependent.
source_title: Muon$^p$: Muon with Fractional Spectral Powers

summary: bAdag updates only a selected variable block and accumulates squared gradients only when coordinates are selected, yielding AdaGrad-style steps without objective-function evaluations or line search. Unified nonconvex convergence analysis covers cyclic, uniformly random, and greedy Gauss-Southwell selection, with a box-constrained extension. Least-squares, log-sum-regularized logistic regression, and robust nonnegative-matrix-factorization experiments examine accuracy and computational cost under multiplicative noise. Results are regime-dependent: line-search block descent is much cheaper on noiseless least squares, while bAdag is more robust at high noise. Greedy selection can require full gradients, and weighted evaluation counts are not universal wall-clock savings or evidence of large-neural-network superiority.
source_title: bAdag: an adaptive block coordinate gradient method for smooth nonconvex functions

summary: N-RSAV augments relaxed scalar-auxiliary-variable optimization with a Nyström low-rank Hessian approximation, truncating negative eigenvalues to preserve the modified-energy dissipation structure. AN-RSAV additionally reuses curvature until the discrepancy between original and modified energies warrants rebuilding it. On an effectively rank-15 quadratic, N-RSAV reduces 10,000-step runtime from Hessian-RSAV's 246 seconds to 76 seconds, and adaptive reuse reduces it further to 24 seconds. Burgers-equation PINN tests use Adam warm-starting before the second-order phase. Guarantees require PL-type conditions and additional convexity assumptions; benefits rely on useful low-rank curvature and do not eliminate Hessian-vector-product costs.
source_title: Accelerating SAV-based optimization via randomized low-rank Hessian approximation

summary: FOGO treats minibatch and continual-learning forgetting as gradient interference, then fuses slow and fast orthogonalized momentum streams, compresses conflicts with a random projection and spherical centroid memory, and lifts corrections through a proximal solve without retaining raw examples. Across imbalanced and continual vision, LLaVA-7B continual VQA, and 49.2B-token GPT-2 training it improved retention; language pretraining converged faster early but reached a similar final loss, clarifying that its main advantage is forgetting control.
source_title: FOGO: Forgetting-aware Orthogonalization Optimizer

summary: Adds stochastic gradients and unbiased quantized communication to decentralized primal-dual gradient descent. Agents communicate only quantized primal parameters, while a local dual state accumulates consensus disagreement and feeds back a correction. Restricted-secant or Polyak-Lojasiewicz geometry yields linear convergence to a noise-dependent neighborhood with constant steps, with diminishing-step results under stated assumptions. Synthetic least squares and 100-agent, approximately 11K-parameter CNN experiments on MNIST/Fashion-MNIST evaluate consensus and accuracy under four-bit communication. Deep-network experiments lie outside the global geometric guarantees and use IID partitions with controlled hyperparameters; they do not establish heterogeneous federated or large-language-model superiority. Quantization and stochastic noise retain explicit residual costs.
source_title: Quantized Stochastic Primal-Dual Methods for Distributed Optimization under Relaxed Global Geometry

summary: AdaDQN couples memoryless BFGS curvature updates with consensus-aware termination of local optimization and event-triggered broadcasts over undirected networks. A safeguarded local criterion stops additional computation when consensus discrepancy dominates local progress, avoiding the worst-case learning-rate shrinkage associated with a fixed local-update budget. Under smooth nonconvex assumptions, the paper proves an inverse-iteration best-stationarity rate and a gradient-complexity bound independent of the maximum local-update count. Numerical tests compare communication volume, gradient evaluations, and iteration efficiency against decentralized baselines. The method uses full local gradients and safeguards; it is not validated as a stochastic, billion-parameter language-model optimizer.
source_title: An Adaptive Decentralized Quasi-Newton Method with Stepsizes Independent of the Local-Update Budget

summary: Rather than explaining Muon only through faster optimization, this work links its orthogonalized updates to representation quality: layerwise probes show larger logit margins, while hidden-state spectra have higher effective rank. Matched-budget ImageNet and FineWeb pretraining finds better corruption robustness and downstream transfer than Adam or SGD, and a stylized multi-component classifier proves Muon’s spectral normalization yields both larger margins and effective rank at matched loss.
source_title: Muon Learns More Robust and Transferable Features than Adam

summary: OptMuon couples Muon’s polar-factor momentum direction with a lagged, running-maximum-corrected AdaGrad-Norm coefficient, making step magnitude a closed-loop function of observed gradient and momentum energy rather than smoothness or noise constants. Its two variants prove noise-adaptive stationarity rates under average and individual smoothness and automatically recover a nearly optimal deterministic first-order rate when gradient noise vanishes, without hyperparameter retuning.
source_title: OptMuon: Closed-Loop Orthogonalized Momentum Methods for Stochastic Optimization with Zero-Noise Optimality

summary: This paper characterizes Muon as a flat-update-spectrum method rather than simple normalization or a nuclear-norm low-rank bias. Under projected polar flow it derives exact singular-value dynamics, an entropy-maximizing one-step result, a geometry-dependent flattening criterion, and polar-map noise sensitivity; matrix-sensing ablations separate these effects from norm-matched gradient descent, while NanoGPT and ViT controls reveal rank preservation and a regime-dependent performance reversal.
source_title: The Spectral Dynamics and Noise Geometry of Muon

summary: Reformulates nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax optimization as joint regularized minimization, then uses adaptive cubic-quadratic Newton majorization to avoid inner maximization and explicit third derivatives. A recursive-variance-reduced stochastic variant yields O(epsilon^-3) gradient and O(epsilon^-2) Hessian sample complexities; deterministic local superlinear convergence requires nondegeneracy. Rates concern the reformulated objective's stationarity, whose worst-case conversion to value-function stationarity incurs condition-number factors. CPU experiments use robust regression on randomly projected E2006-tfidf data, with Lanczos cubic solves and increasing stochastic batches. These small-to-medium-scale second-order results do not imply LLM-training speedups; Hessian access and cubic-subproblem solution remain substantive costs. No paper-linked official implementation was located.
source_title: A Single-Loop Regularized Newton Method for Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization

summary: Multi-Gossip Accelerated DSGD combines Nesterov-style primal-dual extrapolation with multiple fast-gossip averaging rounds. Coupling gossip depth to minibatch size reduces consensus error while controlling stochastic-gradient variance, targeting simultaneous acceleration in objective condition number and network spectral gap. For smooth strongly convex problems, the analysis obtains communication complexity with a square-root condition-number/network term and a variance-dependent term, up to logarithmic factors. The contribution is a decentralized stochastic algorithm and oracle-complexity result, not a demonstrated replacement for AdamW in LLM training. Its guarantees require strong convexity and suitable network mixing, and extra gossip exchanges must be included in deployment cost.
source_title: Accelerated Decentralized Stochastic Gradient Descent for Strongly Convex Optimization

summary: Dominant-Layer ZO identifies a model-specific decoder layer using inference-only activation-outlier analysis, then restricts forward-only zeroth-order adaptation to that layer. The paper links the first activation-outlier layer to high perturbation sensitivity and early residual-stream placement, allowing a small updated block to influence subsequent layers. On Llama2-7B and Qwen3-8B across nine benchmarks, reported average scores improve by 0.86 points over full-model MeZO and 0.61 over LoRA-based ZO, with 1.12-4.52x speedups. This is a parameter-selection strategy around ZO updates rather than a new moment estimator. First-order fine-tuning remains stronger, and broader model-family validation is limited.
source_title: Dominant-Layer ZO: A Single Layer Dominates Zeroth-Order Fine-Tuning of LLMs

summary: DP-MacAdam reuses private running estimates of gradient mean and variance for both coordinate-adaptive clipping and Adam-style momentum, combining mechanisms previously treated separately. The analysis corrects the gradient-variance estimate for privacy noise rather than assuming privatized squared gradients are unbiased. Five-seed experiments train an MNIST multilayer perceptron and a five-layer CIFAR-10 CNN from scratch for five epochs. At MNIST privacy epsilon 1.46, accuracy is 92.6% versus DP-Adam's 91.9% and DP-SGD's 88.7%. Gains are not uniform at the highest CIFAR noise setting. The study is small-scale and still requires learning-rate, moment, and adaptation settings.
source_title: DP-MacAdam: Differentially Private Mechanism with Adaptive Clipping and Adaptive Momentum

optimizer: Why Muon Outperforms Adam: A Curvature Perspective
summary: Using second-order Taylor diagnostics at matched validation loss, the paper finds Muon and Adam obtain similar first-order gains and update norms, but Muon pays a much smaller Hessian penalty because its normalized directional sharpness is lower, with an average Adam-to-Muon ratio of 1.76. Zipf-PCFG experiments show imbalance widens this gap, layer decomposition locates it mainly within layers late in training, and heterogeneous quadratic models prove the balancing mechanism.
source_title: Why Muon Outperforms Adam: A Curvature Perspective

summary: DECA performs decentralized full-parameter LLM fine-tuning by sequentially optimizing disjoint parameter blocks with Adam. Its block-wise moment adaptation combines fresh local gradients with consensus-derived discrepancy signals to reduce drift on heterogeneous clients. Across Llama and Qwen models from 1.5B to 8B, the paper reports classification and generation improvements over decentralized adapter and LoRA baselines. Qwen2.5-3B average classification accuracy rises from the strongest baseline's 76.37% to 79.32%. Block updates reduce activation and update costs, but communication can exceed PEFT baselines because full blocks are exchanged. Evaluation emphasizes small decentralized networks and does not establish universal large-cluster scaling.
source_title: DECA: Decentralizing Block-Wise Adam for Efficient LLM Full-Parameter Fine-Tuning on Non-IID Data

summary: The work explains Muon’s ordering—momentum before polar orthogonalization—as spectral denoising: under a coherent signal plus bounded-variance orthogonal perturbation, momentum suppresses tail singular values, widens the signal-to-noise gap, and stabilizes singular subspaces. It proves pre-polar updates align better with signal than post-polar or no-momentum alternatives, and synthetic, CIFAR-10, NanoGPT probes plus 350M LLaMA training confirm the predicted ordering and loss advantage.
source_title: Denoise First, Orthogonalize Later: Understanding Momentum in Muon via Spectral Filtering

summary: MAdam prewhitens a reconciled multi-objective direction with preference-conditioned scalarized curvature so Adam's second moment does not distort the intended preference or Pareto geometry. It improves over Adam in the reported multitask, Pareto, physics-informed, and medical-imaging solver families. The method is specialized to multi-objective optimization and the abstract supplies neither a uniform effect size nor a verified implementation.
source_title: MAdam: Metric-Aware Multi-Objective Adam

summary: Builds interval-adaptive online convex optimization from optimistic gradient-descent experts and a new Lipschitz-adaptive multiplicative-weights meta-learner. The meta-update clips regret-minus-optimism errors and adjusts individual learning rates using observed error scales, while scheduled sleeping experts track nonstationarity. Unknown-Lipschitz variants avoid supplying a worst-case gradient scale but retain projection and logarithmic expert overhead. Gradient-variation interval-regret guarantees lead to dynamic-regret and stochastic-optimization applications under convexity and bounded-domain assumptions. Synthetic changing-target regression and nonstationary MNIST multiclass logistic regression test adaptation across five runs. These are small convex learners, not evidence of nonconvex language-model training; favorable initial scale estimates and parameter choices affect comparisons.
source_title: Online Learning with Gradient-Variation Interval Regret

summary: The paper tracks Muon momentum-buffer singular-value quantiles across GPT-2 models from 77M to 2.8B parameters and finds post-burn-in stabilization values obey layer-specific power laws. Rank-truncation ablations show roughly half the spectral directions must be orthogonalized for full-Muon quality; extrapolation predicts standard five-step Newton-Schulz remains sufficient through mid-late layers, whereas final projections with exponents as steep as -0.96 require a more accurate, layer-aware configuration at frontier scale.
source_title: Spectral Scaling Laws of Muon

optimizer: A Note on Stability for Orthogonalized Matrix Momentum
summary: This stability analysis extends Muon generalization theory to partially participating federated clients with heterogeneous sample sizes and fixed aggregation weights. A coupled-neighbor recursion retains each client’s exposure amplification and yields conditional high-probability risk-gap bounds; regularized polar and finite-step Newton-Schulz maps satisfy the needed Lipschitz condition, while exact matrix sign requires a shared spectral gap or Gaussian smoothing, a necessity backed by a scalar counterexample.
source_title: A Note on Stability for Orthogonalized Matrix Momentum with Client Sampling

summary: AAMD couples primal-dual mirror updates with acceleration and an accumulated Lyapunov-perturbation budget. Local descent failures are permitted while their accumulated budget remains nonpositive; backtracking repairs curvature and acceleration parameters only when stability is threatened. Homotopy and proximal extensions handle general convex and composite objectives. Deterministic logistic-regression and polynomial-of-norm tests show faster convergence than selected acceleration, preconditioning, and adaptive baselines, with fewer than ten reported backtracking steps. Guarantees depend on dual relative smoothness, mirror-geometry compatibility, and boundedness conditions. An objective-adapted, efficiently invertible mirror map is required; stochastic and nonconvex extensions are explicitly future work, not demonstrated large-model training capabilities.
source_title: Adaptive Accelerated Mirror Descent in Primal and Dual Spaces

optimizer: SAM / USAM with Stochastic Polyak Scheduler
summary: This work derives Polyak-style learning-rate rules specifically for sharpness-aware updates, using the perturbed loss, a lower bound, and gradient geometry rather than a predetermined schedule. Deterministic USAM analysis gives linear convergence under strong convexity and an inverse-iteration rate for convex objectives; stochastic guarantees reach a noise-dependent neighborhood. Experiments compare constant, cosine, and stochastic Polyak schedules on ResNet-20/32 and CIFAR-10/100 over three seeds, generally matching or improving tuned SAM-family baselines. It remains a scheduler-equipped optimizer variant, not a parameter-free cure: the perturbation radius, step cap, and lower-bound choice still matter, and theoretical results focus on USAM.
source_title: Adaptive Sharpness-Aware Minimization with a Polyak-type Step size: A Theory-Grounded Scheduler

summary: LPSGD and LPSGDM begin with p greater than two to suppress high-curvature directions, then anneal the $\ell_p$ geometry toward p=2 as training moves into flatter regions. The paper proves an O(T^-1/2) nonconvex rate and evaluates VGG and ResNet models on CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet-1K. It reports no common numerical gain in the abstract, the p schedule remains a design choice, and Transformers are not tested.
source_title: Beyond $\ell_2$-norm and $\ell_\infty$-norm: A Curvature-Inspired $\ell_p$-Norm Scheme for Deep Neural Networks

summary: GROKtimizer separates interpolation from post-interpolation complexity reduction: an initial fitting phase is followed by critically damped, weight-decayed momentum designed to rapidly approach low-norm interpolating solutions. Under a local quadratic basin model, the paper derives accelerated norm minimization rather than a general neural-network convergence guarantee. Experiments report improvements on six synthetic grokking tasks over ten seeds and biomedical classification and QM9 over five seeds. Modular-addition accuracy reaches 95.1% versus Adam's 70.1%. Data-constrained language-model experiments show smaller benefits and a less direct norm-generalization relationship. The strategy requires sufficient model capacity to interpolate and is not established for large-scale, data-rich pretraining.
source_title: Fast Generalization after Interpolation via Critically Damped Momentum Optimization

summary: FOAM adapts both damping and eigendecomposition refreshes in Shampoo using a cheap proxy for stale inverse-root operator error. It increases damping to suppress spectral drift and recomputes factors when compensation becomes insufficient, avoiding a fixed expensive refresh cadence. On ImageNet ViT, the reported configuration improves accuracy from stale Shampoo's 75.13% to 75.72% while reducing runtime from 1,415 to 1,300 minutes. Conformer and GPT-2 experiments also evaluate the accuracy-cost trade-off. The proxy and controller introduce sensing-frequency, tolerance, and damping-cap choices; overly large damping degrades preconditioning, and the reported language-model speedups are modest rather than universal.
source_title: FOAM: Frequency and Operator Error-Based Adaptive Damping Method for Reducing Staleness-Oriented Error for Shampoo

summary: GRZO draws a pseudo-independent perturbation for each minibatch example and aggregates normalized per-example losses, increasing the effective direction count from one to the batch size without extra forward passes. On Llama3-8B it gains 3.0 average accuracy points over MeZO with 23% lower peak GPU memory, and raises sparse, low-rank, and quantized zeroth-order variants by 6.0 points on average. Results cover fine-tuning rather than pretraining and remain within the query-intensive zeroth-order setting.
source_title: GRZO: Group-Relative Zeroth-Order Optimization for Large Language Model Fine-Tuning

summary: This work extends performance-estimation interpolation to inexactly smooth convex functions and constructs new optimized first-order recurrences. Its SSEP method is minimax optimal for the zero-Hölder endpoint; an inexactly smooth OGM variant improves known leading constants for intermediate Hölder classes. UOBL adds tolerance-aware backtracking without requiring the smoothness profile as input. Numerical evidence concerns performance-estimation values and asymptotic coefficients rather than model-training experiments. Exact optimality is established only in the endpoint case; general leading-constant optimality remains conjectural. The methods require convexity and specified iteration/accuracy budgets, with additional distance or regularity parameters in some variants, so these results do not establish stochastic nonconvex training speedups.
source_title: Inexactly Smooth Performance Estimation and New Optimized Gradient Methods

summary: BregTop studies how Frobenius, von Neumann, and LogDet divergences distribute Kronecker approximation error across curvature directions, then separates a top-eigenspace preconditioner from an isotropic tail. Leading joint Kronecker eigenvalues receive curvature-dependent scaling, while the tail uses an adaptive uniform scale derived from spectral quantiles. In a small four-layer Transformer SST-2 experiment, one variant reaches training-loss EMA below 0.05 in 1,003 steps versus 1,119 for Shampoo. This is a training-loss comparison, not a large-scale generalization or wall-clock result. Spectral selection, decomposition costs, and tail-scale choices remain; first arXiv submission was May 30 despite its June identifier.
source_title: Rethinking Bregman Divergences in Kronecker-Factored Optimizers

optimizer: Higher-order regularized parameter-free GD / Newton / Gauss–Newton / SGD / PAGE
summary: Constructs parameter-free nonconvex methods by regularizing local models with a power strictly above their approximation-error order and prescribing the regularization schedule without backtracking or trial acceptance. Instantiations cover gradient descent, Newton, Gauss–Newton, mini-batch SGD, and variance-reduced PAGE; first-order subproblems yield gradient-norm-scaled steps, with some coinciding with existing normalized-gradient updates. The contribution is a unified construction and accuracy-dependent oracle guarantees under stated smoothness and variance assumptions, not an empirically validated training speedup. Horizon doubling restarts from the initial point when the budget is unknown. Regularization powers, scale constants, batch sizes, and inner-solver requirements remain choices; the paper reports no dataset experiments.
source_title: A General Recipe for Parameter-Free Nonconvex Optimization via Higher-Order Regularization

summary: Analyzes PolarGD on matrix quadratics under exact line search, isolating direction geometry from learning-rate tuning. Orthogonal equivariance and row-isotropic errors explain favorable regimes, while iterate-dependent preconditioning can amplify tiny singular directions and make exact polar descent slower than gradient descent. Finite Newton–Schulz softens those directions rather than merely approximating the polar factor. An added 90M-transformer spectral probe finds this GD-like tail concentrated in attention matrices, especially earlier layers, rather than MLP matrices. Quadratic trajectory results and observational spectra do not establish that more orthogonalization improves neural training or that fewer iterations universally outperform exact polar updates. [Earlier OpenReview version](https://openreview.net/forum?id=TVTwgZp0qe)
source_title: A Quadratic Lens on Muon: Orthogonalization, Invariance, and Implicit Preconditioning

summary: Analyzes how Muon's implicit row-block metric relates to neural Hessian structure by studying expected gradient self-outer-products at initialization. Width-dependent calculations cover symmetric matrix factorization, deep linear networks, two-layer ReLU networks, and the added single-layer linear-attention model. For attention, expected query/key/value Grams are exactly diagonal, while the output projection has an explicit dimension-dependent dominance rate. Synthetic simulations and language-model initialization experiments support the predicted scaling. These results concern expectation and initialization, not concentration for an individual gradient, training-time momentum dynamics, or proof that row normalization replaces practical Muon without loss. [Earlier OpenReview version](https://openreview.net/forum?id=U812abpXRD)
source_title: How Does Orthogonalization Adapt to the Neural-Network Hessian Structure? A Gradient Self Outer-Product Analysis at Initialization

optimizer: How Much Orthogonalization Does Muon Need?
summary: To cut Muon’s orthogonalization cost, the paper derives a five-step cubic Newton-Schulz schedule targeting a BF16 singular-value band of [0.7, 1.3], using 10 dominant matrix multiplications versus 15 for five quintic steps. GPT-2 Small places cubic5, Polar Express, Muon-Jordan, and exact FP32 SVD within 0.003 validation loss, while 1B–4B hybrid MoE/Mamba runs keep cubic5 within about 0.001 of Muon-Jordan, showing training quality is not monotonic in polar accuracy.
source_title: How Much Orthogonalization Does Muon Need?

summary: Connecting Muon to neural scaling laws, the paper uses multi-task sparse parity to show spectral updates acquire rare and common skills more concurrently than Adam or normalized momentum descent, quantified by a new Skill Acquisition Lag metric and shorter coverage times. In a linear-attention in-context regression model, Muon decouples covariance eigenmodes and converges uniformly despite task- and input-frequency imbalance, explaining how parallel acquisition can improve scaling exponents.
source_title: On How Muon Reshapes Skill Learning Dynamics

summary: In the finite-width projected two-layer student–teacher model, this work replaces projected SGD’s rank-one feature update with practical NS5 Muon and a tractable partial-polar population proxy. The proxy removes the small projected-gradient-norm bottleneck and predicts late-time acceleration; fixed-compute sweeps show positive width-scaling exponents for Muon versus negative ones for SGD on hard source-condition tasks, with readout-Hessian spectra indicating stronger low-rank feature alignment.
source_title: Practical Muon Accelerates Projected Feature Learning in Scaling-Law Models

summary: Recasts minimum average variance estimation as optimization on the Stiefel manifold and combines projected-space nearest-neighbor localization with minibatch Riemannian gradient ascent. Normalized gradients, ambient heavy-ball momentum, periodic neighborhood rebuilding, and QR retraction produce a scalable sufficient-dimension-reduction algorithm for regression. Synthetic and four real-data studies report competitive or improved subspace recovery with substantially lower runtime than RMAVE at moderate-to-high dimension. Formal convergence covers a simplified regularized version with fixed neighborhoods, no momentum, and no gradient normalization, not the complete implementation. This is a specialized statistical-learning solver; the paper notes classification extensions remain open and unstructured settings with more dimensions than samples remain challenging.
source_title: Riemannian Stochastic Optimization for Sufficient Dimension Reduction

summary: Rather than attributing optimizer difficulty solely to curvature, this paper models signal-frequency imbalance as correlations between parameter directions and data subsets, producing effective low-rank gradient clusters. Language-model inner-layer measurements find semantically coherent clusters, while a simplified analysis shows minibatch averaging suppresses rare directions and creates ill-conditioning only at large batch sizes; the resulting regime dependence explains why Adam and Muon outperform SGD, and why Muon can surpass Adam in inner layers.
source_title: Signal Frequency Imbalance and Ill-Conditioning

summary: SoftMuon relaxes Muon’s hard spectral sign with a smooth algebraic soft-sign map and a quantile-driven temperature that gradually shifts small singular directions from full-magnitude Muon steps to magnitude-sensitive updates. The Fenchel-regularized framework supplies stochastic nonconvex convergence guarantees; across character modeling, GraphLand, and 130M–720M language-model pretraining, SoftMuon improves the hard baseline, reaching 16.216 versus Muon’s 16.362 perplexity at 720M.
source_title: Softsign: Smooth Sign in Your Optimizer For Better Parameter Heterogeneity Handling

summary: Treating optimizers as feedback controllers, the paper defines total training energy—the cumulative squared back-propagated signal—and proves that, on Kronecker-quadratic losses, it is a closed-loop H2 norm decomposing over Hessian modes. Convexity shows uniform contraction rates minimize this energy, linking Muon’s polar equalization to the optimum; MNIST MLPs find Muon has the lowest per-mode-energy Gini throughout and the lowest cumulative energy in two of three depths, mainly through low-curvature modes.
source_title: Spectral Equalization Minimizes Total Training Energy: A Control-Theoretic Account of Muon's Advantage

summary: Sketched landing replaces expensive tangent and orthogonality-restoring matrix products with unbiased low-dimensional random sketches, avoiding retractions while approaching the Stiefel constraint. Dense Haar/Gaussian constructions and sparse row subsampling reduce landing-field arithmetic; an SVRG variant periodically computes an unsketched reference direction to control sketch noise. Expected stationarity and infeasibility bounds use decaying steps under smoothness and bounded-variance assumptions. Preliminary circle, orthogonalization, and Rayleigh-quotient experiments show the uncorrected method's noise floor and improved accuracy with variance reduction. Large-scale computational gains are explicitly left for future work, so arithmetic reductions are not demonstrated end-to-end training speedups; stepsize tuning and snapshot frequency remain important.
source_title: The sketched landing method for large-scale optimization under orthogonality constraints

optimizer: Capped MGDA / Greedy-DCP / Mixed Aggregator Scheduling
summary: Introduces Capped MGDA by deriving multiobjective gradient aggregation from a CVaR primal problem, producing a minimum-norm simplex quadratic program with upper bounds on each gradient weight. The cap is enforced during optimization rather than by post-hoc coefficient clipping. The framework also develops mixed-aggregator scheduling and a greedy dual-cone-projection variant. Synthetic and fairness studies examine Pareto stationarity, while full-batch CIFAR-10 federated CNN experiments show improved robustness to injected opposing gradients compared with uncapped MGDA. Capped directions need not be non-conflicting, and experiments do not establish a universal method ranking or general Byzantine guarantee; stochastic, constrained, and nonsmooth extensions remain future work.
source_title: A Unified Framework for Gradient Aggregation in Multi-Objective Optimization

summary: S-Adam estimates local nonsmooth instability from the variance of randomized directional derivatives and damps Adam by exp(-lambda rho) near large estimated Clarke subdifferentials. It proves an optimal-order Clarke-stationarity result and reports gains up to 4.54 points on CIFAR-100 and 4.27 on TinyImageNet in quantization-aware or noisy small-batch training. Evidence is limited to those nonsmooth vision regimes and geometric probing adds extra evaluations.
source_title: Singularity-aware Optimization via Randomized Geometric Probing: Towards Stable Non-smooth Optimization

summary: DECO-EF combines coin-betting predictions with compressed error-feedback gossip, transmitting differences between clean accumulated states and local trackers to preserve the clean network average. Its comparator-adaptive online convex regret avoids learning-rate dependence on the horizon or comparator norm. LIBSVM regression streams demonstrate reduced tuning sensitivity, while synthetic 20-agent tests expose quantization and topology tradeoffs. Importantly, the proved near-square-root regret uses gossip substeps growing linearly with time; experiments instead use constant communication, leaving a theory-practice gap. Initial wealth and graph/compressor relaxation parameters remain, communication is synchronous and reliable, and deep-network or LLM training is not evaluated.
source_title: Decentralized Parameter-Free Online Learning with Compressed Gossip

summary: Motivated by localized, entry-wise heavy-tailed gradient noise, the paper derives Bayes-inspired smooth shrinkage as a cheap spectral-control surrogate and applies it after Adam updates or before Muon orthogonalization. A localization metric and Cauchy-contamination analysis give standard fourth-order stationarity complexity; on 276M Modded-NanoGPT, shrinkage saves 7.6% of Adam’s tokens and 1.9% beyond Muon while restoring spike-corrupted spectral subspaces.
source_title: Can Entry-Wise Clipping Give Spectral Control of Stochastic Gradients?

summary: Spectral Descent and its rank-truncated variant receive the first global linear convergence guarantees for convex, Lipschitz, sharp but nonsmooth objectives, with TSD interpreted as Ky Fan-norm steepest descent and able to reduce SVD cost. Adding decoupled weight decay turns the method into a conditional-subgradient Frank-Wolfe update with sublinear convergence; ReLU-network, linear-program, matrix-classification, and robust LAD low-rank-recovery experiments support the predicted acceleration and mixed-noise robustness.
source_title: Convergence of Spectral Descent for Non-smooth Optimization

summary: MONA inserts an exponential moving average of consecutive gradient differences before Muon’s momentum and Newton-Schulz stages, using this Hessian proxy to bias orthogonalized updates away from sharp directions while retaining spectral normalization. It proves nonconvex stationarity and sharp-minimum selectivity; 1B, 6B, and 68B MoE pretraining shows lower validation loss, with the 68B model improving average general capability from Muon’s 0.4478 to 0.4557, while MONA-Lite cuts added memory about 75%.
source_title: MONA: Muon Optimizer with Nesterov Acceleration for Scalable Language Model Training

summary: MuCon replaces Muon’s polar factor with the Frobenius projection onto a spectral-norm ball, clipping only singular values above a threshold and therefore preserving moderate update geometry. Rather than presenting training results, the report derives exact low-rank-correction, polar/absolute-value, and rational-Newton formulations: it recommends partial SVD or Lanczos when few values violate the threshold and shows global matrix-function filters become ill-conditioned near the boundary unless their solves are explicitly regularized.
source_title: MuCon: Clipped Muon Updates for LLM Training

summary: The paper adapts Muon to multi-norm adversarial training and proves its polar update imposes an operator-norm ceiling plus a nuclear-norm descent guarantee, limiting abrupt spectral growth without claiming small final weight norms. Across five CNN and ViT architectures and three threat norms, Muon strongly outperforms unstable AdamW and often matches SGD on CIFAR-10, but SGD remains better in the ImageNet pilot and SAM is usually stronger at extra backpropagation cost.
source_title: When Muon Optimizer Meets Adversarial Training: A Theoretical and Empirical Study

summary: EMA-Nesterov replaces Nesterov’s noisy one-step displacement lookahead with an exponential moving average of realized parameter updates, providing a low-pass trajectory estimate that wraps arbitrary base optimizers while retaining accelerated convex rates. Across NanoGPT/Llama pretraining with Adam, SOAP, Muon, and NorMuon, it consistently improves optimization; with tuned Muon it reaches validation loss 3.28 in roughly 6% fewer steps and remains effective across model and token scales.
source_title: EMA-Nesterov: Stabilizing Nesterov's Lookahead for Accelerated Deep Learning Optimization

summary: This work reparametrizes Shampoo-family preconditioners to retain an orthogonal complete basis while refreshing only selected basis subspaces through QR or eigendecomposition. A GPU-friendly greedy block selector captures strongly coupled directions, reducing decomposition work and making BF16 preconditioner storage more robust. FineWeb experiments with nanoGPT and LLaMA models from 119M to 598M parameters show smaller FP32-to-BF16 loss degradation across KL-Shampoo, SOAP, and KL-SOAP; for example, nanoGPT SOAP's degradation falls from 0.013 to 0.005. Smaller subspaces trade accuracy against runtime, and repeated subspace updates recover quality at additional cost. This is a preliminary optimizer reparameterization, not evidence of universally superior training.
source_title: Reparametrizing Shampoo and SOAP for Subspace Basis Updates and BFloat16 Storage

summary: BSFW extends boosted Frank-Wolfe to stochastic and nonconvex constrained optimization through a new stepsize strategy requiring neither line search nor the gradient Lipschitz constant. Repeated linear-minimization-oracle calls align a feasible direction with a gradient estimator; a norm-ratio scaling controls the update and falls back to ordinary Frank-Wolfe when needed. The framework supports variance-reduced, momentum, coordinate, and zeroth-order estimators while matching their corresponding non-boosted worst-case rates under stated assumptions. Sparse logistic regression, quantum process tomography, and collaborative filtering experiments report improved progress over matched-estimator baselines. Extra boosting oracle calls are a real cost, so gains depend on inexpensive constraint oracles and alignment tolerances.
source_title: Boosted Stochastic Frank-Wolfe for Constrained Nonconvex Optimization

summary: This study shows that Muon’s advantage in Vision Transformers depends strongly on the training recipe rather than optimizer choice alone: augmentation, Mixup/CutMix, and label smoothing prevent late gradient-mode collapse, while Muon redistributes spectral energy more broadly than AdamW. Across ImageNet-100, Pl@ntNet-300K, segmentation, and masked-autoencoder pretraining, matched-recipe Muon consistently wins, including 37.7% versus 16.3% macro top-1 on Pl@ntNet under the full recipe.
source_title: Muon in Vision Transformers: Optimizer-Recipe Interactions and Gradient Spectra

summary: PILOT learns a compact polynomial policy online from consecutive-gradient directional agreement, controlling momentum reliance, variance-normalization strength, and interpolation toward sign-based updates. This lets a first-order optimizer adjust its update structure without offline meta-training or explicit curvature estimation. Experiments on FashionMNIST and CIFAR-10 with small CNNs and ResNet-18 report the strongest evaluated classification results, including 93.42% CIFAR-10 accuracy for ResNet-18; a policy-transfer test provides initial cross-dataset evidence. The study remains restricted to small convolutional benchmarks, with no transformer or language-model validation. Online policy learning introduces extra computation and state, but systematic overhead and sensitivity measurements are still missing.
source_title: PILOT: Policy-Informed Learned Optimization for Adaptive Deep Network Training

summary: ZOCOON combines clipped two-point gradient estimates with an online-to-nonconvex conversion for nonsmooth objectives under heavy-tailed noise. It targets Goldstein stationarity and provides complexity guarantees assuming bounded p-th moments of stochastic Lipschitz constants; at finite variance, its bound matches the best-known dependence on smoothing accuracy and dimension for this setting. Ten-seed numerical studies on a9a, covtype, and w8a show more stable behavior than the unclipped ZOO2N baseline. Evidence concerns classical datasets rather than LLM fine-tuning. Clipping thresholds, smoothing radii, and step sizes remain choices, while optimal dimension dependence under heavy tails is unresolved.
source_title: Zeroth-Order Nonconvex Nonsmooth Optimization with Heavy-Tailed Noise

summary: Rather than treating Muon orthogonalization as an ad hoc matrix operation, this paper derives a smooth regularized polar map as the gradient of a Fenchel-dual smoothing of the nuclear norm, yielding a mirror/proximal momentum interpretation. Its finite-particle and mean-field Hamiltonian formulations establish well-posedness, propagation of chaos, exact energy dissipation, and exponential objective convergence under stated geometry assumptions, then extend the construction to product-matrix features relevant to transformer mixtures of experts.
source_title: Move on Muon : A Hamiltonian probability gradient flow perspective of Muon optimizer

summary: AMUSE combines Muon’s bulk-oriented orthogonalized updates with Schedule-Free averaging, but replaces the latter’s fixed interpolation with a horizon-independent coefficient that moves gradient evaluation from the fast iterate toward the stable averaged iterate after warmup. River-valley measurements show this suppresses high-curvature wall oscillations without sacrificing early progress; on vision, segmentation, and FineWeb LLM pretraining it dominates AdamW, Muon, and schedule-free baselines, reaching Muon’s final 720M-model result in 1.51× fewer steps.
source_title: AMUSE: Anytime Muon with Stable Gradient Evaluation

summary: IAdaPID-ADG augments adaptive PID optimization with an AMSGrad-style nonincreasing effective learning rate and DiffGrad-style modulation from consecutive-gradient changes. It reports improvements on MNIST, CIFAR-10, IARC, and AnnoCerv benchmarks. The evaluated tasks are small, the contribution composes existing mechanisms, the abstract gives no uniform numerical effect, and no official code is linked.
source_title: An Improved Adaptive PID Optimizer with Enhanced Convergence and Stability for Deep Learning

summary: SF-NorMuon makes normalized spectral training schedule-free and applies weight decay at the fast iterate so long-horizon averaging does not destabilize regularization. One configuration matches or exceeds separately tuned AdamW across 125M and 772M language models trained for 1-8x Chinchilla horizons. Validation stops at 772M, the method still exposes core optimizer hyperparameters, and no dedicated public implementation is linked.
source_title: Anytime Training with Schedule-Free Spectral Optimization

summary: Layerwise Learning Rate turns Heavy-Tailed Self-Regularization from a diagnostic into a controller: it periodically fits each layer’s weight-correlation spectrum and assigns larger steps to weakly heavy-tailed layers and smaller steps to strongly self-regularized ones, then freezes the ratios after an early calibration window. On 60M–3B LLaMA/GPT models with AdamW or Muon, it accelerates training by up to 1.5×, transfers across base rates, and improves 1B/3B zero-shot averages by about two points.
source_title: One LR Doesn't Fit All: Heavy-Tail Guided Layerwise Learning Rates for LLMs

summary: ChunkFT partitions parameters into byte-balanced chunks, including slices within a matrix, and rotates active chunks for consecutive local updates while freezing the others. AdamW moments persist across rotations, with per-chunk counters for bias correction; chunk-aware backward avoids dense inactive gradients. Llama-2-7B fine-tuning at sequence length 1,024 uses 13.72 GB in one reported configuration, and a batch-eight timing improves over BAdam and HiFT. This is a block-coordinate optimization wrapper with CPU-state streaming, not a new AdamW formula. Its convergence discussion begins with block-gradient updates, while practical speed depends on custom backward operators, transfer bandwidth, and chunk scheduling.
source_title: ChunkFT: Byte-Streamed Optimization for Memory-Efficient Full Fine-Tuning

summary: This method uses microbatch cross-fitting to decouple gradient numerators from adaptive preconditioners and a delta-method correction for inverse-root bias, wrapping AdamW, Sophia, or Shampoo. On Qwen2.5-0.5B it reduces held-out loss by 0.15, 0.07, and 0.11 nats for the three optimizers respectively. Evidence is limited to a 0.5B model and the required microbatch organization adds implementation and sampling cost.
source_title: Correcting Stochastic Update Bias in Preconditioned Language Model Optimizers

summary: DualOptim+ shares a base optimizer state between retain and forget objectives, maintains a delta state for each, and recombines them according to gradient conflict. On safety unlearning it reports 56.45% overall score and 32.81% utility; 8-bit states lower peak memory from 39.04 to 33.68 GB per GPU with similar quality. The extra states and controller are specific to machine unlearning rather than general pretraining.
source_title: DualOptim+: Bridging Shared and Decoupled Optimizer States for Better Machine Unlearning in Large Language Models

summary: HORST noncommutatively composes an adaptive $\ell_\infty$ step with a hyperbolic mirror map that promotes $\ell_1$ sparsity, aligning the update geometry with sparse Transformer training. It reports significant gains over AdamW on every tested sparsity level in vision and language, with the largest improvements at high sparsity. The method is specialized to sparse training, the abstract gives no common effect size, and the linked pruning repository does not verify a HORST implementation.
source_title: HORST: Composing Optimizer Geometries for Sparse Transformer Training

summary: Ada2MS continuously interpolates between coordinatewise and global second-moment normalization through exponential mixing, gradually shifting AdamW-like adaptive updates toward momentum-SGD-like behavior while preserving update-scale stability. Under a shared vision-comparison protocol, SwinV2-S CIFAR-100 top-1 error is 29.17% versus AdamW's 29.38%, although Lion remains better at 28.67%. On VOC detection with YOLOv7-tiny, mAP@0.5 reaches 59.40% versus AdamW's 59.12%; U-Net segmentation is competitive rather than best. The method adds a mixing schedule and retains adaptive state. More hybrid baselines, switching-schedule ablations, and non-visual validation are explicitly left open; the advertised repository currently contains no implementation.
source_title: Ada2MS: A Hybrid Optimization Algorithm Based on Exponential Mixing of Elementwise and Global Second-Moment Estimates

summary: AR1-ZO cycles through matched rank-one LoRA column–row pairs and calibrates their active scaling to preserve finite-difference signal at higher adapter ranks. Each step uses two forward evaluations and perturbs only an atom-sized block, avoiding auxiliary bases, activation hooks, and curvature estimates. OPT and Qwen3 experiments from 1.7B to 32B parameters report stronger matched-query ZO fine-tuning; OPT-2.7B SQuAD F1 reaches 77.8 versus MeZO-LoRA's 64.6. First-order Adam remains stronger on many tasks. Rank still determines how long all atoms take to revisit, so active-atom stationarity is not rank-free full-adapter convergence, and broader free-form generation needs further evaluation.
source_title: AR1-ZO: Topology-Aware Rank-1 Zeroth-Order Queries for High-Rank LoRA Fine-Tuning

summary: FSGD couples an Oja-style streaming estimate of a low-dimensional latent factor space with SGD, optionally freezing the learned projection after calibration.
