In a d=4000 experiment its factor neural network reaches 0.0687 test loss and approaches an oracle projection with less time and memory than ambient SGD. Theory assumes a latent-factor data model, and empirical evidence is dominated by synthetic and NCEP-style settings rather than modern foundation models.
source_title: Factor Augmented High-Dimensional SGD

summary: FINCH is a learning-rate wrapper, not a new base optimizer: it divides a tuned base rate by the square root of an EMA of mini-batch loss and applies a maximum-rate cap. Motivated by an SGD forgetting bound, this schedule makes smaller updates on high-loss batches without discarding difficult tokens. Qwen3-4B and Llama-3-8B experiments report 93% less aggregate signed benchmark degradation across six settings while retaining target-task accuracy. It adds scalar bookkeeping rather than extra model passes. The analysis does not cover the AdamW used experimentally, calibration degradation remains, and the base rate still needs tuning.
source_title: Fine-Tuning Without Forgetting via Loss-Adaptive Learning Rates

summary: SMuon generalizes SGD and Muon through Schatten-p geometry, estimating a layerwise proxy-optimal p from activations, gradients, and momentum via a one-step random-feature regression; adding second moments likewise interpolates toward Adam. A Taylor–Horner fractional-polar approximation keeps overhead near 3%, while NanoGPT, ImageNette, and Qwen LoRA experiments show SMuon matches or beats the best fixed optimizer, notably improving Muon’s NanoGPT validation loss from 3.376 to 3.366 across six seeds.
source_title: From SGD to Muon: Adaptive Optimization via Schatten-p Norms

summary: Alternates expensive Muon spectral steps with cheap Lion sign steps using one dual-EMA buffer, retaining Lion/Muon memory and halving AdamW's optimizer state. The original 124M–720M study relates the period to smoothness, heavy-tailed noise, and compute and reports a favorable loss/FLOP frontier. A September-28 distributed follow-up (arXiv:2609.35297) finds period-5 LionMuon reaches the 124M Muon target with 0.79× update FLOPs, 0.69× communicated bytes, and 0.70× PCIe time; the 124M results use three seeds, 355M uses one, hyperparameters require period-dependent retuning, and the distributed comparison is limited to four-GPU DDP.
source_title: LionMuon: Alternating Spectral and Sign Descent for Efficient Training

summary: MiMuon addresses a stability weakness of always orthogonalizing momentum: when the momentum matrix has a small singular-value gap, the polar map can make Muon’s generalization bound deteriorate. It gates between Muon and raw-momentum descent using a practical Frobenius-norm proxy, proving gap-independent O(1/N) generalization with the same O(T^-1/4) convergence rate, and improves Qwen3-0.6B WikiText validation loss to 3.684 and YOLO26m Pascal-VOC fitness to 0.461 over both constituent optimizers.
source_title: MiMuon: Mixed Muon Optimizer with Improved Generalization for Large Models

summary: This paper identifies why Muon can fail after pretraining: uniform spectral whitening amplifies noisy tail modes in low-SNR RLVR and destroys useful low-rank action structure in vision-language-action models, while global matrix treatment ignores head specialization. Pion replaces whitening with a same-cost Promotion-and-Suppression Newton–Schulz polynomial, optionally per head, that flattens leading modes and suppresses tails; it improves LIBERO and real-robot success, while Muon collapses to zero reward on Qwen3 RLVR tasks that Pion solves.
source_title: Rethinking Muon Beyond Pretraining: Spectral Failures and High-Pass Remedies for VLA and RLVR

summary: AMO makes Muon’s Newton–Schulz budget operator-aware: an early observe phase measures condition numbers by operator type, projects residual-error curves, and greedily reallocates a fixed global iteration budget before smoothly locking the schedule. This targets systematic heterogeneity without per-layer overhead; across Llama-3.1 and Qwen3 pretraining from 0.6B to 1.7B, AMO gains up to 0.76 average downstream points in standard, prolonged, and continual regimes while slightly reducing update time and preserving Muon’s memory.
source_title: AMO: Adaptive Muon Orthogonalization

summary: Distance-Aware Muon separates Muon’s matrix direction from its fixed scalar radius and derives three adaptive scales: a trajectory radius, a smoothness-certificate radius, and a trust-region/one-dimensional majorization rule. The variants obtain nonconvex, star-convex, and distance-dependent rates without fixed domains, while DF-Muon improves GPT-124M WikiText-103 loss from 3.7166 to 3.6714 and ViT-Tiny CIFAR-100 top-1 from 67.69% to 67.93% over tuned fixed-radius Muon at about 5% extra runtime.
source_title: Distance-Aware Muon: Adaptive Step Scaling for Normalized Optimization

summary: MANGO augments online continual-learning updates with sigmoid gradient gates based on layer-normalized parameter magnitudes and meta-learned drift penalties. A virtual gated update is evaluated on replay examples, allowing meta-gradients to adjust stability coefficients before the actual parameter step. Five-seed ResNet-18 experiments on Split CIFAR-100, Split Tiny-ImageNet, and CLEAR-10 improve retention and accuracy over replay and regularization baselines; with a 2,000-example buffer, CIFAR-100 final accuracy is 19.72% versus LODE's 14.36%. This is a specialized SGD-based learning framework, requiring replay storage, virtual-update computation, and known task/domain boundaries. It is not established as a generic optimizer or a task-free foundation-model solution.
source_title: MANGO: Meta-Adaptive Network Gradient Optimization for Online Continual Learning

summary: Ringmaster LMO is the first asynchronous momentum method built around a linear minimization oracle, accepting a worker gradient only when its delay is below an adaptive threshold; choosing spectral-norm geometry directly covers Muon-style updates. Under generalized smoothness it proves heterogeneous-worker iteration and wall-clock bounds while recovering optimal Euclidean Ringmaster ASGD, and simulations calibrated to measured GPU times show the lowest NanoChat loss across 8- and 32-worker delay profiles and strong stochastic-quadratic performance.
source_title: Ringmaster LMO: Asynchronous Linear Minimization Oracle Momentum Method

summary: ScheduleFree+ combines schedule-free iterate averaging with restored inner Adam momentum, an adaptive Polyak step size, fully decoupled AdamC weight decay, delayed averaging, and optional averaging-weight and interpolation annealing. These changes address large-batch instability and weight-norm transients without a learning-rate grid search. LLaMA-style scaling ladders span 120M–2B parameters and 20–1000 tokens per parameter; at 1000 tokens per parameter, the 120M model reaches a matched loss with 31% less training time than tuned linear decay. Benefits are strongest on long runs: some larger short-budget models still favor linear decay. Warmup, weight decay, averaging settings, and additional state remain necessary.
source_title: ScheduleFree+: Scaling Learning-Rate-Free & Schedule-Free Learning to Large Language Models

summary: The symmetry-compatible principle designs each parameter-block update to be equivariant to its model reparameterizations while projecting away quotient-redundant directions, unifying Muon, SSD, Scion, and polar updates under bi-orthogonal symmetry. It yields specialized one-sided, row-normalized, hybrid, and projected rules for embeddings, language heads, SwiGLU matrices, and MoE routers; Qwen3, Gemma3, OLMoE, and gpt-oss pretraining consistently lowers validation loss, while router-aware updates also reduce expert imbalance and router z-loss.
source_title: Symmetry-Compatible Principle for Optimizer Design: Embeddings, LM Heads, SwiGLU MLPs, and MoE Routers

summary: Q-LocalAdam compresses client-side Adam states using blockwise linear INT8 encoding for signed momentum and logarithmic INT8 encoding for positive variance, while retaining full-precision model weights and arithmetic for each update. States are reset each federated round and FedAvg aggregation is unchanged. On CIFAR-10/100 ResNet-18 experiments across Dirichlet heterogeneity levels, stored optimizer memory falls 3.37-fold; under extreme CIFAR-100 heterogeneity, best accuracy improves from 55.73% to 61.47%. Multi-seed experiments support the reported gains. The saving concerns persistent optimizer states, not total peak training memory; dequantized FP32 temporaries remain, and evidence is limited to small federated vision benchmarks.
source_title: Q-LocalAdam: Memory-Efficient Client-Side Adaptive Optimization for Edge Federated Learning

summary: RSC-ZO clips each scalar directional finite-difference estimate before aggregating two-point zeroth-order queries, limiting heavy-tailed outliers without storing full adaptive moment vectors. The paper proves high-probability convergence under bounded noise moments and introduces momentum variants that reduce the query batch per iteration. RoBERTa-large fine-tuning on small SNLI, MNLI, and TREC training subsets improves over MeZO, including SNLI accuracy of 83.0 versus 74.2 in the reported single-momentum setting. These experiments use 100,000 steps and task-specific clipping-threshold searches. Reduced per-step query counts do not eliminate total evaluation complexity, and guarantees retain dimension-dependent factors.
source_title: Stochastic Zeroth-Order Optimization Under Heavy-Tailed Noise

summary: CGTVR combines decentralized gradient tracking, clipped updates, and recursive variance reduction using local rather than global smoothness estimates. Its staggered variant restarts each agent's estimator when displacement exceeds an epoch radius, allowing less conservative clipping and avoiding broadcasts of local smoothness constants. A relative-uniform-continuity condition controls changing local curvature and supports finite-sum complexity guarantees. Quadratic inverse and dimension-reduction experiments compare data passes with GT-VR, GT-SARAH, and D-GET. Practical inverse-problem estimates replace a prohibitively conservative smoothness bound with a Gaussian-model approximation, and baseline restart settings are modified. Computing suitable local curvature bounds remains problem-dependent; neural-network and language-model training are not demonstrated.
source_title: Clipped Stochastic Gradient Tracking For Locally Smooth Functions

summary: DynMuon treats spectral shaping as a continuum UΣ^pVᵀ, with SGD at p=1, Muon at p=0, and inverse-like updates at p=-1, then uses a decreasing schedule from positive to mildly negative p. Its noise-aware curvature model explains why dominant modes should be favored early and flatter residual modes later; efficient Newton–Schulz polynomial corrections add at most 2.5% step cost and cut the steps to target by 10.6–26.5% across 127M–1.1B GPT pretraining.
source_title: DynMuon: A Dynamic Spectral Shaping View of Muon

summary: CT-AGD estimates local curvature from finite-difference quotients and uses inexpensive safeguards to limit minibatch noise and estimator bias. Across the reported benchmarks it reaches matched accuracy in 33% fewer epochs on average with storage and compute comparable to Adam. Its controller includes heuristic protections, the abstract does not identify large-model experiments, and no official implementation is linked.
source_title: Accelerated Gradient Descent for Faster Convergence with Minimal Overhead

summary: NAPTS combines parallel, locally constrained Adam subdomain updates with a nonlinear additive Schwarz preconditioner and a windowed nonmonotone trust-region acceptance test. Cached boundary activations and downstream gradients reduce local recomputation, while controlled temporary loss increases avoid rejecting useful global proposals. A 1.2M-parameter CIFAR-10 CNN experiment reports 115.88 seconds per epoch versus APTS's 169.14, with comparable validation accuracy and roughly one-third as many rejected steps. This is an improvement within the preconditioned trust-region family, not a universal throughput win: Adam/SGD takes about 40 seconds per epoch in the same setup. Additional local solves, acceptance evaluations, memory windows, and domain partitioning remain required.
source_title: A Non-Monotone Preconditioned Trust-Region Method for Neural Network Training

summary: DBS-Adam multiplies Adam's base learning rate by a clipped batch-difficulty score combining EMA-normalized gradient norms and batch loss. The extra statistics are scalar, while ordinary Adam moments and model architecture remain intact. A five-seed Bi-LSTM accident-severity study with focal loss, label refinement, and SMOTE-ENN reports 95.22% accuracy versus AdamW's 95.12%. Accuracy differences are not statistically significant; only precision against AdaBound improves significantly, by 0.30 percentage points. Reaching the best validation loss takes 17.6 epochs versus 9.4–11.2 for comparators. Evidence therefore supports a small, domain-specific adaptive variant, not a demonstrated generic speedup or large-model replacement.
source_title: Novel Dynamic Batch-Sensitive Adam Optimiser for Vehicular Accident Injury Severity Prediction

summary: HMSFW tracks a stochastic Jacobian and inner-function values, then passes their affine model to a generalized linear minimization oracle for nonsmooth compositional objectives. Polyak and Taylor-corrected variants trade memory against assumptions. Under finite variance, guarantees give O(K^-1/4) nonconvex gaps and, under model minorization, O(K^-1/3) convex error. The revised paper tests group-robust MovieLens matrix completion at equal optimizer time, obtaining lower mean test losses than ablations and projection-based baselines. These five-seed comparisons make no statistical-significance claim, and the best fixed-inner-budget variants lack the certified-oracle guarantee. Generalized oracle solves are nontrivial; neural-network and heavy-tailed empirical validation remain absent.
source_title: Stochastic Compositional Optimization via Hybrid Momentum Frank--Wolfe

summary: CoCD reuses historical coordinate-gradient estimates through a coherent momentum-style update instead of discarding them after each finite-difference block. The method is interpreted as warm-started block-cyclic coordinate descent, with explicit compute and memory budgets; larger smoothing radii can stabilize the resulting landscape under the analyzed error bounds. MLP, CNN, and ResNet-20 experiments up to roughly 270,000 parameters improve sample efficiency and stability against ordinary block coordinate and randomized ZO baselines. Constant per-step query cost does not remove the need to refresh many coordinates. Beyond small-to-medium models the necessary compute budget becomes impractical, and LLM fine-tuning is proposed as future work rather than demonstrated.
source_title: Turning Stale Gradients into Stable Gradients: Coherent Coordinate Descent with Implicit Landscape Smoothing for Lightweight Zeroth-Order Optimization

summary: Adam-SHANG combines a lagged adaptive preconditioner with a curvature-aware correction derived from a Lyapunov argument, avoiding the update bias that complicates Adam convergence proofs. It establishes expectation convergence for stochastic smooth convex objectives under a conservative spectral stepsize condition. The paper provides no neural-network evidence and does not cover the nonconvex regime that dominates deep learning.
source_title: Adam-SHANG: A Convergent Adam-Type Method for Stochastic Smooth Convex Optimization

summary: DP-KFC constructs Kronecker-factored preconditioners from structured synthetic probes, estimating architecture-dependent sensitivity without spending private-data budget or requiring a public dataset. It scales gradients before privacy clipping and noise addition, extending data-free private optimization beyond diagonal geometry. Vision and language experiments include MNIST CNNs, CIFAR-100 CrossViT, BERT, and logistic regression; synthetic preconditioning reaches 94.2% MNIST accuracy at epsilon one versus DP-SGD's 91.7%. It does not always match useful public data: on StackOverflow, public preconditioning remains substantially stronger. Synthetic-probe computation, factor storage and inversion still cost resources, and deep-layer eigenvector alignment and realistic language-manifold modeling remain imperfect.
source_title: DP-KFC: Data-Free Preconditioning for Privacy-Preserving Deep Learning

summary: DP-Muon clips per-example matrix gradients in Frobenius norm, averages them with Gaussian noise, then applies momentum and Newton–Schulz orthogonalization entirely as privacy-preserving post-processing. Its analysis separates optimization, clipping, privacy, momentum-drift, and approximation errors and identifies a nonlinear noise-induced bias; the antithetic-probe DP-MuonBC cancels the leading bias at no privacy cost, outperforming DP-Adam and DP-Muon on private GPT-2 E2E and DART generation, including E2E NLL 0.449 and BLEU 34.92 at ε≈8.
source_title: DP-Muon: Differentially Private Optimization via Matrix-Orthogonalized Momentum

summary: Rescaled ASGD multiplies worker-specific learning rates by relative computation times so fast workers' more frequent updates do not overweight their local objectives. It retains asynchronous stale-gradient updates without gradient-gathering phases, additional optimizer memory, or forced worker idleness. Analysis in a fixed-computation-time model gives near-optimal leading wall-clock complexity for the equal-weighted objective and identifies vanilla ASGD's frequency-weighted target. Five-seed MNIST experiments use ten label-partitioned workers and compare fixed versus fluctuating computation times. The latter regime lies outside the theorem; correcting objective inconsistency also sacrifices some fast-worker progress. Evidence is a small proof of concept, not a distributed large-model throughput validation.
source_title: Rescaled Asynchronous SGD: Optimal Distributed Optimization under Data and System Heterogeneity

summary: This work argues that Muon’s main benefit is spectral flattening: polar preconditioning makes its stable step size depend on the average rather than largest gradient singular value, and a K-FAC/PL analysis predicts a better effective condition ratio. Controlled CIFAR-10 convolution experiments confirm faster milestone attainment and stability where SGD diverges; the proposed Frobenius normalization further reduces the dominant activation-covariance eigenvalue, letting Muon exceed 80% accuracy at a learning rate where unnormalized Muon stays below 50%.
source_title: Spectral Flattening Is All Muon Needs: How Orthogonalization Controls Learning Rate and Convergence

summary: BMFO addresses bilevel optimization with a fixed compact polyhedral lower feasible set and a strongly convex lower objective. It smooths lower constraints with a logarithmic barrier, tracks exact and penalized lower solutions using barrier-metric gradient steps, and forms a first-order proxy for the outer update. The explicit constraint-barrier Hessian supplies geometry without differentiating the lower objective twice, although general constraints still require metric linear solves. Dikin-neighborhood analysis yields deterministic and upper-noise-only stochastic stationarity guarantees for the smoothed surrogate. Congestion-toll and constrained MNIST hypercleaning experiments show favorable update costs or validation-loss progress against selected bilevel baselines. Coupled constraints and fully stochastic lower oracles remain outside scope.
source_title: A Barrier-Metric First-Order Method for Linearly Constrained Bilevel Optimization

summary: This paper extends stochastic spectral preconditioning to constrained or regularized nonconvex problems through a matching anisotropic proximal step, avoiding spurious fixed points created by Euclidean projection after a Muon/Scion direction. It proves heavy-tail, STORM variance-reduced, and adaptive convergence while analyzing finite Polar Express/Newton–Schulz polynomials rather than an idealized matrix sign; spectral- and Frobenius-ball experiments accelerate DivMod97 grokking, push CIFAR-10 Scion above 93%, and make constrained NanoGPT competitive with unconstrained Scion.
source_title: Constrained Stochastic Spectral Preconditioning Converges for Nonconvex Objectives

summary: BCD-SLM is a specialized block-coordinate solver for the fixed-noise scalar likelihood of probabilistic partial least squares, not a general neural-network optimizer. It combines exact-feasibility Stiefel loading updates with closed-form latent-variance updates, positive cubic-root coefficient updates, and a one-dimensional residual-noise minimization. Conditional separability avoids repeatedly optimizing every scalar block with generic manifold steps. Under exact-block and descent assumptions, the paper establishes objective monotonicity and critical-point convergence. Synthetic and multi-omics experiments compare parameter recovery, calibration, and cost with manifold, interior-point, and EM/ECM alternatives. BCD-SLM and full-manifold fitting reach similar statistical solutions; iteration reductions do not imply uniformly faster wall-clock time, and weak-factor detection remains difficult.
source_title: Exact Stiefel Optimization for Probabilistic PLS: Closed-Form Updates, Error Bounds, and Calibrated Uncertainty

summary: Spectral clipping clamps only gradient singular values above a threshold while preserving singular vectors and the remaining spectrum. The paper supplies spectrally clipped SGD guarantees under heavy-tailed noise, layerwise EMA or sliding-quantile thresholds, and truncated randomized-SVD implementations compatible with momentum, Adam, and Muon. Experiments span ResNet-18/CIFAR-10, Shakespeare NanoGPT, FineWeb GPT-2-124M, and injected low-rank Pareto noise. Reported SGDM losses are lower at matched wall-clock checkpoints despite decomposition overhead. This is an optimizer preprocessing wrapper, not a new polar-normalization rule; threshold/rank choices and tuning remain relevant, while short vision runs and small language models limit conclusions about larger-scale training.
source_title: Gradient Clipping Beyond Vector Norms: A Spectral Approach for Matrix-Valued Parameters

summary: MuonQ observes that low-bit Muon should preserve update direction, not elementwise momentum values, because the polar map discards singular magnitudes but amplifies singular-vector rotation. It combines unit-Frobenius pre-normalization, power-iteration top-k factorization with singular-aligned row/column quantization, and μ-law companding; pure 4-bit experiments on GPT-2 and LLaMA pretraining closely track FP32, improve a 1.1B zero-shot average from naïve quantization’s 39.8 to 45.2, and reduce optimizer-state memory by 7.3× on average.
source_title: MuonQ: Enhancing Low-Bit Muon Quantization via Directional Fidelity Optimization

summary: Pion updates each weight by alternating left and right orthogonal transformations generated from skew-projected gradients, preserving the entire singular spectrum and minimal hyperspherical energy without POET-style reparameterization. RMS-consistent scaling, Lie-algebra momentum, and a second-order exponential approximation give O(T^-1/2) convergence with only 3.2% extra step time; on 54B-token LLaMA-1.3B pretraining it raises downstream average to 47.69 versus Muon’s 46.34, remains stable without normalization and at 200 layers, and leads Qwen/DeepSeek RLVR averages.
source_title: Pion: A Spectrum-Preserving Optimizer via Orthogonal Equivalence Transformation

summary: RPQN minimizes smooth-plus-prox-bounded nonsmooth objectives using shifted limited-memory quasi-Newton models and actual-versus-predicted decrease tests to adapt regularization. A new compact limited-memory Kleinmichel representation supplies positive-definite rank-one curvature updates and small semismooth-Newton proximal subproblems; averaged nonmonotone globalization is also implemented. Convergence covers nonconvex losses and regularizers under local assumptions, with stronger iterate results under the KL property. MATLAB experiments include synthetic sparse logistic regression with 10,000 features and 100,000 samples, Student-t regression, and obstacle subproblems. Reported runtime advantages are within these controlled solver comparisons, not neural-pretraining evidence; subproblem solution, proximal access, memory settings, and regularization controls remain computational requirements.
source_title: Proximal Limited-Memory Quasi-Newton Methods for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization

summary: STAM adapts first-order momentum using a bounded, normalized proxy built from gradient–momentum residual statistics; volatile signals lower beta1, while stable signals restore its chosen base value. A running product replaces Adam's fixed-beta bias correction, and STAMLITE approximates the signal with fewer stored statistics. CPU-only tests show competitive nonstationary classification and hyperparameter-sweep averages, but evidence is small: MNIST/CIFAR phases use only ten updates and the tiny Transformer uses twenty. The paper establishes coefficient bounds and constant-gradient correction, not a general convergence theorem. Memory descriptions are internally inconsistent, so claimed state reductions need independent verification; larger accelerator experiments remain future work.
source_title: Stable Training with Adaptive Momentum (STAM): A Variance-Adaptive Optimizer for Non-Stationary Gradient Regimes

summary: BROS performs lower-level and auxiliary bilevel updates in random low-rank subspaces, using a Rademacher bi-probe correction to recover unbiased full-space Hessian actions rather than silently changing the hypergradient target. Under smoothness and strongly convex lower-level assumptions, its SGD-style recursion retains the full-space single-loop stationarity-rate order, with rank-dependent variance constants. Hyper-data cleaning, data-mixture learning, hyper-representation, and ViT reweighting experiments report up to 44.9% lower peak memory while closely matching full-space results. Thin-QR projector generation and correction probes add computation; aggressive rank reduction can require smaller steps or more iterations. Adaptive/momentum extensions are implementation-compatible but not covered by the main guarantee.
source_title: BROS: Bias-Corrected Randomized Subspaces for Memory-Efficient Single-Loop Bilevel Optimization

summary: Adam-to-Muon optimizer mismatch is traced to their different max-norm versus spectral-norm implicit biases, which make strong fine-tuning updates disrupt pretrained structure. Constraining updates with LoRA shrinks the mismatch by 78% on Adam-pretrained NanoChat and significantly reduces the Adam–Muon gap across T5 GLUE, Llama-2 generation, and CLIP vision tasks; rank and forgetting studies confirm the benefit weakens as update strength grows.
source_title: Can Muon Fine-tune Adam-Pretrained Models?

summary: CAQ-ZO performs zeroth-order updates in companded coordinates and aligns Rademacher finite-difference stencils with a single quantization grid, avoiding query-endpoint rounding inconsistencies. This changes the query and update geometry rather than merely attaching a quantizer to a floating-point optimizer. Matched NF4 fine-tuning experiments on Qwen2.5-1.5B and Llama-2-7B outperform QuZO, including Qwen CB accuracy of 60.5 versus 41.7 and Llama SQuAD scores of 58.6 versus 30.5. BF16 MeZO is a different-precision reference, not an equivalent memory baseline. Theory assumes scalar monotone companders and does not cover arbitrary block-coupled quantizers; forward-query costs and finite tuning budgets remain.
source_title: Compander-Aligned Query Geometry for Quantized Zeroth-Order Optimization

summary: Error whitening explains Gauss–Newton’s edge in function space: generalized Gauss–Newton projects the Newton direction onto the model tangent space under the loss-Hessian metric, while a Jacobian-only variant projects the loss gradient; both cancel nonzero singular values of JJᵀ rather than following parameter-space curvature. Sketched implementations match predicted mismatch dynamics and achieve orders-of-magnitude lower errors on regression, an Allen–Cahn PINN where Newton fails, and approximate dynamic programming where they remain stable while Adam and Muon miss value-function structure.
source_title: Error whitening: Why Gauss-Newton outperforms Newton

summary: LE-SAM fixes an adversarial loss budget instead of a perturbation radius, scaling the ascent radius approximately inversely with the current gradient norm. The implementation stops gradients through this scaling, caps the maximum radius, and anneals the budget near training completion. CIFAR-100 accuracy improves from 80.17 to 81.51 with ResNet-18 and from 83.42 to 84.91 with a wide ResNet; ImageNet ResNet-50 gains 0.71 points. Like SAM, it uses two gradient evaluations per update, plus inexpensive norm calculations. Loss-budget, radius-cap, and annealing choices remain, and large-language-model pretraining and fine-tuning are not evaluated.
source_title: Fix the Loss, Not the Radius: Rethinking the Adversarial Perturbation of Sharpness-Aware Minimization

summary: Challenging geometry-first explanations of Muon, the paper introduces Freon, a QDWH-computed Schatten family that extends beyond norm-based LMOs, and Kaon, which randomizes singular values yet retains convergence. GPT-2/NanoGPT and random-feature experiments show quasi-norm exponents and even random spectra can match or beat Muon once large modes are suppressed; a Taylor decomposition instead attributes performance to batch-gradient alignment, directional descent potential, and correctly tuned step size.
source_title: Muon is Not That Special: Random or Inverted Spectra Work Just as Well

summary: Muown decomposes each weight into row magnitudes and directions after diagnosing maximum row-norm growth—not row coherence—as the source of Muon’s spectral-norm drift; it updates magnitudes in ℓ∞ geometry while retaining Muon on directions. Mixed-geometry convergence matches optimal deterministic and stochastic rates, and FineWeb-Edu runs from 124M to 2.7B improve perplexity, widen stable learning-rate plateaus, remove meaningful weight-decay benefit, and match sharded Muon step time.
source_title: Muown: Row-Norm Control for Muon Optimization

summary: SODA generalizes optimistic dual averaging by combining gradient averaging and optimism in the dual with iterate averaging and extrapolation in the primal, recovering Muon, Lion, NAdam, Adam, and Scion through different geometries. Its hyperparameter-free wrapper anchors updates at initialization and induces a theoretically motivated 1/(k+2) decay; NanoGPT/FineWeb100 experiments show consistent gains over tuned weight decay across base optimizers, 1×–4× Chinchilla horizons, and 64M–1B scales.
source_title: Optimistic Dual Averaging Unifies Modern Optimizers

summary: This work refines mode connectivity by conditioning solution sets on optimizer-induced norm constraints, proving sufficiently wide two-layer ReLU networks are connected within AdamW, Muon, and other Lion-K regions while finite-width cross-optimizer solutions can face a genuine barrier. On 30M–50M GPT-2 models, a polychain-plus-alignment path preserves spectra within an optimizer and smoothly transitions AdamW outliers to Muon isotropy across optimizers, with intermediate models improving out-of-distribution loss.
source_title: Optimizer-Induced Mode Connectivity: From AdamW to Muon

summary: PowerStep applies a signed nonlinear power transform directly to one momentum buffer, obtaining coordinate adaptivity from an $\ell_p$ steepest-descent geometry without storing a second moment. Across Transformer models from 124M to 235B it matches Adam's convergence while halving optimizer memory; stable int8 state reduces memory by about 8x versus full-precision Adam. Evidence is concentrated on Transformer training, and the power geometry remains a tunable design choice.
source_title: PowerStep: Memory-Efficient Adaptive Optimization via $\ell_p$-Norm Steepest Descent

summary: Using a spiked rectangular gradient model, the paper argues Muon’s Newton–Schulz spectral shaping avoids AdamW’s coordinatewise dimensional trap: incoherence suppresses orthogonal drift, producing dimension-free diffusive incubation and an O(1) ballistic ejection once a spectral gap locks the signal subspace. Controlled saddles and matrix factorization up to dimension 8192, plus LLaMA-160M landscape probes, show dimension-invariant escape, sudden rank expansion, higher effective rank, and two-orders-of-magnitude spike-curvature collapse.
source_title: Dimension-Free Saddle-Point Escape in Muon

summary: Intrinsic Muon lifts any unitarily invariant norm through the Riemannian metric, avoiding the quotient-symmetry breaking and coupled tangent/norm constraints of factor-wise Muon, Spectron, and Riemannion. This yields exact closed-form LMOs on fixed-rank, SPD, Stiefel, and Grassmann manifolds with rank- rather than conditioning-dependent rates; LoRA fine-tuning reaches 86.25 GLUE average versus 81.68 for factor-wise Muon, while every intrinsic norm variant improves SPD classification.
source_title: Intrinsic Muon: Spectral Optimization on Riemannian Matrix Manifolds

summary: Through exact high-dimensional random-matrix dynamics for matrix least squares, the paper shows SignSVD—the idealized Muon limit—square-root preconditions covariance modes only when minibatches resolve them, with a critical transition at batch size equal to matrix width; SignSGD has no analogous transition. Power-law covariance analysis yields hard, mixed, and easy phases where Muon, crossover behavior, or SignSGD prevails, and Newton–Schulz Muon simulations track the predicted learning curves and scaling laws.
source_title: Phases of Muon: When Muon Eclipses SignSGD

summary: ZO-MOPI replaces ZO-Muon’s full Newton–Schulz whitening—which amplifies noisy spectral tails—with warm-started power iteration that orthogonalizes only dominant directions, supported by low-dimensional perturbations and projected momentum. A tracking-error bound and nonconvex convergence result justify the design; on OPT-13B and LLaMA-3-8B SuperGLUE fine-tuning it preserves zeroth-order memory use, often reaches target accuracy 1.5–4× faster than ZO-Muon, and remains competitive in final accuracy.
source_title: Accelerating Zeroth-Order Spectral Optimization with Partial Orthogonalization from Power Iteration

summary: AdaPreLoRA builds a diagonal Kronecker Adafactor preconditioner in full-weight space, then solves the singular LoRA factor-space system using a weighted balance criterion. The resulting update is a metric-consistent projection of the preconditioned weight direction, with O((m+n)r) state and an additional cubic-in-rank solve. GPT-2, Mistral-7B, Qwen2-7B, and diffusion-personalization experiments show competitive or improved quality across tuned LoRA baselines. Memory efficiency is not free speed: its Mistral AdamW variant uses 26.0 GB versus vanilla AdamW's 25.8 GB, but takes 0.99 versus 0.24 seconds per step. Practical performance remains task-, rank-, and learning-rate-dependent.
source_title: AdaPreLoRA: Adafactor Preconditioned Low-Rank Adaptation

summary: BroxGD replaces a projection or proximal step with a local linear optimization oracle over the intersection of the feasible set and a ball around the current iterate. The framework develops convergence guarantees for convex and nonconvex constrained problems and explains how the neighborhood radius controls progress. Extensive numerical checks include structured matrix and simplex problems, but do not show a reliable advantage over projected gradient descent across configurations. Projection-free therefore describes the outer update, not a universally cheap implementation: some local oracles themselves use projections. Neural-network training and large-language-model performance are not demonstrated.
source_title: Broximal Gradient Descent: A Projection-Free Sister of Projected Gradient Descent

summary: CGAD discounts delayed pseudo-gradients with exponential age decay and a cosine cutoff before they enter the outer Adam moments, targeting staleness in asynchronous DiLoCo. Tests from 25M to 7B parameters remain stable under delayed updates, while an ungated Adam-Decay comparison becomes sharply more seed-sensitive at large scale. It is specific to a distributed outer loop, adds two hyperparameters, and has no verified public implementation.
source_title: Cosine-Gated Adam-Decay: Drop-In Staleness-Aware Outer Optimization for Decoupled DiLoCo

summary: FedVSSAM uses a globally anchored, variance-suppressed direction to construct local SAM perturbations, guide client descent, and aggregate server updates under heterogeneous data. It aims to reduce client drift and the mismatch between local sharpness directions and global generalization, without communicating an additional auxiliary vector. Experiments span CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and DBpedia with partial client participation, showing improved accuracy or communication-round efficiency over federated SAM baselines. The method still inherits SAM's additional gradient evaluation and introduces mixing and perturbation parameters. Smoothness and heterogeneity assumptions underpin its convergence analysis; it is not uniformly superior to every non-SAM federated baseline.
source_title: FedVSSAM: Mitigating Flatness Incompatibility in Sharpness-Aware Federated Learning

summary: By reducing Muon exactly to signed momentum on diagonal matrix objectives, the paper constructs convex Lipschitz functions on which Muon fails for any offline decreasing step schedule and, for momentum below one-half, almost every nearby initialization. Viewing regularized non-Euclidean updates as compressors yields convergent error-feedback Muon, but tuned CIFAR-10 and 206M NanoGPT experiments worsen validation loss, indicating nonsmooth convex theory diagnoses a limit rather than explaining Muon’s practical success.
source_title: Muon Does Not Converge on Convex Lipschitz Functions

summary: Muon-OGD replaces the Frobenius geometry of OGD-style continual-learning projections with a spectral-norm-constrained Muon update: dual subgradient iterations correct momentum against protected low-rank directions, then Newton–Schulz supplies the matrix sign. Across T5 5/15-task streams, TRACE, and Qwen coding–math–medical curricula, it beats orthogonal-gradient baselines, reaching 78.9% standard-stream accuracy and 49.4% TRACE accuracy with less backward transfer loss.
source_title: Muon-OGD: Muon-based Spectral Orthogonal Gradient Projection for LLM Continual Learning

summary: Rennala MVR extends asynchronous optimization for heterogeneous workers with momentum variance reduction, targeting wall-clock complexity rather than a synchronous iteration count. Under mean-square smoothness, the paper gives time-complexity upper bounds and matching lower-bound regimes, and validates the exact algorithm on stochastic quadratic problems. Its MNIST study uses a small two-layer network and simulated worker times, with an implementable MARS-inspired approximation that reuses previous gradients instead of the exact theoretical recursion. Thus the neural experiment supports a practical approximation, not a direct verification of the theorem's method. Batch size, learning rate, and correction parameters require tuning.
source_title: Rennala MVR: Improved Time Complexity for Parallel Stochastic Optimization via Momentum-Based Variance Reduction

summary: Group Muon treats attention-head grouping as an optimizer hyperparameter, replacing the binary choice between full-QKV Muon and per-head MuonSplit with group-wise polar whitening. A one-step bound isolates nuclear-norm whitening gain versus additional update-norm cost, explaining why fine groups win early but over-splitting loses later; on GPT-2 Small/FineWeb, random six-head Q/K groups achieve 3.2722 validation loss versus 3.2780 for full Muon and 3.2799 for MuonSplit.
source_title: When and Why Grouping Attention Heads Accelerates Muon Optimization

summary: AdamFLIP treats PINN training as equality-constrained optimization and computes Lagrange multipliers through feedback linearization, aiming to contract constraint residuals rather than tune soft-penalty weights. Adam-style moments then precondition the feedback-linearized Lagrangian direction. Forward and inverse PDE benchmarks include Burgers, diffusion-wave, heat, and Navier–Stokes equations; the latter reports over two-thirds lower relative solution error than the next-best method. Constraint Jacobians and damped linear solves add work, and objective-versus-constraint choices remain problem dependent. Importantly, the convergence proof covers a metric-compatible variant, not exactly the experimentally used algorithm, and requires full-row-rank constraint Jacobians that may fail near feasibility.
source_title: AdamFLIP: Adaptive Momentum Feedback Linearization Optimization for Hard Constrained PINN Training

summary: MoLF uses an optimizer-level gate to route exact gradients between full-rank and LoRA experts, while MoLF-Efficient routes between two LoRA groups. Across Gemma-3-1B and Qwen2.5 models it stays within 1.5% of the better full-fine-tuning or LoRA choice in every setting; the efficient variant reports gains of 20% on factual tasks and 9% on medical or SQL tasks. Evidence is confined to 1-3B supervised adaptation rather than pretraining.
source_title: Beyond LoRA vs. Full Fine-Tuning: Gradient-Guided Optimizer Routing for LLM Adaptation

summary: OrScale adds time-varying layerwise trust ratios to Muon, but—unlike naive Muon–LAMB ports—divides by the Frobenius norm of the actual coupled update λW+sQ; OrScale-LM further uses Moonlight scaling and one-time calibration to preserve learning-rate transfer. It proves O(T^-1/2) nuclear-norm convergence and a strict heterogeneity-dependent descent gain, raises CIFAR-10 DavidNet accuracy from Muon’s 93.70% to 94.05%, and improves Muon+Moonlight at three of four 125M–1.1B FineWeb-Edu scales.
source_title: OrScale: Orthogonalised Optimization with Layer-Wise Trust-Ratio Scaling

summary: These penalty-based first-order methods handle bilevel problems with minimax lower levels without requiring strong lower-level convexity. A lifted penalty formulation and inexact proximal-point subproblems reduce the task to first-order minimax optimization; constrained convex lower problems follow through Lagrangian duality. Deterministic analysis gives approximately epsilon-to-the-minus-four oracle complexity for an epsilon-KKT point, while the stochastic extension has substantially higher epsilon-to-the-minus-nine complexity. Experiments cover constrained linear bilevel problems and deep distributionally robust learning on CelebA and Waterbirds, jointly tuning representations and robustness parameters. The guarantees concern lifted-space stationarity under compact-domain assumptions, not universal improvement over standard single-level neural-network optimizers.
source_title: Penalty-Based First-Order Methods for Bilevel Optimization with Minimax and Constrained Lower-Level Problems

summary: PolarAdamW polarizes AdamW’s coordinate-preconditioned direction, preserving Muon’s spectral control while intentionally breaking its proved Schur multiplicity-basis equivariance. The controlled double dissociation shows why both properties matter: on four random 100-class ImageNet subsets it beats Muon by 1.93 points at 100 epochs and 1.37 at 300, whereas on 100-seed SO(3)-equivariant point-cloud regression Muon wins at every width with a growing capacity gap.
source_title: PolarAdamW: Disentangling Spectral Control and Schur Gauge-Equivariance in Matrix Optimisation

summary: LMO-IGT accelerates Lion/Muon-style linear-minimization-oracle updates by evaluating one stochastic gradient at a transported lookahead point, avoiding the doubled gradient cost of variance-reduced LMO; its regularized support function unifies gradient-norm and Frank–Wolfe-gap stationarity. The theory improves stochastic LMO complexity from O(ε^-4) to O(ε^-3.5), between plain and O(ε^-3) variance-reduced methods, while Muon-IGT gives the best CIFAR-10 accuracy and lower Shakespeare/OpenWebText losses at nearly Muon’s wall-clock cost.
source_title: Accelerating LMO-Based Optimization via Implicit Gradient Transport

summary: GONO measures cosine agreement between consecutive gradients and uses it to adapt Adam's first-moment coefficient, reducing momentum when directions oscillate. Its detector reaches F1=1.00 versus 0.45 for gradient norm in a controlled test, and the optimizer is competitive on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ResNet-18 benchmarks. The reported accuracies come from relatively small tasks and do not establish a large-model advantage.
source_title: Directional Consistency as a Complementary Optimization Signal: The GONO Framework

summary: This work supplies the first Muon theory simultaneously covering practical Nesterov momentum, finite-step Newton–Schulz polar maps, and α-heavy-tailed stochastic gradients, using an alignment/feasibility framework that also admits randomized low-rank sketches. It proves optimal ε-stationarity complexity O(ε^{-(3α-2)/(α-1)}) and α-adaptive guarantees when σ1=0; randomized Muon cuts NanoGPT optimizer cost from 2,136 to 251 GFLOPs at 29.72 versus 28.08 full-Muon perplexity, and CIFAR-10 cost from 14.80 to 8.08 GFLOPs at 93.62% versus 93.70% accuracy.
source_title: Muon with Nesterov Momentum: Heavy-Tailed Noise and (Randomized) Inexact Polar Decomposition

summary: Orth-Dion identifies Dion’s column normalization—not low-rank subspace selection—as a geometric error: it can inflate the Ky Fan dual norm by √r, whereas QR-orthogonalizing the right factor forces a valid rank-r polar direction at unchanged communication. The resulting O(√(Lr/T)) rate matches exact spectral descent; LLaMA-320M measurements confirm ν=1 and lower loss at every rank, while adaptive rank reaches Dion’s best loss 18.3% sooner and matches its 17.1B step time.
source_title: Orth-Dion: Eliminating Geometric Mismatch in Distributed Low-Rank Spectral Optimization

summary: Pro-KLShampoo exploits a newly observed spike-and-flat spectrum in KL-Shampoo’s Kronecker factors, retaining full preconditioning in a tracked rank-r subspace and using Muon-style orthogonalization on the complement to algebraically recover per-direction whitening. With an idealized O(T^-1/2) guarantee, it beats KL-Shampoo at every tested rank on GPT-2 124M/350M and LLaMA 134M/450M, lowering validation loss and peak memory and saving 2.28–13.43% wall-clock time to matched loss.
source_title: Pro-KLShampoo: Projected KL-Shampoo with Whitening Recovered by Orthogonalization

summary: MoLS calibrates Adam-family updates at module level by estimating gradient signal-to-noise ratios during warmup and scaling each module's learning rate relative to a reference module. It complements coordinatewise adaptivity rather than replacing the underlying optimizer, and also works with Adam-mini, 8-bit Adam, and LoRA. In LLaMA-1.3B pretraining, validation perplexity falls from 14.51 to 13.45 with about 1.66% longer training; larger pretraining and downstream fine-tuning experiments report consistent gains. The scaling is static after its initial estimate and can miss late-training changes. Sampling noise, batch size, reference-module choice, and the interaction with adaptive preconditioning remain practical limitations.
source_title: Revealing Modular Gradient Noise Imbalance in LLMs: Calibrating Adam via Signal-to-Noise Ratio

summary: PrePO is an optimizer-trajectory wrapper: two temporary same-batch updates estimate motion persistence, predict a virtual multi-step endpoint, partially reposition parameters, then apply a fresh-gradient correction from the original saved optimizer state. Probes are discarded, so active cost stays three backward passes regardless of virtual depth. AdamW uses coordinatewise trend ratios and Muon uses a matrixwise scalar fit. Reported Muon RLVR experiments show up to 2.52-fold matched-target wall-clock speedup, while SFT gains shrink to about 1.2–1.4-fold because each wrapper step costs more. Depth, blending, clipping, and an entropy-triggered fallback matter; convergence guarantees require bounded prediction and gradient-bias errors. Some OPD configurations run slower.
source_title: Skip What You Can Predict: Predictive Repositioning for Policy Optimization for Efficient LLM Training

summary: This proximal-gradient scheme scales its step using accumulated squared gradient-mapping norms, incorporating the regularizer rather than accumulating raw gradients alone. One recursion handles smooth nonconvex, smooth convex, and nonsmooth convex objectives without supplied smoothness or noise constants; a convex accelerated variant achieves near-optimal smooth stochastic rates. Regularized nonconvex SVM and logistic-regression experiments compare gradient mappings, objective gaps, and accuracy. The accelerated method matches AcceleGrad on the reported non-composite test, while the basic method can be slower and its last iterate degrades at larger initial scales. Bounded iterates and noise assumptions matter, and acceleration additionally uses a known domain-diameter condition.
source_title: Universal Adaptive Proximal Gradient Methods via Gradient Mapping Accumulation

summary: By changing the comparison from Euclidean stationarity to the geometry sign updates actually optimize—ℓ∞ smoothness, ℓ1 stationarity, and separable coordinate noise—the paper derives matching SignSGD upper/lower bounds and an SGD lower bound that yields up to a d-fold advantage under sparse noise. It extends the result to spectral smoothness and nuclear-norm stationarity for Muon, while GPT-2-124M/C4 measurements show noise density falling toward 0.03 and SignSGD continuing to improve after SGD plateaus.
source_title: When and Why SignSGD Outperforms SGD: A Theoretical Study Based on $\ell_1$-norm Lower Bounds

summary: SHAPE is a learned task-family optimizer that lifts gradient descent into a port-Hamiltonian phase space with directional momentum, energy shaping, and a slower planner-memory controller. Fixed event stages trigger new exploration when local equilibria become uninformative, balancing descent, basin exploitation, and minima hunting under a limited oracle budget. Held-out synthetic and differentiable engineering tasks show improved best-so-far gaps and hit rates, including multi-well, phase-retrieval, and control objectives. It is not a neural-network training benchmark: RMSProp remains stronger on high-dimensional Rastrigin, and good control minima do not always yield the best terminal objective. Meta-training, rollout particles, and stage budgets add substantial design choices.
source_title: When Descent Is Too Stable: Event-Triggered Hamiltonian Learning to Optimize

summary: BAOC profiles blockwise gradient stability and anisotropy, then allocates optimizer precision, momentum, and related configuration choices subject to memory and time budgets. Across vision, language, and diffusion workloads it reports substantial optimizer-state savings while preserving training quality. The method needs a gradient-stream profiling phase, combines configuration search with update design, and its linked implementation remains an anonymous review snapshot.
source_title: Budget-aware Auto Optimizer Configurator

summary: MACRO projects momentum toward a weight manifold's tangent space, applies a matrix-sign transformation, rescales the direction using the constraint radius, and retracts updated weights onto Frobenius or spectral spheres. Initialization-based radius rules control activation and relative-update scales. Five-seed Qwen3-style pretraining from 240M to 1.2B parameters at 40 tokens per parameter improves over Muon; MACRO-fro obtains 1.2B validation perplexity 12.85 versus 12.99. Its reported 240M step cost is 1.6% higher than Muon's. Constraints also reduce BF16 update cancellation without eliminating late-stage precision loss. Radius tuning remains, and the single-loop matrix-sign direction only approximately satisfies tangency. Costs use plain implementations without specialized kernels.
source_title: Demystifying Manifold Constraints in LLM Pre-training

summary: By separating layerwise norm choice, cross-layer aggregation, and constrained versus regularized normalization, this work turns Muon/Adam hybrids into a systematic non-Euclidean steepest-descent design space and derives MuonMax. FineWeb experiments over 36 variants show MuonMax is far less learning-rate sensitive than Muon; adding model-based Momo momentum further widens the robust hyperparameter range and often improves validation loss, motivating MuonMax-Momo for untuned tasks.
source_title: An Exploration of Non-Euclidean Gradient Descent: Muon and its Many Variants

summary: FiBeR filters privatized gradients in innovation space and analytically subtracts the attenuated privacy-noise contribution from AdamW's second moment, correcting the miscalibration caused by temporal filtering. At matched privacy budgets it reports improvements over state-of-the-art private optimizers on multiple vision and language tasks. The method and analysis are specific to differentially private training and assume a stable linear filtering model.
source_title: FIBER: A Differentially Private Optimizer with Filter-Aware Innovation Bias Correction

summary: This paper replaces the fragile uniformly bounded-variance assumption with expected smoothness, or the ABC condition, for a unified momentum-LMO family covering normalized SGD, sign/Adam-like directions, and spectral Muon updates. A new self-bounding argument controls momentum’s history coupling and yields nonconvex rates, explicit τ-nice sampling laws, an optimal batch size, and the prediction that sample-efficient momentum rises with batch size; linear and matrix regression recover the predicted diagonal optimum.
source_title: General Analysis of LMO-based Optimizers: Beyond Bounded Variance

summary: Layerwise LQR rewrites Newton, Gauss-Newton, Fisher, and related quadratic steepest-descent steps as a finite-horizon control problem, then learns reusable diagonal or Kronecker-structured inverse preconditioners under that global objective. ResNet and Transformer experiments improve optimization dynamics and often final test performance with modest wall-clock overhead. Structured relaxations still discard part of the dense geometry, and the abstract gives no uniform quantitative gain.
source_title: Layerwise LQR for Geometry-Aware Optimization of Deep Networks

summary: This paper recasts weight-decayed Lion and Muon as stochastic Frank–Wolfe on ℓ∞- and spectral-norm constraint sets, proving nonconvex Frank–Wolfe-gap convergence and that gap stationarity yields KKT points of the corresponding constrained problems. Gradient-clipped and clipped variance-reduced extensions handle heavy-tailed noise on general compact sets without giant batches; on Shakespeare nanoGPT, Lion+ and Muon+ lower validation loss and reach targets in 19.18% and 5.88% fewer steps than their unclipped baselines.
source_title: Lions and Muons: Optimization via Stochastic Frank-Wolfe

summary: Using directional smoothness, the authors define optimizer-relative generalized sharpness as the maximum Hessian quadratic form over an arbitrary norm ball, covering Euclidean and preconditioned GD, ℓ∞ descent, block coordinate descent, spectral GD, and momentum-free Muon. Quadratic analysis recovers the 2/η stability boundary, while neural-network experiments show each geometry progressively sharpens then oscillates near or above that threshold and becomes unstable on its local quadratic model after entering the edge-of-stability regime.
source_title: Non-Euclidean Gradient Descent Operates at the Edge of Stability

summary: Nora improves RMNP’s cheap row-normalized approximation to Muon by first projecting momentum rowwise onto each weight row’s tangent space, removing scale-invariant radial noise while preserving O(mn) preconditioning. Its µP analysis prescribes η∝n^-1/2 and its nonconvex theory proves projected stationarity; in optimizer-specific sweeps on 60M/135M LLaMA models Nora obtains the best losses (3.37/3.079), while row normalization is about 9.5–73.5× faster than five-step Newton–Schulz on representative matrices.
source_title: Nora: Normalized Orthogonal Row Alignment for Scalable Matrix Optimizer

summary: MEAZO replaces ZO-Adam's per-coordinate moments with one bias-corrected scalar moving average of projected finite-difference gradients, using it to adapt the global step size. The motivating analysis shows that isotropic high-dimensional ZO estimators lose much of the coordinate heterogeneity that makes Adam useful, so vector moments can waste memory. Across OPT and LLaMA fine-tuning tasks, MEAZO matches adaptive ZO performance with ZO-SGD-like state requirements and improves step-size robustness, including grouped settings. The theory assumes smooth sample losses, bounded variance, and bounded gradients. It does not claim better final accuracy than carefully tuned ZO-SGD, and grouped estimators can require substantially more forward evaluations.
source_title: On Adaptivity in Zeroth-Order Optimization

summary: PF-AGD combines accelerated gradient descent, adaptive backtracking estimates of local smoothness, and restart tests that detect insufficient progress or negative curvature. It obtains a near O(epsilon^-5/3) deterministic first-order complexity without requiring smoothness constants as inputs. Experiments cover robust regression, small MNIST neural networks, and analytic objectives, showing advantages over AGD-until-guilty and competitive behavior against other accelerated methods. This is not a stochastic large-model optimizer: the improved rate assumes Lipschitz third derivatives, and the practical procedure still includes line searches and restart overhead. Results do not establish uniform superiority over conjugate-gradient baselines.
source_title: A Parameter-Free First-Order Algorithm for Non-Convex Optimization with $\tilde{\mkern1mu O}(\epsilon^{-5/3})$ Global Rate

summary: Anon makes preconditioner adaptivity continuously tunable over a real-valued range, interpolating between SGD-like and Adam-like behavior and extrapolating beyond both; an incremental-delay update replaces AMSGrad's hard maximum. Convex and nonconvex guarantees accompany reported gains on image classification, diffusion, and language modeling. The abstract provides no common quantitative effect size and no official implementation is linked.
source_title: Anon: Extrapolating Adaptivity Beyond SGD and Adam

summary: Sign-Muon combines Muon’s local polar momentum with signSGD-style one-bit transmission and majority-vote aggregation, optionally re-orthogonalizing the aggregated sign matrix without extra communication. It proves O(T^-1/2) spectral-smooth nonconvex convergence and a 1/√M noise benefit across workers, cuts bandwidth 32× versus float32, reaches 92.15% CIFAR-10 accuracy and 92.02% on four GPUs with 37% less time, and improves nanoGPT perplexity with favorable scaling to 16 GPUs.
source_title: SignMuon: Communication-Efficient Distributed Muon Optimization

summary: AdamO augments Adam critic updates with a decoupled weight-orthogonality correction, scaled by a per-layer task-alignment budget and bounded relative to the ordinary Adam step. A frozen, linearized temporal-difference model links value collapse to the update operator's spectral radius; conflict-free corrections obtain conditional one-step safety, while positive conflict budgets allow quantified degradation. Across six offline-RL algorithms and D4RL domains, the optimizer generally improves returns and suppresses collapse, including more than doubling TD3+BC's average AntMaze score. It adds meaningful runtime cost: one TD3+BC comparison increases from 144 to 172 minutes. The guarantees are local and task-specific rather than general LLM-training results.
source_title: AdamO: A Collapse-Suppressed Optimizer for Offline RL

summary: Ordered momentum weights arriving gradients according to their original timestamps rather than their arrival order, correcting the recency distortion caused by data-dependent asynchronous delays. The framework extends to ordered STORM and an anytime double-momentum method, with convex and nonconvex guarantees under stated delay and smoothness assumptions. Fashion-MNIST experiments with a small CNN and simulated heterogeneous workers show a wider stable learning-rate range than unordered momentum when delays correlate with data. Updates need not wait for a global ordering queue, but require timestamp-aware weighting. Experiments do not establish throughput gains on a real large-model distributed-training cluster.
source_title: Bringing Order to Asynchronous SGD: Towards Optimality under Data-Dependent Delays with Momentum

summary: AdaMeZO reconstructs Adam-style first- and second-moment guidance from forward-only zeroth-order observations without keeping parameter-sized moment buffers. It outperforms MeZO while requiring up to 70% fewer forward passes and retaining inference-level memory. The study is limited to LLM fine-tuning, and its gains remain subject to the query cost and variance of zeroth-order optimization.
source_title: AdaMeZO: Adam-style Zeroth-Order Optimizer for LLM Fine-tuning Without Maintaining the Moments

summary: RS-NAG uses a three-sequence accelerated recurrence driven only by low-dimensional projected gradients. Separate convex and strongly convex variants recover classical Nesterov acceleration with a full sketch, while matrix-smoothness and sketch-moment bounds expose when Haar, coordinate, or Gaussian subspaces improve directional-derivative complexity. Quadratic and regularized logistic-regression experiments support the predicted dependence on sketch distribution and effective geometry. The accounting charges a full gradient as d directional derivatives and a rank-r sketch as r queries; this is appropriate for forward-mode or communication-limited settings, not a universal reverse-mode wall-clock comparison. Problem and sketch constants remain inputs, and no nonconvex large-transformer benchmark is supplied.
source_title: Randomized Subspace Nesterov Accelerated Gradient

summary: DSGD dynamically downweights gradient contributions from correctly classified examples to reduce cancellation against misclassified examples within a minibatch. The classification-specific adjustment can be implemented through weighted losses without separate per-example backward passes, and combines with an ordinary backend optimizer. Experiments across fourteen NLP and vision tasks with RoBERTa, LLaMA, and ViT report improved mean accuracy and lower seed sensitivity, particularly under strong class imbalance; several tasks match larger bagging ensembles without their repeated-training cost. The theoretical stability and stationary-point comparisons rely on the stated gradient structure assumptions. Its mechanism depends on classification correctness and is not directly demonstrated for next-token pretraining or general generation.
source_title: Dynamic Scaled Gradient Descent for Stable Fine-Tuning for Classifications

summary: LiMuon combines momentum variance reduction with randomized SVD so that Muon-style orthogonalization can be computed at controllable low rank, reducing both state memory and stochastic-oracle cost. It proves O(ε^-3) sample complexity under ordinary and generalized smoothness versus O(ε^-4) for prior Newton–Schulz Muon analyses; Mamba-130M, Qwen2.5-0.5B, and Tiny-ImageNet ViT experiments show low-rank memory–quality tradeoffs, while full-rank LiMuon gives the best perplexities, accuracy, and time to target.
source_title: LiMuon: Light and Fast Muon Optimizer for Large Models

summary: MuLoCo replaces DiLoCo’s AdamW inner optimizer with Muon, whose orthogonalized local steps produce more consistently aligned, stable-norm pseudogradients across workers and are therefore easier to aggregate and compress. Decoder-only LM studies show row-wise/statistical 2-bit deltas retain strong quality at 8× lower communication, whereas global-linear 2-bit degrades and error feedback only partly recovers it; MuLoCo degrades less as worker count or synchronization interval grows, and tests through 15B parameters show larger critical batches and a Pareto-optimal single-worker performance–time tradeoff.
source_title: MuLoCo: Muon is a Practical Inner Optimizer for DiLoCo

summary: Scale-Shape Dual Newton solves entropy-regularized least squares over nonnegative variables using a reformulated dual that separates total scale from normalized shape. Stable log-sum-exp and softmax evaluations avoid exponential overflow, while a nonsingular Jacobian enables damped inexact Newton steps with positivity safeguards and residual-based backtracking. The paper proves global linear residual convergence and local superlinear-to-quadratic behavior under stated conditions, plus stability of the solution map. Analytic-continuation experiments on quantum Monte Carlo data demonstrate robustness where safeguarded classical dual Newton stalls at large scales. This is a specialized inverse-problem solver, not an evaluated neural-network optimizer; small regularization can still worsen conditioning and convergence.
source_title: A Scale-Shape Dual Newton Method for Entropic Least Squares

summary: NeuroPlastic multiplies raw gradients by a clipped combination of normalized gradient, activity-like magnitude, and memory-like moment signals, then applies norm clipping and RMS-based homeostatic gain control. Its rule-based modulation uses no extra trainable controller, although it maintains several moving-average statistics and introduces modulation hyperparameters. Across three seeds, Fashion-MNIST accuracy improves by roughly 0.6 percentage points over a controlled gradient-only ablation, with similar small gains in reduced-data settings. On CIFAR-10 ResNet-18, tuned SGD, Adam, and AdamW still achieve higher final performance. The paper therefore supports a formulation-sensitive optimizer extension, not general superiority, and provides no transformer-scale evidence.
source_title: NeuroPlastic: A Plasticity-Modulated Optimizer for Biologically Inspired Learning Dynamics

summary: SSF performs heterogeneity-corrected federated updates in a low-dimensional subspace while preserving full-dimensional control information through residual backfill when projectors change. This avoids repeatedly discarding complementary drift information and retains a standard parallel-speedup term in its nonconvex analysis. Matrix-regression experiments show favorable rank–accuracy trade-offs and greater stability than subspace-only controls. In a CIFAR-100 ResNet-110 submission run, final accuracy is 45.43% versus FedAvg's 34.35%, but full SCAFFOLD remains stronger at 52.92%. The deep-learning schedules are not compute-matched, and full-space dual information still exists; reduced active-device state should not be confused with eliminating all full-dimensional memory.
source_title: Subspace Optimization for Efficient Federated Learning under Heterogeneous Data

summary: FedSLoP samples a shared low-rank Stiefel subspace each federated round and projects local gradients and momentum into it without restricting the model to low rank. The full-participation analysis resets momentum each round and establishes nonconvex stationarity bounds under smoothness and bounded variance. On non-IID MNIST, three-seed accuracy is 95.11% versus FedAvg-M's 95.51%. The reported one-seventh compression should not be read as verified communication savings: the algorithm and public implementation upload full-model deltas. More severe label-skew ablations use one seed, and learning rates are selected for FedSLoP then shared across baselines. Larger models and partial participation remain unvalidated.
source_title: FedSLoP: Memory-Efficient Federated Learning with Low-Rank Gradient Projection

summary: SUDA-Muon isolates the modular communication backbone of decentralized Muon inside a primal–dual template supporting ED/D², EXTRA, and gradient tracking, while identifying two non-modular constraints: tracking must precede polarization, and local-polarize-then-average cannot reproduce federated average-then-polarize speedup. Its nuclear-geometry rate separates leading optimization from topology terms; CIFAR-100 and GPT-2 experiments show comparable variants near IID data and clear gains over DeMuon on long-horizon non-IID training.
source_title: SUDA-Muon: Structural Design Principles and Boundaries for Fully Decentralized Muon

summary: RF-EXTRA replaces Stiefel retractions with an approximate gradient map and orthogonality-restoring penalty inside an EXTRA-style decentralized primal-dual recursion. A joint consensus-and-direction error analysis yields an inverse-iteration stationarity and feasibility bound with sufficiently small constant steps on connected undirected networks. Synthetic and MNIST PCA plus low-rank matrix completion show competitive communication efficiency against retraction-based and retraction-free baselines. Matched synthetic timings are close to REXTRA, with RF-EXTRA not faster in every setting. Guarantees require neighborhood-preserving initialization and penalty/stepsize conditions; empirical evidence concerns structured matrix problems, not full neural-network or language-model training. No verified official implementation is linked.
source_title: A Retraction-Free EXTRA Method for Decentralized Optimization on the Stiefel Manifold

summary: Layer-separation training introduces auxiliary hidden-output variables to replace deeply nested softmax cross-entropy optimization with neighboring-layer subproblems and alternating minimization, including closed-form least-squares updates. The separated objective upper-bounds the original loss, and suitable updates decrease it under specified conditions. Ten-seed experiments on synthetic binary classification, PDE-interface classification, and MNIST CNNs show lower training losses and more stable optimization in deeper networks. These are training metrics rather than established test-generalization gains. The proposed solvers run in MATLAB while gradient baselines use PyTorch, so raw runtime comparisons are intentionally not claimed; auxiliary-variable storage and scaling to modern residual or transformer architectures remain unresolved.
source_title: A Layer Separation Optimization Framework for Cross-Entropy Training in Deep Learning

optimizer: Online Newton with Nesterov Accelerated Sketching
summary: This online Newton variant averages sampled Hessians and approximates each Newton direction with a fixed number of Nesterov-accelerated sketch-and-project iterations. It targets streaming optimization with uncertainty quantification, avoiding a dense exact Newton solve while retaining quadratic-scale storage and arithmetic for fixed sketch budgets. The analysis accounts jointly for data noise and randomized computation, proving convergence, last-iterate asymptotic normality, and consistency of an online covariance estimator. Linear and logistic regression experiments compare accelerated and unaccelerated sketching, exact Newton, and SGD using estimation error and confidence-interval coverage. Guarantees require strong positive-curvature and moment assumptions; acceleration-parameter estimation introduces practical overhead beyond the nominal sketching cost.
source_title: Inference of Online Newton Methods with Nesterov's Accelerated Sketching

summary: BOOOM is a derivative-free optimizer for column-orthonormal matrices, including nonsmooth and black-box objectives. A global Givens-rotation representation preserves Stiefel feasibility exactly while recursive modified pattern search tests positive and negative plane rotations, accepts improving moves, and contracts search steps. The paper establishes angle-space/manifold equivalence, stationarity transfer, and probabilistic global convergence under additional restart assumptions. Experiments cover quadratic forms, low-rank/sparse decomposition, ICA, Varimax, joint diagonalization, reduced electronic-structure problems, and supervised PCA. Reported performance is competitive with specialized Riemannian solvers rather than uniformly superior. Each full sweep requires quadratically many objective evaluations in the ambient row dimension, so inexpensive or parallelizable objectives are important.
source_title: BOOOM: Loss-Function-Agnostic Black-Box Optimization over Orthonormal Manifolds for Machine Learning and Statistical Inference

summary: ZO-MGT combines two-query Rademacher forward differences, exponential momentum, and decentralized gradient tracking to stabilize derivative-free optimization under heterogeneous local objectives. Each node mixes parameters and trackers with neighbors, then corrects its tracker using the change in local momentum. Experiments simulate twenty agents on a9a sigmoid least-squares classification and compare stationarity, consensus, and runtime against two distributed zeroth-order baselines. The displayed constant-step theorem gives a decaying transient plus smoothing- and heterogeneity-dependent error floors, rather than unconditional exact convergence. Its graph, smoothness, momentum, and stepsize restrictions matter; proposed bitwise acceleration is not demonstrated by a dedicated hardware implementation or large-model experiment.
source_title: Distributed Zeroth-Order Optimization with Rademacher Perturbations and Momentum Gradient Tracking

summary: Par-S2ZPO partitions policy parameters across federated agents, assigns Rademacher perturbations to their blocks, and aggregates majority-voted binary preference feedback into sign-based zeroth-order update directions. It avoids backpropagation and transmitting dense local gradients, with convergence bounds exposing the trade-off among trajectory-batch size, agent count, and preference distinguishability. Four MuJoCo experiments with small pretrained neural policies outperform a FedAvg-style RLHF baseline under matched sampling budgets. The experimental implementation additionally uses server-side acceptance tests, rejection-triggered step reduction, and Adam after accepted updates. Feedback comes from simulated preference panels, not human annotators or LLM post-training, so practical large-language-model and privacy conclusions remain unverified.
source_title: Efficient Federated RLHF via Zeroth-Order Policy Optimization

summary: PRIME-SR adapts momentum in stochastic reconfiguration using effective spectral dimension and overlap between consecutive principal sample-space eigenspaces. It reuses SPRING's regularized natural-gradient solve while reducing reliance on a manually chosen momentum coefficient. Spin-lattice, atomic, and molecular variational-Monte-Carlo experiments reach energies comparable to well-tuned fixed-momentum SPRING, with improved stability across five electronic-system initializations. The convergence proof applies to fixed-momentum SPRING, not the proposed adaptive controller. Computing and retaining sample-space eigenvectors adds work and memory, and learning rate, regularization, and update-norm constraints remain prescribed. These specialized wavefunction-optimization results do not establish general neural-network or language-model training gains.
source_title: Momentum Stability and Adaptive Control in Stochastic Reconfiguration

summary: AdaLeZO allocates zeroth-order perturbations across layers using a nonstationary multi-armed-bandit strategy instead of uniformly perturbing all parameters. Count-aware inverse-probability weighting with replacement preserves unbiased gradient estimation while concentrating work on sensitive layers and reducing parameter-update overhead. Fine-tuning OPT and LLaMA models from 6.7B to 30B parameters reports 1.7–3.0-fold wall-clock acceleration across representative baselines; OPT-6.7B throughput rises from 4,501 to 7,728 tokens per second. The framework also composes with other ZO estimators. It still trails backpropagation on difficult tasks such as DROP, and evidence is limited to supervised NLP fine-tuning rather than multimodal training or RLHF.
source_title: Universally Empowering Zeroth-Order Optimization via Adaptive Layer-wise Sampling

summary: ADPREC unifies adaptively preconditioned vector and matrix blocks, covering AdaNorm, full and diagonal AdaGrad, and an adaptive Muon-like rule while allowing heterogeneous geometries and two momentum variants in one algorithmic framework. It proves fully stochastic nonconvex global rates without assuming bounded stochastic gradients or a sufficiently small fixed step. The contribution is theoretical: it includes no neural-network training study or systems evidence.
source_title: A unified convergence theory for adaptive first-order methods in the nonconvex case, including AdaNorm, full and diagonal AdaGrad and Muon

summary: Grasp uses self-bounding initial sampling to determine parameter-search ranges and runs base optimizers over the resulting grid, avoiding unverifiable prior bounds on smoothness or distance to a solution. Nonconvex and convex variants provide near-optimal stochastic guarantees up to logarithmic and ensemble terms, with acceleration and Hölder-smoothness adaptivity in the convex setting. CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 experiments compare whole-network training and frozen-feature linear learning under a fixed oracle budget; outcomes remain competitive with finely tuned bases. This is a budget-allocating search-and-selection framework, not a cost-free Adam replacement. Initial exploration and parallel candidates consume training budget, and a loss lower bound is still used.
source_title: Towards Fully Parameter-Free Stochastic Optimization: Grid Search with Self-Bounding Analysis

summary: FedMuon applies orthonormalized Muon momentum to periodic federated aggregation, obtaining nonconvex convergence and O(ε^-3) communication complexity without heterogeneity assumptions or transmitted control variates. The bounded search direction also makes its learning rate independent of problem constants and extends naturally to p-moment heavy-tailed noise without clipping; across ResNet-18, ViT, recurrent, transformer, image, and text workloads, FedMuon converges fastest and leads accuracy under both IID and Dirichlet-heterogeneous client splits.
source_title: On Provable Benefits of Muon in Federated Learning

summary: CLion uses Lion’s sign update only when every nonzero momentum coordinate exceeds a threshold, reverting to the raw momentum otherwise to avoid the instability and poor stability bound caused by tiny coordinates. Algorithmic-stability analysis improves Lion and signSGD’s gap-dependent bound to O(1/N) while retaining O(√d/T^1/4) nonconvex convergence; WikiText-2/103 Transformers and CIFAR-10/Tiny-ImageNet ResNets show lower test loss, perplexity, and generally higher accuracy than Lion and RLion.
source_title: CLion: Efficient Cautious Lion Optimizer with Enhanced Generalization

summary: This paper constructs Heavy-Ball and Nesterov acceleration in function space, then maps the resulting momentum back to parameter coordinates through tangent-space Gram systems.
