Exact natural momentum and cheaper quasi-natural or functional-difference variants avoid requiring explicit geodesic maps on a particular manifold. Small neural-network experiments cover Mackey–Glass regression, classification, and two physics-informed PDE tasks; on Mackey–Glass, natural momentum reaches the target error in less than half NGD's iterations and time. Gram solves, spectral regularization, clipping, and momentum choices remain necessary. The tested networks contain only five or ten hidden units, so the results do not establish large-model scalability.
source_title: Natural gradient descent with momentum

summary: StoSignSGD injects structured randomness into the sign operator while keeping the update unbiased, and supplies a conversion framework for constructing sign versions of general optimizers. It proves sharp convex and improved nonsmooth nonconvex guarantees, gives 1.44-2.14x speedups in FP8 pretraining, and improves FP4 OLMo2-370M downstream accuracy by 1.13 points over the strongest stable baseline. Large-scale pretraining stops at 370M, with separate 7B evidence limited to math fine-tuning.
source_title: StoSignSGD: Unbiased Structural Stochasticity Fixes SignSGD for Training Large Language Models

summary: Communication-Efficient Gluon compresses layerwise non-Euclidean LMO updates with either unbiased sparsification or contraction plus error feedback, using SARAH/PAGE-style gradient differences so compression noise vanishes; MVR variants weaken the required conditions and also yield a faster uncompressed Gluon. The theory supplies convergence and communication/oracle complexities under layerwise generalized smoothness, while a5a logistic regression and spectral-LMO CIFAR-10 training reduce normalized uplink cost by about 60% and 65% versus tuned momentum baselines.
source_title: Communication-Efficient Gluon in Federated Learning

summary: Muon² applies Adam-style second-moment scaling before Newton–Schulz orthogonalization, tightening the momentum spectrum and moving singular values out of the iteration’s dead zone; Muon²-F factorizes that state to retain Muon-like memory. Directional-alignment diagnostics show three steps already rival five-step Muon, and GPT, LLaMA, and MoE pretraining up to 13B parameters consistently improves perplexity with 40% fewer polar iterations and up to 25% less time to the same loss.
source_title: Muon$^2$: Boosting Muon via Adaptive Second-Moment Preconditioning

summary: MetaAdamW uses a small attention model over group-level gradient and momentum statistics to set learning rates and weight decay, trained by a meta-objective combining alignment, loss, and generalization signals. Across five tasks it reports up to 17.11% less total training time or 11.08% better performance. Tests use lightweight models; meta-steps raise peak memory to roughly 1.5-2x AdamW and increase total time by 27-173% on some tasks, so billion-scale practicality is unproven.
source_title: A Self-Attentive Meta-Optimizer with Group-Adaptive Learning Rates and Weight Decay

summary: APT diagnoses that EMA makes optimization-based multi-task learning amortize rather than immediately resolve task conflicts, while Muon’s spectral flattening can amplify a poor aggregated direction. It adapts momentum from adjacent-gradient cosine similarity and adds lightweight direction-preserving task gating before Muon; tracking-error theory links this control to a tighter Pareto-stationary neighborhood, and experiments on NYUv2, CityScapes, CelebA, and QM9 broadly improve CAGrad, FAMO, and FairGrad, with APT-Muon achieving leading scene-understanding results.
source_title: Delve into the Applicability of Advanced Optimizers for Multi-Task Learning

summary: Adam-HNAG uses variable/operator splitting and a curvature-aware gradient correction to uncouple Adam’s adaptive metric from Nesterov-style momentum, producing a dissipative continuous flow plus lagged and synchronous discretizations with an explicit Lyapunov function. For smooth convex full-batch objectives it gives the first Adam-type iterate convergence proof and a k^-2 accelerated regime; quadratic, logistic-regression, and Reddi-counterexample experiments support the predicted contraction, with the lagged variant remaining stable where Adam and the synchronous variant drift.
source_title: Adam-HNAG: A Convergent Reformulation of Adam with Accelerated Rate

summary: SAGE combines a Lion-style sign direction with an O(d) adaptive scale bounded by one, acting as a memory-light damper for sparse, high-variance embedding gradients. Used in a Sinkhorn-style hybrid, it replaces the AdamW embedding fallback and reports the best perplexity among tested baselines on Llama models up to 1.3B while reducing optimizer-state memory. The abstract gives no common absolute effect size and pretraining evidence stops at 1.3B.
source_title: SAGE: Sign-Adaptive Gradient for Memory-Efficient LLM Optimization

summary: FlowAdam detects difficult coupled geometry with EMA statistics, switches to clipped ODE gradient-flow integration, and softly blends the resulting velocity into Adam momentum to avoid transition collapse. It reduces held-out error by 10-22% on low-rank matrix and tensor recovery and by 6% on Jester while matching Adam on CIFAR-10; hard momentum replacement drops one ablation from 100% to 82.5% accuracy. Benefits are concentrated in coupled-parameter problems and the ODE integration adds work.
source_title: FlowAdam: Implicit Regularization via Geometry-Aware Soft Momentum Injection

summary: LSRTR-M retains low-separation-rank tensor GLM block coordinate descent but replaces repeated QR projection of orthonormal factor matrices with Muon momentum and Newton–Schulz updates, directly targeting the original solver’s main bottleneck. Across synthetic linear, logistic, and Poisson tensor regressions it converges faster in iterations and wall time with lower estimation and prediction error; on Vessel MNIST 3D it trains faster while matching or improving classification metrics.
source_title: A Muon-Accelerated Algorithm for Low Separation Rank Tensor Generalized Linear Models

summary: This theoretical work lifts normalized matrix descent to mean-field probability measures through Spectral Wasserstein distances: trace geometry recovers W2, operator geometry models idealized Muon, and Schatten gauges interpolate between them. It develops Kantorovich and robust max–min costs, Gaussian/Bures reductions, and a Benamou–Brenier equivalence with geodesics for monotone norms, then identifies the normalized continuity equation as the metric gradient flow; MMD, Gaussian, two-layer ReLU, and shallow-attention simulations illustrate the construction.
source_title: Muon Dynamics as a Spectral Wasserstein Flow

summary: SIFT treats constrained model steering as spectral subspace interference: it derives a one-shot orthogonalized model-merging solution, connects that solution to Muon’s matrix-sign gradient update, and localizes intervention to selected layers and steps. This makes objective–constraint tradeoffs controllable rather than globally suppressing updates; across Zephyr/LLaMA unlearning and safety, GLM-4-Voice adaptation, and RAGTruth mitigation, SIFT consistently beats control-based and control-free baselines, including a 32.7% hallucination rate versus Muon’s 38.5%.
source_title: Subspace Control: Turning Constrained Model Steering into Controllable Spectral Optimization

summary: FaSO explains Muon’s long-tail benefit as equalizing update strength across positive-curvature modes, reducing the dominance of sharp tail-class directions, then avoids paying for orthogonalization throughout training. Its normalized-time probabilistic schedule uses cheap SGD early and increasingly frequent Muon steps near convergence; CIFAR/ImageNet long-tailed benchmarks match or approach Muon’s accuracy with over 50% less overhead, improve few-class generalization across standard rebalancing losses, and reach flatter tail minima than SGD.
source_title: Fast Sharpness-escaping Optimization for Long-tailed Learning

summary: Sven preserves per-example residual structure and applies a truncated-SVD pseudoinverse of the loss Jacobian, yielding a minimum-norm update that generalizes natural gradient beyond likelihood losses. Small regression MLPs converge faster and to lower loss than Adam while approaching L-BFGS quality at much lower wall time. Its cost is roughly rank times SGD, batch-conditioned Jacobians can consume substantial memory, classification gains are smaller, and large convolutional or Transformer models are not tested.
source_title: Sven: Singular Value Descent as a Computationally Efficient Natural Gradient Method

summary: Newton–Muon derives a triplet quadratic surrogate using the gradient, output-space curvature, and layer-input matrix, revealing standard Muon as a Newton-type step that omits right preconditioning by the activation second moment. It applies the matrix sign to G(ZZᵀ)^-1 and approximates the inverse efficiently; on a Modded-NanoGPT GPT-2 speedrun it reaches target validation loss in 6% fewer steps and over 4% less wall time, with direction diagnostics consistently favoring its update over Muon.
source_title: The Newton-Muon Optimizer

summary: MuonEq rebalances momentum with transient row/column norm equilibration before finite-step Newton–Schulz, unlike post-orthogonalization rescaling or persistent Shampoo-style whitening; its row-only default adds no optimizer state. Analysis links polar-approximation quality to stable rank and conditioning, treats equilibration as zeroth-order whitening, and retains Õ(T^-1/4) nonconvex stationarity with weight decay and inexact NS5; LLaMA2 130M–1B C4 runs consistently improve loss, perplexity, and hyperparameter robustness over Muon.
source_title: MuonEq: Balancing Before Orthogonalization with Lightweight Equilibration

summary: HyperP derives learning-rate transfer laws for Muon on a fixed Frobenius hypersphere across width, depth, token budget, and MoE granularity, proving weight decay is first-order inert and retaining Depth-µP plus the 0.32 data-scaling exponent. One base rate transfers from 208M active parameters through 6×10²¹ FLOPs with 1.58× compute efficiency over a strong Muon baseline; bounded stability metrics, SqrtGate’s RMS-preserving MoE scaling, and stronger load balancing validate transferable stability through 13.3B total parameters.
source_title: Rethinking Language Model Scaling under Transferable Hypersphere Optimization

summary: Moving beyond prior orthogonal-embedding analyses, this paper studies Gaussian superposition in power-law associative memory and proves one Muon step recovers Θ̃(min{d^(1+1/(2α)), B^(1/α)}) items, matching Newton versus SGD’s Θ̃(min{d^(1/(2α)), B^(1/α)}). Its thresholded multi-step theory says Muon’s gain is early because both methods eventually approach information-theoretic d² capacity; synthetic scaling experiments and a two-layer transformer induction-head task validate the capacity exponents, larger critical-batch regime, and early recall advantage.
source_title: Sharp Capacity Scaling of Spectral Optimizers in Learning Associative Memory

summary: NucGD is a nuclear-norm-constrained normalized steepest-descent method designed to induce low-rank structure, with an asynchronous power-iteration update that avoids a full SVD. The paper connects its geometry to maximum-margin implicit bias and studies how minibatch noise and momentum alter the selected solution. Evaluation centers on multiclass separable data and implicit-bias diagnostics rather than general large-model training.
source_title: Towards The Implicit Bias on Multiclass Separable Data Under Norm Constraints

summary: CurvZO infers coordinate-wise curvature online from scalar zeroth-order feedback, uses it to sample informative parameters, and adapts the perturbation budget as the curvature distribution changes. Across OPT and Llama fine-tuning tasks it improves accuracy by up to 4.4 points and training speed by up to 2x over zeroth-order baselines while preserving their memory advantage. Results cover fine-tuning rather than pretraining and remain tied to the evaluated models and tasks.
source_title: CurvZO: Adaptive Curvature-Guided Sparse Zeroth-Order Optimization for Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning

summary: Embedding practical momentum and decoupled weight decay into Lion-K, the paper identifies Muon as nuclear-norm Lion-K and shows it implicitly optimizes inside the spectral ball ||W||₂≤1/λ, not merely taking spectral steepest-descent steps. Discrete Lyapunov analysis proves deterministic and stochastic convergence to KKT points; toy problems plus ResNet-18/50, ViT-B/16, Qwen-100M, and LLaMA-300M/500M experiments show singular values enter the predicted constraint and remain regularized unlike AdamW.
source_title: Muon Optimizes Under Spectral Norm Constraints

summary: RMNP replaces Muon’s five matrix-multiplication Newton–Schulz passes with rowwise ℓ2 normalization, motivated by Transformer Hessian block-diagonal dominance and empirical asymptotic equivalence of the two preconditioners. It cuts operator complexity to O(mn) and retains minimax-optimal nonconvex guarantees; GPT-2 125M–1.5B and LLaMA 60M–1B runs match or beat Muon and AdamW, while preconditioning is 13–44× faster, including 42.9× at 1.5B.
source_title: RMNP: Row-Momentum Normalized Preconditioning for Scalable Matrix-Based Optimization

summary: MUD substitutes Muon’s symmetric polar whitening with one or a few triangular Gram–Schmidt/Gauss–Seidel-like solves, making row-orthonormal matrices fixed points and admitting local quadratic convergence while using roughly one-twelfth the FLOPs per pass. Across GPT-2 124M–775M on three corpora and three GPU platforms, it improves time-to-perplexity by 10–50% and Muon throughput by 1.3–2.6×, nearly 3× once; ESM-2 150M reaches Muon quality substantially sooner.
source_title: Beyond Muon: MUD (MomentUm Decorrelation) for Faster Transformer Training

summary: Rather than fitting empirical laws or analyzing quadratics and SDEs, the paper minimizes a recent LMO convergence bound covering normalized SGD, SignSGD/Adam proxies, and Muon to derive token-budget schedules. Fixed momentum gives b*∝T^1/2 and η*∝T^-1/4, fixed batch requires 1−β∝bT^-1/2, while joint tuning yields b*∝T^1/6, η*∝T^-7/12, and 1−β∝T^-1/3; a 160M SlimPajama sweep qualitatively confirms predicted learning-rate shifts.
source_title: Deriving Hyperparameter Scaling Laws via Modern Optimization Theory

summary: Extending Muon theory beyond Lipschitz smoothness and bounded variance, this paper analyzes nonconvex Hölder-smooth empirical risk under bounded p-th-moment noise for p∈(1,2], including heavy tails, without gradient clipping. For diminishing ηt∝(t+1)^−a and suitable batch growth, both momentum and non-momentum Muon converge almost surely; its expected gradient-norm bound scales as O(T^(−(1−a))), versus O(T^(−(1−a)/2)) for mini-batch SGD under the paper’s respective stationarity measures.
source_title: Muon Converges under Heavy-Tailed Noise: Nonconvex Hölder-Smooth Empirical Risk Minimization

summary: SPECTRA wraps coordinatewise optimizers with post-spectral clipping of updates and optional pre-clipping of gradient spikes, using a soft Newton–Schulz implementation instead of SVD. Post-clipping is proved equivalent to composite Frank–Wolfe under a spectral constraint with implicit weight regularization, while spike analysis explains its advantage over global clipping; FineWeb-Edu LLaMA runs from 160M to 820M improve AdamW, Signum, MARS, and AdEMAMix uniformly, with about 2% post-clipping overhead and stronger downstream averages.
source_title: Enhancing LLM Training via Spectral Clipping

summary: This item-wise sharpness-aware optimizer scales its penalty by item frequency so rare recommendation items receive finer protection without paying the full two-pass SAM cost everywhere. Across three datasets it reports average overall NDCG@10 and HR@10 gains of 3.53% and 4.54% over the strongest baseline, tail gains of 8.90% and 8.44%, and only 5.3% extra time per epoch versus SAM. Evidence is specific to long-tailed LLM recommender systems.
source_title: Taming the Long Tail: Efficient Item-wise Sharpness-Aware Minimization for LLM-based Recommender Systems

summary: ZO-SAM replaces SAM's inner perturbation gradient with a zeroth-order estimate, retaining one backpropagation while targeting flat minima during sparse training. On ResNet-32 it improves CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 accuracy by up to 2.31 and 2.54 points, and on DeiT/ImageNet by up to 1.17 points; selected CIFAR-10 runs reach 90% accuracy substantially earlier than SGD. The evidence is limited to sparse computer-vision models and no public implementation is linked.
source_title: ZO-SAM: Zero-Order Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Efficient Sparse Training

summary: HTMuon replaces Muon’s all-ones update spectrum by raising momentum singular values to p∈(0,1), preserving matrix coupling while downweighting noisy trailing directions and inducing heavier-tailed weight spectra. It is Schatten-q steepest descent with O(ε^-4) nonconvex sample complexity; tuned LLaMA C4 runs reduce Muon perplexity by 0.92/0.98 at 60M/135M, GPT-2 and image models also improve, and interval or Newton–Schulz approximations retain gains up to LLaMA-1B.
source_title: HTMuon: Improving Muon via Heavy-Tailed Spectral Correction

summary: Mousse first whitens momentum with Shampoo’s Kronecker curvature statistics, applies Muon’s polar step in that basis, then unwhitens—an anisotropic spectral trust region that corrects Muon’s isotropic geometry without SOAP’s Adam second-moment state. Trace normalization, milder spectral tempering, and grafting stabilize the method; 160M–800M FineWeb runs give the lowest validation loss across scales, reaching Muon’s 800M loss in about 12% fewer steps for only 3% wall-clock overhead.
source_title: Mousse: Rectifying the Geometry of Muon with Curvature-Aware Preconditioning

summary: By replacing ordinary p-to-q matrix norms with mean-normalized operator norms, this work makes layerwise geometry composable and derives width-aware learning-rate scalings that recover μP for Adam/SignSGD while covering row and column normalization. It shows Muon can incur O(√w) worst-case smoothness, whereas row-normalized MOGA has width-independent bounds; GPT-2 models from 124M to 1.5B transfer one peak learning rate, and long-budget GPT-2/LLaMA runs match or beat Muon.
source_title: On the Width Scaling of Neural Optimizers Under Matrix Operator Norms I: Row/Column Normalization and Hyperparameter Transfer

summary: OptEMA uses a corrected AdaGrad-Norm controller to adapt the decay of first- or second-moment exponential averages, producing OptEMA-M and OptEMA-V without requiring the gradient-noise level. The analysis gives a unified near-optimal stochastic rate and automatically recovers the faster zero-noise regime. The paper is theory-only and relies on unbiased-oracle, variance, and average-smoothness assumptions rather than neural-network experiments.
source_title: OptEMA: Adaptive Exponential Moving Average for Stochastic Optimization with Zero-Noise Optimality

summary: This paper gives convergence bounds for Muon in four practical configurations spanning Nesterov momentum and weight decay, extending prior analyses to the commonly deployed combination. Weight decay is shown to ensure almost-sure bounded parameters and gradients without a bounded-gradient assumption; the derived critical-batch-size lower bound predicts qualitative dependence on momentum β and decay λ, which image-classification and language-modeling experiments validate rather than claiming an absolute batch-size estimate.
source_title: Convergence Bound and Critical Batch Size of Muon Optimizer

summary: NuMuon turns Muon’s spectral-ball linear minimization oracle into an intersection with a nuclear-norm budget, whose closed-form solution keeps equal-magnitude top-k momentum singular directions and explicitly controls update rank; a tail-energy-dependent theorem extends Muon’s nonconvex stationarity bound. On 0.6B–1.8B LLMs it sacrifices some uncompressed perplexity but, across ASVD, SVD-LLM, and Dobi-SVD at 40–80% compression, improves downstream averages by 4.2–55.8% and sharply lowers perplexity.
source_title: NuMuon: Nuclear-Norm-Constrained Muon for Compressible LLM Training

summary: Eight-bit Muon blockwise-quantizes its momentum state and, unlike 8-bit AdamW, needs only simple linear quantization: the paper proves bounded per-step error depending on the momentum matrix’s smallest singular value, while AdamW’s quantized second-moment denominator can yield unbounded error. Chinchilla-optimal GPT pretraining through 2.7B parameters and Alpaca instruction tuning match FP32 Muon, cutting optimizer-state memory 62%; quantizing auxiliary AdamW states reaches 75% savings with at most 0.5% higher validation loss.
source_title: On quantizing the state of the Muon optimizer

summary: MuonRec ports Muon to recommendation through a hybrid recipe—Newton–Schulz-orthogonalized momentum for hidden 2-D matrices, Adam for embeddings, heads, norms, and biases—rather than changing model architecture. Across GRU4Rec, Caser, SASRec, TIGER, and 0.5B–3B MiniOneRec on two Amazon datasets, optimizer-specific sweeps yield 32.4% fewer convergence steps and 12.6% higher NDCG@10 on average; TIGER needs roughly one-third the steps, while 1.5B MiniOneRec saves 27–30%.
source_title: MuonRec: Shifting the Optimizer Paradigm Beyond Adam in Scalable Generative Recommendation

summary: Rather than treating Muon’s speed as unconditionally beneficial, this paper shows spectral orthogonalization avoids gradient descent’s saddle-to-saddle curriculum by learning principal components and attention heads simultaneously, thereby removing a dynamical simplicity bias. Controlled MNIST, multimodal-routing, and two-layer transformer cycle tasks show the consequence: depending on feature strength Muon can favor spurious cues, and despite fitting training data it fails unseen source pairs or skips that SGD solves through shared low-rank representations.
source_title: To Use or not to Use Muon: How Simplicity Bias in Optimizers Matters

summary: LoRA-Pre recasts EMA momentum as online linear regression and factorizes its solution into two learned rank-r factors, updating the subspace every step instead of periodically projecting gradients; it compresses first and second moments and plugs into Adam or Muon. On C4 LLaMA pretraining from 60M to 1B it is the best or second-best efficient method, matching GaLore at 8–16× lower rank, while MetaMath tuning lifts average LLaMA-3.1-8B and LLaMA-2-7B scores from LoRA’s 43.91/25.98 to 47.05/32.15.
source_title: Taming Momentum: Rethinking Optimizer States Through Low-Rank Approximation

summary: LITE views preconditioners as Riemannian geometry and momentum as Riemannian damping, then uses gradient-covariance eigenspaces to identify sharp directions and selectively raises learning rate and Hessian damping in the flat complement; specializations add two parallel Newton–Schulz calls to Muon or masks to SOAP. Theory tightens flat-manifold gradient bounds with both gains, while 130M–1.3B dense and 1B MoE pretraining lowers loss, delivers about 2× long-horizon speedup, and costs only about 1% in Muon throughput.
source_title: Accelerating LLM Pre-Training through Flat-Direction Dynamics Enhancement

summary: FlashOptim preserves optimizer equations while compressing storage: it represents each FP32 master weight as BF16 plus an 8-bit ULP-scaled residual, compands momentum and variance before groupwise 8-bit quantization, stores BF16 gradients, and fuses reconstruction, update, and recompression in Triton. AdamW falls from 16 to 7 bytes per parameter, or 5 with gradient release; ResNet-50, GPT-2-124M, and LLaMA-3.1-8B match baseline quality, with LLaMA fine-tuning peak memory dropping from 175.2 to 112.9 GiB without slower steps.
source_title: FlashOptim: Optimizers for Memory-Efficient Training

summary: MUON+ identifies post-polar imbalance: finite Newton–Schulz steps can amplify row or column norm variance, and a blockwise descent bound links that variance to curvature-weighted second-order cost and smaller stable steps. A single post-polar row/column normalization adds no state; across GPT and LLaMA models from 60M to 7B and token-to-parameter ratios near 200, it lowers perplexity by up to 2.02, raises seven-task accuracy 1.3 points, and reaches Muon’s target loss up to 37.1% faster.
source_title: MUON+: Towards More Effective Muon via One Additional Normalization Step for LLM Pre-training

summary: Replacing tensor-program derivations with tractable spectral-norm conditions on each optimizer’s update map, this paper extends μP scaling rules to AdamW, ADOPT, LAMB, Sophia, Shampoo, and Muon. NanoGPT and Llama-2 width sweeps exhibit stable features and zero-shot optimal-learning-rate transfer, but the analysis fixes batch size across widths and preliminary depth-scaling experiments do not consistently transfer learning rates.
source_title: Extending $μ$P: Spectral Conditions for Feature Learning Across Optimizers

summary: NAMO adds an Adam-like norm-adaptive scalar to Muon’s orthogonalized momentum, preserving orthogonality, while NAMO-D uses clamped columnwise scaling for neuron-level noise adaptation. Both reach O(T^-1/2) deterministic stationarity and O(T^-1/4) stochastically with sufficiently growing batches; on GPT-2 124M/355M, NAMO-D lowers validation loss to 3.0246/2.9507 versus Muon’s 3.0435/2.9684, but evaluation is small-scale and NAMO-D introduces a tuned clamping hyperparameter.
source_title: Adam Improves Muon: Adaptive Moment Estimation with Orthogonalized Momentum

summary: ZO-Muon combines lazily sampled low-rank zeroth-order projections with multi-query averaging and Muon-style orthogonalization; its lossless-top-subspace proposition explains the method as a zeroth-order low-rank Muon approximation. Across LLaMA-3-8B/OPT-13B and ViT-B/L fine-tuning, it uses 24.7% of MeZO’s SST-2 queries and gains 25.1 points on ViT-L CIFAR-100, but performance is rank-sensitive and full pretraining remains untested.
source_title: Powering Up Zeroth-Order Training via Subspace Gradient Orthogonalization

summary: SpecMuon decomposes each matrix gradient into dominant singular modes and applies a relaxed scalar-auxiliary-variable controller per mode, adding loss-energy damping to Muon’s scale-balanced geometry. It proves modified-energy dissipation and linear convergence under a PL condition; Burgers PINN loss drops from Muon’s 3.39e-4 to 1.55e-4 and DeepONet/fPINN tests also improve accuracy, but spectral bookkeeping costs 21–68% more time and stochastic training plus automatic rank selection remain open.
source_title: Muon with Spectral Guidance: Efficient Optimization for Scientific Machine Learning

summary: Casting momentum methods as approximate steepest-descent trajectories, this paper proves that decaying-learning-rate Muon, MomentumGD, Signum, Adam without its stability constant, and Muon-Adam converge directionally to KKT points of optimizer-specific max-margin problems on smooth homogeneous models. MNIST and CIFAR-10 networks maximize the predicted spectral, ℓ2, ℓ∞, or hybrid margins; the theory assumes directional convergence, and extending it to nonsmooth ReLU models without strong trajectory assumptions remains open.
source_title: The Implicit Bias of Adam and Muon on Smooth Homogeneous Neural Networks

summary: Magma keeps adaptive moments dense but Bernoulli-masks whole parameter-block updates, then damps survivors when gradient–momentum cosine alignment is weak; a Taylor expansion identifies the masking noise as a block-curvature regularizer. On 60M–1B Llama C4, RMSProp+Magma reaches 13.19 perplexity versus Muon’s 14.52 and Adam’s 16.35, with MoE and heavy-tail tests supporting the mechanism; however, Magma is biased, unbiased variants were unstable, and gains do not extend to ResNet-like geometry.
source_title: On Surprising Effectiveness of Masking Updates in Adaptive Optimizers

summary: TrasMuon retains a Newton–Schulz/NorMuon mixing direction but calibrates its global RMS and multiplicatively damps columns whose momentum energy exceeds a robust median-based trust region, with effective-time smoothing. In a fixed-hyperparameter Qwen3-0.6B pilot it reaches loss 7 in 80 versus Muon’s 140 steps, or 48 versus 83 without warmup, and burst/ViT/PINN tests reduce spikes; results add many tuning knobs, target 2D matrices, and lack broad language-model multi-seed sweeps.
source_title: TrasMuon: Trust-Region Adaptive Scaling for Orthogonalized Momentum Optimizers

summary: On strongly convex quadratics, this paper shows exact-polar Muon with a fixed step confines singular values to a lattice, creating an O(α²) loss floor, while relative speed versus GD flips across Hessian spectra with identical condition numbers. Moderate projection error can break confinement—Newton–Schulz beats exact projection on 94% of min-spiked runs—and greedy one-step superiority can still lose globally; these cautionary results are restricted to synthetic quadratics, not neural training.
source_title: Insights on Muon from Simple Quadratics

summary: For norm-induced stochastic steepest descent, this paper proves that no-momentum worst-case max-margin guarantees collapse to full batches, whereas momentum recovers an approximate bias through a batch–momentum tradeoff and variance reduction recovers the exact full-batch bias at slower rates; a two-sample counterexample and batch-one construction show genuinely different biases. Synthetic multiclass and MNIST tests agree, but the main theory covers separable linear classifiers and special sampling/data structures rather than practical deep Muon.
source_title: The Implicit Bias of Steepest Descent with Mini-batch Stochastic Gradient

summary: Shampoo’s matrix update is decomposed into left/right adaptation around Muon’s polar factor, motivating the view that it relaxes instantaneous spectral descent into time-averaged semi-orthogonality across stochastic batches and the parameter trajectory. Tuned 320M–1.5B C4 Llamas show Shampoo matching or beating exact-SVD Muon, with KL-Shampoo at 24.95 versus 25.68 perplexity; the study ignores practical preconditioner overhead and is limited to dense Llama, one dataset, and fixed schedules.
source_title: Clarifying Shampoo: Adapting Spectral Descent to Stochasticity and the Parameter Trajectory

summary: An admissible-smoothing framework for operator-norm online matrix learning replaces one-sided Shampoo’s quadratic projection with Gaussian FTPL or deterministic hyperbolic FAML, retaining its adaptive regret up to constants with closed-form matrix operations. Online-to-nonconvex conversion yields Pion and Leon, which reach Goldstein-style (ρ,ε)-stationarity where Muon’s equivalent follow-the-leader update lacks nonsmooth guarantees; only discontinuous synthetic matrix sensing is tested, so deep-learning quality and the new polar/inverse-root costs remain unestablished.
source_title: Adaptive Matrix Online Learning through Smoothing with Guarantees for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization

summary: TSR-Adam all-reduces only the two-sided core UᵀGV, keeps Adam moments in r×r space, reconstructs updates locally, and refreshes bases through communicated randomized-SVD sketches, extending the scheme to embeddings. C4 Llamas average 13× fewer bytes per step and GLUE uses 25× less communication than Adam, but 1B loss is 3.08 versus 2.74 and theory covers a simplified momentum update with rank-dependent approximation floors and refresh sensitivity, not full Adam.
source_title: From $O(mn)$ to $O(r^2)$: Two-Sided Low-Rank Communication for Adam in Distributed Training with Memory Efficiency

summary: Under a generalized finite-p-moment noise model whose scale can grow with the gradient, this paper derives sharp O(T^{-(p−1)/(3p−2)}) rates for SignSGD, Lion, Muon, and Muonlight using new non-Euclidean martingale concentration bounds—the first matrix-sign analysis for p<2. NanoGPT-124M C4 measurements support the model and report 1.07×/1.32× Lion/Muonlight speedups over AdamW, but evidence is one fixed-hyperparameter setup and guarantees rely on generalized-smoothness and structured heavy-tail assumptions.
source_title: Sign-Based Optimizers Are Effective Under Heavy-Tailed Noise

summary: DeVA factorizes preconditioned descent into a variance-adaptation matrix and a scale-invariant sign or matrix-sign direction; its spectral variant estimates expected singular-value products in Shampoo’s rotating eigenbasis, giving Adam-like reliability scaling to Muon. A block-smooth analysis shows reduced weighted curvature, and 274M FineWeb validation loss improves from Muon’s 3.305 to 3.271; however, runtime rises 54%, while theory removes momentum, assumes bounded predictable scaling, and uses batch size proportional to the horizon.
source_title: Decoupling Variance and Scale-Invariant Updates in Adaptive Gradient Descent for Unified Vector and Matrix Optimization

summary: Although Muon orthogonalizes LoRA factors separately, this paper observes nearly parallel product-spectrum growth on RoBERTa and Llama-3.2-1B, then proves for continuous-time spectral gradient flow on squared matrix factorization that active square-root singular modes grow at equal rates and smaller targets finish first. Regularization yields almost-sure global convergence, but unregularized factor norms may diverge, discrete-time Muon is not covered, and uniform growth can amplify unnecessary modes when the desired rank is lower.
source_title: Uniform Spectral Growth and Convergence of Muon in LoRA-Style Matrix Factorization

summary: ADana lets AdamW’s first- and second-moment horizons grow logarithmically, pairs them with t^-1 weight decay, and damps Nesterov momentum as (1+t)^(1-κ) to control stochastic instability. FineWeb transformer ladders from 45M to 2.6B parameters show up to 40% compute-efficiency improvement over tuned AdamW and about 10% from log-time decay alone; experiments emphasize batch 32, larger-batch scaling is preliminary, and the LLM-optimal κ lacks a full explanation.
source_title: Logarithmic-time Schedules for Scaling Language Models with Momentum

summary: In a linear softmax associative-memory model with hierarchical frequencies, Muon’s matrix-sign update implicitly aligns to task representations and equalizes learning across groups, yielding exponential noiseless acceleration and a noisy power-law excess-loss rate of O~(T^-2) versus GD’s lower bound Ω~(T^{-(1-1/β)}). Imbalanced-MNIST tests and 100M-parameter LLaMA pretraining show a steeper fitted slope, -1.13 versus -0.66, but theory assumes orthogonal embeddings, zero initialization, no momentum, and a linear model.
source_title: Muon in Associative Memory Learning: Training Dynamics and Scaling Laws

summary: Assuming curvature falls polynomially with the suboptimality gap, this paper derives an LMO learning rate η=Δ/K(Δ) that rises then decays while retaining O(1/T) deterministic convergence, and turns it into a loss-driven scheduler that selects its warmup endpoint once. Across 124M/210M FineWeb Llamas with Muon, Lion, or normSGD and Swin-B ImageNet, it matches or beats manual sweeps; it still requires a target-loss estimate, and theory assumes star-convexity and boundedness, with stochastic guarantees only for Euclidean normalized SGD.
source_title: Where Does Warm-Up Come From? Adaptive Scheduling for Norm-Constrained Optimizers

summary: Canzona decouples logical optimizer ownership from physical sharding: α-balanced whole-parameter partitioning preserves ZeRO-1 bucket geometry for communication-free data-parallel updates, while asynchronous micro-group scheduling reconstructs tensor-parallel fragments with fused All-to-All. On Qwen3 1.7B–32B over 256 GPUs it reduces optimizer latency 5.8× and iteration time 1.57× while matching loss; evaluation centers on Megatron/ZeRO-1, and hybrid FSDP ZeRO-2/3 would require costly cross-dimensional reconstruction and more engineering.
source_title: Canzona: A Unified, Asynchronous, and Load-Balanced Framework for Distributed Matrix-based Optimizers

summary: A unified UΣ^pVᵀ family places Muon at p=0, raw gradients at p=1, and computes p=1/2 or p=1/4 variants through coupled Newton–Schulz iterations without SVD. In controlled 124M GPT-2/OpenWebText training, RMS-normalized variants are consistently stronger and AdamS reaches 2.870 validation loss versus Muon’s 2.887; the study omits weight decay and auxiliary stabilizers, tests one model/data setting, and fractional iterations add nontrivial overhead.
source_title: Delving into Muon and Beyond: Deep Analysis and Extensions

summary: Non-Euclidean GNS derives critical-batch metrics from ℓ∞/spectral steepest-descent geometry—using ℓ1 gradient variance for sign methods and S1/nuclear-norm row covariance for spectral methods—rather than reusing SGD’s Euclidean noise scale, and estimates them from per-rank DDP gradients. On 160M Llama, adaptive batches match small-batch loss while cutting Signum/Muon steps by about 66%; however, theory targets stateless sign/specSGD and extending it cleanly to momentum, mixed optimizers, and general Hessians remains open.
source_title: Adaptive Batch Sizes Using Non-Euclidean Gradient Noise Scales for Stochastic Sign and Spectral Descent

summary: PRISM augments Muon momentum with innovation G−M before polar decomposition, producing a low-rank covariance proxy that damps low-SNR directions instead of whitening every singular direction equally, with no extra persistent state. On a 22M Qwen2-style model trained for 2.6B FineWeb-Edu tokens, it improves loss from 3.285 to 3.266 and remains stable where Muon diverges; evaluation is one small setup and lacks a convergence theorem.
source_title: PRISM: Structured Optimization via Anisotropic Spectral Shaping

summary: OLion applies Lion-style two-timescale momentum, Newton–Schulz orthogonalization, then entrywise sign, approximating a maximal update over the intersection of spectral and ℓ∞ constraints instead of choosing Muon’s global or Lion’s coordinate geometry alone. It proves O(T^-1/2) deterministic stationarity under diagonal-isotropy and dense-polar assumptions and outperforms AdamW, Lion, and Muon from GPT-2 to Llama-2-7B, SiT, and SFT; the theory omits practical momentum and stochasticity and depends on restrictive spectral structure.
source_title: OLion: Approaching the Hadamard Ideal by Intersecting Spectral and $\ell_{\infty}$ Implicit Biases

summary: Mano projects momentum onto the tangent space of normalized weights and alternates row- and column-wise Oblique-manifold normalization, preserving spectral ordering without AdamW’s second moment or Muon’s Newton–Schulz whitening. Across LLaMA/Qwen models up to 1.7B it lowers final perplexity and reaches matched loss up to 1.75× faster than Muon with momentum-level state; its convergence proof removes momentum and rotation, and compute limits prevented larger-model overtraining and broad hyperparameter tests.
source_title: Mano: Restriking Manifold Optimization for LLM Training

summary: Spectra warm-starts a rank-1.5% power iteration to identify the persistent gradient spike, shrinks only that subspace toward the tail RMS, and leaves the noisy tail unchanged, unlike AdamW’s spike-dominated second moment or Muon’s full spectral flattening. On LLaMA3-8B over 50B tokens it beats both in loss and downstream accuracy while using 49.25% less optimizer-state memory than AdamW; the design assumes an empirical fixed spike ratio, and its local PSD-Hessian bound is not an optimizer convergence proof.
source_title: Spectra: Rethinking Optimizers for LLMs Under Spectral Anisotropy

summary: In an anisotropic phase-retrieval model, this work reduces GD and spectral gradient descent to signal, spurious-spike, and bulk dynamics, showing polar normalization acts like sign updates in an adaptive basis: SpecGD grows components uniformly and avoids GD’s multiplicative nuisance-spike amplification. Theorems yield dimension-independent Stage I and faster alignment, supported by power-law covariance and spiked MNIST experiments; conclusions are mainly for population dynamics on a special invariant manifold, leaving online noise, general covariance, and richer nonlinear models open.
source_title: Spectral Gradient Descent Mitigates Anisotropy-Driven Misalignment: A Case Study in Phase Retrieval

summary: TEON stacks same-type gradients from adjacent Transformer layers into a third-order tensor, matricizes and orthogonalizes it jointly, capturing cross-layer singular-vector correlations that layerwise Muon ignores. Norm comparison gives up to a √K better convergence bound when leading singular vectors align, and GPT/LLaMA runs from 60M to 1B consistently lower perplexity; the best-case theory assumes near-shared low-rank structure, while larger stacks or extreme aspect ratios degrade approximate orthogonalization and require grouping choices.
source_title: TEON: Tensorized Orthonormalization Beyond Layer-Wise Muon for Large Language Model Pre-Training

summary: FISMO alternates Kronecker Fisher-factor estimates, whitens gradients, orthogonalizes momentum in that geometry, then maps updates back, retaining curvature anisotropy that Muon discards while avoiding a full Fisher matrix. A trust-region derivation gives the closed-form structured polar step and the paper claims O(T^-1/2) nonconvex convergence; 124M GPT-2 and CIFAR-10 curves beat Muon and Shampoo, but no large-model, wall-clock, or memory study establishes that repeated inverse roots and factor updates are practical at scale.
source_title: FISMO: Fisher-Structured Momentum-Orthogonalized Optimizer

summary: MCSD applies a norm-specific linear minimization oracle to the Riemannian gradient in ambient space and projects once back to the manifold, avoiding Manifold Muon’s iterative tangent-space subproblem; SPEL specializes this to spectral LMOs and Stiefel matrix-sign projections. It proves O(T^-1/2) deterministic and O(T^-1/4) stochastic stationarity, wins CIFAR-100 accuracy and speeds PCA versus nested solvers, but costs two matrix-sign operations, trains slower than Muon on CNNs, and only matches StelLA in 8B adapter tuning.
source_title: Manifold constrained steepest descent

summary: PRISM fits one coefficient of each Newton–Schulz-like polynomial to the current residual spectrum through a small randomized sketch, adapting matrix-sign, root, inverse, and polar iterations without prior spectral bounds unlike fixed-range PolarExpress. It preserves quadratic worst-case convergence for degree one and improves Shampoo/CNN speed plus GPT-2 Muon validation loss from 5.4523 to 4.9886; guarantees do not cover the higher-degree practical variants, and neural tests are modest, including only 200M GPT tokens.
source_title: PRISM: Distribution-free Adaptive Computation of Matrix Functions for Accelerating Neural Network Training

summary: This paper closes the exact-SVD gap in Muon theory: finite-step Newton–Schulz reaches the same nonconvex nuclear-norm stationarity rate as ideal polar orthogonalization up to a factor that approaches one doubly exponentially with iteration count and improves with polynomial degree. CIFAR-10 and 124M–1.3B language-model ablations show two or three steps nearly match SVD while running faster; guarantees still assume standard smoothness and bounded variance.
source_title: Convergence of Muon with Newton-Schulz

summary: Using a direct descent-lemma analysis of Muon’s orthogonalized update, this theory paper covers Nesterov and non-Nesterov variants with constant, cosine, polynomial, or diminishing learning rates and fixed or growing batches under standard nonconvex assumptions. It improves prior O(T^-1/4)–O(T^-1/2) bounds to O(1/T) by coupling η=O(1/T) with b=O(T²) or exponential batch growth; however, it supplies no experiments and the fastest regimes require aggressive batch scaling.
source_title: Improved Convergence Rates of Muon Optimizer for Nonconvex Optimization

summary: 4-bit-Muon-GRASP diagnoses that Newton–Schulz amplifies quantization error concentrated in Muon momentum’s top singular subspace and row/column outliers, then stores warm-started low-rank factors in 8-bit while grid-quantizing the residual to 4-bit with two-axis scales. It cuts normalized error from 1.78 to 0.14 and training memory up to 28%, matching FP32 across 130M–1.1B pretraining and 7B tuning; pretraining stops at 1.1B and rank selection remains manual.
source_title: Achieving low-bit Muon through subspace preservation and grid quantization

summary: EF21-Muon extends error feedback to non-Euclidean linear-minimization-oracle optimizers, combining stochastic momentum with biased worker-to-server gradient compression and server-to-worker model compression so Muon, Scion, or Gluon never transmits dense messages. Its deterministic, stochastic, and layerwise theory covers smooth and (L0,L1)-smooth objectives while matching Euclidean rates; NanoGPT-124M reaches loss 3.31 with up to 7× less communication, but compression costs extra tokens, retaining only 5% degrades convergence, and evaluation remains small-scale.
source_title: Error Feedback for Muon and Friends

summary: This controlled benchmark replaces inherited recipes with per-optimizer coordinate-descent tuning across eleven methods, 130M–1.2B Llamas, and 1–8× Chinchilla budgets, showing that early-checkpoint rankings and shared hyperparameters can manufacture large gains. Matrix preconditioners remain best, but Muon and SOAP speedups over tuned AdamW shrink from about 1.4× at 130M to 1.1× at 1.2B, and SOAP or Kron overtake Muon at high data ratios; models above 1.2B are not tested.
source_title: Fantastic Pretraining Optimizers and Where to Find Them

summary: FedMuon shows that simply placing Muon inside FedAvg can stagnate under heterogeneous clients because the nonlinear linear-minimization oracle is biased, then applies SCAFFOLD-style local and global control variates to momentum before orthogonalization. It proves stationary convergence and convergence with any number of Newton–Schulz iterations, improving as the oracle is refined, and leads FedAvg/SCAFFOLD variants on Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10; evidence is limited to small vision federated tasks, not LLM-scale training.
source_title: FedMuon: Federated Learning with Bias-corrected LMO-based Optimization

summary: Modeling Muon and Shampoo by spectral gradient descent, this paper proves on imbalanced Gaussian mixtures that UVᵀ updates learn all principal components equally, unlike gradient descent’s majority-first dynamics; early-stopped minority and balanced-loss advantages grow linearly and persist against normalized gradient descent, while depth accelerates components and narrows their saturation gaps. Colored-MNIST, 20:1 CIFAR, Dominoes, CelebA/MultiNLI, and TinyStories support better minority learning than SGD, but Adam sometimes matches or beats Muon and theory is restricted to population squared-loss models.
source_title: How Muon's Spectral Design Benefits Generalization: A Study on Imbalanced Data

summary: Riemannion optimizes LoRA updates directly on the fixed-rank manifold, transporting momentum between tangent spaces, applying a Muon-like low-rank spectral oracle, and retracting by truncated SVD, thereby removing factorization-dependent behavior; a gradient-aligned randomized-SVD initialization adds negligible one-time cost. It improves Llama-3-8B commonsense accuracy and Stable-Diffusion-2 DreamBooth convergence, learning complex subjects in 600 steps, but offers no convergence theorem and tests only one backbone per modality.
source_title: LoRA meets Riemannion: Muon Optimizer for Parametrization-independent Low-Rank Adapters

summary: By ablating transformer blocks, this paper localizes Muon’s advantage to value-output attention and feed-forward associative memories: on 160M FineWeb, using Muon only there nearly matches full Muon, with losses 3.5858 versus 3.5654, while QK-only reaches 3.8925. A one-layer theory gives balanced learning for any orthonormal embeddings, and heavy-tailed QA tail accuracy is 0.976 versus Adam’s 0.264; the proof assumes orthonormal embeddings and two-group imbalance, and experiments stop at 0.7B.
source_title: Muon Outperforms Adam in Tail-End Associative Memory Learning

summary: MuonBP avoids Muon’s model-parallel all-gathers on most steps by orthogonalizing local shards, periodically restoring a global orthogonalization, with theory requiring distinct block and full-step learning rates and interpolating between BlockMuon and Muon. With period five it cuts optimizer communication 5×; on Llama-style models through 8B it preserves or improves perplexity, raises throughput 8%, and reaches target perplexity 10–13% sooner, though period selection and large-scale Dion comparisons remain open.
source_title: MuonBP: Faster Muon via Block-Periodic Orthogonalization

summary: Unlike prior Muon theory that assumes an exact SVD oracle, this paper models practical Newton–Schulz orthogonalization as an additive-error linear minimization oracle and derives deterministic and stochastic momentum bounds whose degradation is explicit in the approximation error. NanoGPT/FineWeb and CIFAR-10 sweeps support its prediction that lower precision needs a smaller learning rate and larger momentum; the analysis assumes a uniform bounded oracle error, and validation stops short of full-scale LLM training.
source_title: Beyond the Ideal: Analyzing the Inexact Muon Update

summary: Muon-NSR and the extra-hyperparameter-free Muon-VS maintain an elementwise gradient-variance EMA and use it to scale Nesterov momentum before Newton–Schulz, adding Adam-like noise adaptivity while retaining an orthogonal output; NSR gates by noise-to-signal ratio, whereas VS whitens by estimated variance. GPT-2/LLaMA tests up to 1.2B report lower loss and 1.36× fewer steps than tuned Muon, but require a full extra buffer, lack convergence theory, and weaken when batches are too small.
source_title: Variance-Adaptive Muon: Accelerating LLM Pretraining with NSR-Modulated and Variance-Scaled Momentum

summary: Using simplified Muon with exact matrix-sign updates, this paper shows spectral dynamics decouple into scalar recurrences for symmetric matrix factorization and one-layer linear-transformer in-context learning, yielding linear convergence independent of condition number while GD and SignGD incur polynomial condition-number dependence. Synthetic matrix experiments across condition numbers and ranks match the theory; the result covers only two stylized problems, omits momentum and approximate orthogonalization, and relies on special initialization regimes.
source_title: Preconditioning Benefits of Spectral Orthogonalization in Muon

summary: IFNSO replaces a recursively composed Newton–Schulz chain with one learned polynomial expressed through repeatedly squared residual powers, leaving only one multiplication by the long matrix dimension while preserving its orthogonalization target. Matrix tests report 0.040 error versus 0.330 for the strongest comparator and roughly 4× fewer FLOPs, with 98.87% MNIST accuracy; it has no convergence theory or LLM validation, can fluctuate near convergence, and remains expensive for highly rectangular matrices.
source_title: IFNSO: Iteration-Free Newton-Schulz Orthogonalization

summary: Spectral Sphere Optimization constrains both two-dimensional weights and updates to a μP-scaled spectral sphere, using top-singular-vector tangent projection and a bisection-solved Lagrange multiplier instead of Muon’s update-only control. A 1.7B dense model reaches AdamW’s target loss in 19% fewer steps (Muon: 12%), with gains on downstream, MoE, and 200-layer stability tests; the root solver and extra matrix-sign work make SSO 11.45% slower per step than Muon.
source_title: Controlled LLM Training on Spectral Sphere

summary: Muon++ projects momentum away from the current weight’s leading left and right singular vectors before applying matrix sign, preserving the top singular value—and therefore μP spectral conditions—throughout training without repeatedly renormalizing moderate-width weights. It proves a spectral-gap step-size condition and analyzes adaptive scaling under a correlated-Gaussian model, but provides no training experiments; ultra-wide layers still need explicit rescaling, and the theory assumes a unique leading mode and simplified gradient–weight correlation.
source_title: Towards a Principled Muon under $μ\mathsf{P}$: Ensuring Spectral Conditions throughout Training

summary: Muon-MVR imports STORM-style variance-reduced momentum into the Gluon linear-minimization-oracle framework, correcting momentum with same-sample gradient differences and extending the analysis to general norms and layerwise generalized smoothness. It improves the nonconvex rate from O(K^-1/4) to O(K^-1/3), and the star-convex rate from about O(K^-1/3) to O(K^-1/2); one 124M NanoGPT run improves loss from 3.832 to 3.682, but extra gradient-difference cost, transient spikes, and large-scale robustness remain unquantified.
source_title: Muon is Provably Faster with Momentum Variance Reduction

summary: These LMO momentum methods add a Hessian–vector correction along the previous step—evaluated either at a random interpolation point or the new iterate—to exploit second-order information without forming the Hessian, unlike ordinary Polyak momentum. Under relaxed gradient smoothness (and Hessian smoothness for one variant) they achieve O(K^-1/3) nonconvex stationarity versus O(K^-1/4), while small MLP/LSTM experiments are mixed; no Muon-scale LLM or wall-clock study establishes whether the extra HVP pays off.
source_title: Better LMO-based Momentum Methods with Second-Order Information

summary: By deriving duals of Ky Fan k-norms, this paper shows their LMO is a rank-k sum of leading singular-vector pairs and builds the Fanion family, which connects rank-one Neon, low-rank Dion, and full-rank Muon; conic combinations further mix normalized or sign updates. Thick-restart Lanczos makes low-rank variants practical, but CIFAR-10 and GPT experiments mostly match rather than beat Muon, and native PyTorch support and theory explaining the empirical trade-off are absent.
source_title: The Ky Fan Norms and Beyond: Dual Norms and Combinations for Matrix Optimization

summary: This work derives width/depth scaling rules for the learning rate and epsilon of Shampoo, SOAP, and Muon under μP, including blocking and grafting, and argues compute-optimal independent weight decay should scale inversely with width. FineWeb pretraining from 190M to 1.4B yields roughly 1.4× compute speedups over tuned AdamW, while incorrect scaling erases most of Muon’s gain; reported FLOP speedups exclude optimizer-transform overhead, span under one decade of width, and may not extrapolate to larger models.
source_title: Hyperparameter Transfer Enables Consistent Gains of Matrix-Preconditioned Optimizers Across Scales

summary: Turbo-Muon replaces Frobenius initialization of Newton–Schulz with a cheap Gershgorin/AOL column preconditioner, reuses the initial Gram matrix, and removes one of five iterations while remaining a descent direction under an induced norm. On 4096×4096 matrices the core routine is 2.83× faster, and NanoGPT, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet runs save up to 3.6% end-to-end time at similar quality; theory assumes the exact polar factor even though deployment uses a finite approximation.
source_title: Turbo-Muon: Almost-Orthogonal Pre-Conditioning for Fast Muon Updates

summary: The paper predicts a spectral block update beats a Euclidean one when the gradient’s squared nuclear-to-Frobenius ratio exceeds the incoming activation’s stable rank, then proves low stable rank at Gaussian initialization and dimension-growing gradient nuclear rank over long windows in spiked random-feature models. Synthetic and NanoGPT diagnostics support the criterion and a SwiGLU counterexample violates it as predicted, but the analysis compares ideal one-step SpecGD with GD—not practical momentum Muon or AdamW—and large-transformer causal ablations remain open.
source_title: When do spectral gradient updates help in deep learning?

summary: Preconditioned matrix norms unify steepest descent, Kronecker quasi-Newton, and elementwise adaptive methods by applying a base-norm LMO in a transformed gradient space, yielding necessary-and-sufficient affine/scale-invariance conditions and the spectral–adaptive hybrids MuAdam and MuAdam-SANIA. DistilBERT GLUE, Qwen2-7B LoRA, and small Shakespeare tests are competitive but inconsistent across tasks; the work gives invariance rather than convergence guarantees and does not test full LLM pretraining or quantify preconditioning overhead.
source_title: Preconditioned Norms: A Unified Framework for Steepest Descent, Quasi-Newton and Adaptive Methods

summary: NorMuon keeps Muon’s orthogonalization but tracks one second-moment scalar per output neuron and row-normalizes the orthogonalized update, addressing Muon’s uneven neuron norms with negligible state; its FSDP2 implementation distributes full-matrix orthogonalizations and uses shard-local normalization. Across 124M–5.4B pretraining it reduces steps to AdamW’s loss by 21.74% at 1.1B and 13.91% at 5.4B, but increases communication volume by 33–50% and offers no convergence analysis.
source_title: NorMuon: Making Muon more efficient and scalable

summary: DP-Adam-AC augments DP-Adam with history-percentile adaptive clipping, clip-rate-driven learning-rate nudges, evaluation-only EMA, microbatch clipping, and a variable-sampling-rate Rényi privacy accountant, targeting short private fine-tuning of locally runnable models. One-epoch Qwen2.5-0.5B and BitNet-2B tests show the expected privacy–loss trade-off at ε≈1.75–12.57, but use only two synthetic 10,000-example datasets, measure mainly training loss, and omit competing private optimizers, leaving utility and generality weakly established.
source_title: DP-Adam-AC: Privacy-preserving Fine-Tuning of Localizable Language Models Using Adam Optimization with Adaptive Clipping

summary: Hill-ADAM deterministically alternates Adam minimization and maximization whenever loss improvement falls below a threshold, resets moments at each switch, escapes runaway ascent with a loss ceiling, and returns the best visited state instead of settling at the first basin. It finds equal or lower minima on five hand-designed polynomials and a 12-case color-correction task, but has no global-convergence guarantee, is sensitive to switching/ceiling thresholds and learning rate, and is untested on standard high-dimensional learning benchmarks.
source_title: Explore the Loss space with Hill-ADAM

summary: DeMuon combines local Muon matrix-sign steps with gradient tracking and graph mixing so heterogeneous peers approach both stationarity and consensus without a central server; DeMuon-A adds multi-extrapolation under higher-order smoothness. Dimension-free analysis gives O(K^-1/4) stationarity for DeMuon and O(K^-p/(3p+1)) for the accelerated variant, while an eight-node 7.4M GPT experiment beats decentralized SGD baselines across three topologies; theory assumes exact matrix sign, and empirical scale and communication-cost evidence are limited.
source_title: DeMuon: A Decentralized Muon for Matrix Optimization over Graphs

summary: Conda periodically estimates an orthogonal subspace by SVD, projects Adam’s first and second moments into it, and applies column-wise variance normalization, retaining Adam adaptivity while avoiding Muon’s full singular-value flattening; lazy updates every 2,000 steps limit overhead. LLaMA 60M–1B and GPT-2 tests report up to 2.7× step-based and about 2.5× wall-clock convergence speed over AdamW plus better downstream results, but 13B and MoE scalability are untested and SVD adds state and compute.
source_title: Conda: Column-Normalized Adam for Training Large Language Models Faster

summary: Muon-MVR2 corrects momentum using same-minibatch gradients at the current and previous iterates, unlike cheaper one-batch MVR1, and with horizon-free schedules attains the optimal anytime O(T^-1/3) stochastic nonconvex rate versus O(T^-1/4) for standard/MVR1 Muon, plus PL guarantees. CIFAR-10 and 130M LLaMA/C4 tests favor MVR2 per step, but its second gradient roughly doubles wall time; theory assumes exact matrix signs and omits finite Newton–Schulz, practical schedules, and weight decay.
source_title: On the Convergence of Muon and Beyond

summary: AdaGrad++ and Adam++ replace a tuned global learning rate with a simple trajectory-distance scale—maximum distance from initialization, normalized by dimension and, for Adam, time—while preserving the coordinatewise preconditioning of their namesakes. In convex stochastic optimization, AdaGrad++ retains O(T^-1/2) and Adam++ matches Adam’s rate; CIFAR-10 and GPT-2 experiments show modest gains, but nonconvex guarantees are absent and the experimentally used AdamW++ has no proof.
source_title: Towards Simple and Provable Parameter-Free Adaptive Gradient Methods

summary: AdaGrad++ and Adam++ replace a tuned global learning rate with a simple trajectory-distance scale—maximum distance from initialization, normalized by dimension and, for Adam, time—while preserving the coordinatewise preconditioning of their namesakes. In convex stochastic optimization, AdaGrad++ retains O(T^-1/2) and Adam++ matches Adam’s rate; CIFAR-10 and GPT-2 experiments show modest gains, but nonconvex guarantees are absent and the experimentally used AdamW++ has no proof.
source_title: Towards Simple and Provable Parameter-Free Adaptive Gradient Methods

summary: Low-rank Muon Gaussian-sketches momentum, QR-factorizes the sketch, orthogonalizes only QᵀM, then lifts the result, replacing full Newton–Schulz while suppressing noise-sensitive tail singular directions. It proves near-optimal MSGD stationarity and optimal epsilon dependence under heavy-tailed noise, while GPT-2/LLaMA tests through 1B usually beat tuned Muon at ranks 100–200; end-to-end savings are modest, small models can regress, and rank selection or safeguarded error checks add overhead.
source_title: Low-rank Orthogonalization for Large-scale Matrix Optimization with Applications to Foundation Model Training

summary: SRON rescales each two-dimensional gradient row by its current RMS before an SGD step, targeting attention-induced row-scale disparities without momentum, SVD, or persistent state; unlike global normalization, it preserves matrix structure. Under bounded-gradient/variance assumptions it proves O(log T/√T) nonconvex stationarity, and LLaMA/GPT/Gemma tests through 7B report 90–100% less optimizer state and up to 67% less time; the best hybrid still uses Adam for nonmatrix parameters, while fully state-free SRON† loses accuracy.
source_title: SRON: State-free LLM Training via Row-wise Gradient Normalization

summary: KL-Shampoo jointly estimates both Kronecker covariance factors by minimizing Gaussian KL divergence, then uses infrequent QR bases and per-step EMA eigenvalue corrections, unlike Shampoo’s one-sided Frobenius-motivated factors or SOAP’s full Adam state. Across four language models up to 227M, plus a 450M check, 150-run searches show it beats Shampoo/SOAP without grafting at SOAP-like iteration cost; no optimizer convergence theorem is given, and evidence remains sub-billion-scale after unusually extensive tuning.
source_title: Understanding and Improving Shampoo and SOAP via Kullback-Leibler Minimization

summary: ZO Fine-tuner replaces MeZO’s fixed isotropic Gaussian sampling with tiny per-parameter-block networks that predict normalized perturbation variances from compressed model and loss statistics, meta-trained once along a first-order trajectory and then reused. A block-diagonal-Hessian argument gives a tighter one-step expected-loss bound, and four LLMs across seven datasets win 82.1% of loss comparisons at near-MeZO memory; the result is not a global convergence theorem, and diagonal variances ignore cross-parameter correlations.
source_title: Learning a Zeroth-Order Optimizer for Fine-Tuning LLMs

summary: AdaMuon sign-transforms first-moment matrices before Newton–Schulz, tracks an elementwise EMA of squared orthogonal directions, divides by that RMS, and rescales to Adam-like update magnitude, adding coordinate adaptivity absent from Muon. GPT-2 and Qwen2.5 pretraining experiments through 7B report up to 40% token-efficiency gains, while an O(log T/√T) bound assumes directional alignment; the full second-moment buffer forfeits Muon’s memory advantage and adds compute.
source_title: AdaMuon: Adaptive Muon Optimizer

summary: SCALE normalizes every matrix-gradient column and applies first-moment momentum only to the output layer, retaining essentially SGD elsewhere; this bottom-up design seeks the minimum useful state rather than compressing Adam’s two moments. LLaMA/Qwen experiments from 60M to 7B match or beat Adam, Muon, GaLore, Fira, and APOLLO using 35–45% of Adam’s total memory, with theory supporting variance-targeted momentum; evidence stops at 7B/100B tokens and the 7B comparison is a single run.
source_title: Memory-Efficient LLM Pretraining via Minimalist Optimizer Design

summary: SPlus replaces Shampoo’s inverse-square-root preconditioned gradient with a bounded instant-sign update in a historical eigenbasis, adds symmetric shape scaling for width-transferable learning rates, and averages fast iterates to suppress high-rate noise. Transformer language, vision, and diffusion tests match Adam in 44–58% of steps and 62–83% of wall time, but the empirically designed method lacks convergence theory, uses roughly 60% more memory than Adam for square layers, and still pays periodic eigendecompositions.
source_title: A Stable Whitening Optimizer for Efficient Neural Network Training

summary: This paper does not alter Muon; it analyzes exact matrix-sign updates under Frobenius-, spectral-, and nonuniform-smoothness models, showing any advantage over GD arises when blockwise Hessians are low rank or the trajectory-averaged curvature J is small. Quadratic, MNIST, MLP, and six-layer GPT-2 experiments track the predicted ratios, but the evidence is small-scale and relies on exact orthogonalization plus structural, star-convex, or bounded-third-derivative assumptions rather than production Muon.
source_title: On the Convergence Analysis of Muon

summary: PolarGrad multiplies a gradient’s polar factor by its nuclear norm, restoring update magnitudes that vanish with the gradient, and replaces Muon’s tuned Newton–Schulz approximation with QDWH or ZOLO-PD. Under smooth PL objectives this yields linear convergence where constant-step matrix-sign descent reaches a floor; matrix problems and small Qwen/GPT-2 runs are favorable, but momentum/non-PL theory is left open, GPT-2 losses are often similar, and scalable distributed implementations remain future work.
source_title: PolarGrad: A Class of Matrix-Gradient Optimizers from a Unifying Preconditioning Perspective

summary: Polar Express replaces Muon’s fixed Newton–Schulz polynomial with per-iteration odd polynomials chosen by a minimax problem over the current singular-value interval, plus safeguards for bfloat16. It proves worst-case-optimal, super-exponential polar-factor convergence and gives small but consistent GPT-2 gains over recent five-step alternatives from 1B to 10B tokens; benefits shrink with longer training, CIFAR results are inconclusive, and the method depends on a supplied lower singular-value bound.
source_title: The Polar Express: Optimal Matrix Sign Methods and Their Application to the Muon Algorithm

summary: Gluon formalizes practical Muon/Scion as independent layer-wise linear-minimization-oracle steps with adaptive radii and introduces layer-wise (L0,L1)-smoothness, replacing prior global smoothness analyses that prescribe unusably small steps. Deterministic theory produces radii close to tuned values, stochastic convergence is also established, and 124M NanoGPT plus CIFAR-10 trajectories support the model; however, theory assumes exact LMOs and bounded variance, while adaptive-radius guarantees remain deterministic.
source_title: Gluon: Making Muon & Scion Great Again! (Bridging Theory and Practice of LMO-based Optimizers for LLMs)

summary: Rather than comparing optimizers at fixed resources, this study maps compute-time Pareto frontiers across model sizes, batch sizes, and TPU counts. Muon needs about 10-15% fewer tokens than AdamW at matched training loss, with the advantage remaining beyond the critical batch size; a 3.7B model trained for 160B tokens combines Muon with maximal-update parameterization and telescoping hyperparameter transfer. The proposed tuning strategy reduces search complexity to O(C log N), but evaluation uses fresh-batch training loss as a generalization proxy, relies on an in-house JAX implementation, and provides no downstream evaluation outside language pretraining.
source_title: Practical Efficiency of Muon for Pretraining

summary: Across small modular-arithmetic and parity tasks with softmax, stablemax, and sparsemax attention, this study reports that Muon reaches stable 95% validation accuracy earlier than AdamW: pooled mean grokking epochs are 102.89 versus 153.09, with a reported p-value of 6.33e-8. It establishes an early empirical link between orthogonalized updates and grokking but does not isolate Newton-Schulz from update scaling, pool task effects with limited per-task detail, and remains confined to small algorithmic transformers; later work provides the missing mechanism ablation.
source_title: Muon Optimizer Accelerates Grokking

summary: Dion replaces Muon’s full-matrix Newton–Schulz pass with amortized power iteration on a slowly changing momentum buffer; sharding-aware low-rank factors, rank fraction, and error feedback compress both computation and communication. GPT-style models through 3B retain Muon-like convergence and hyperparameter transfer, with larger models tolerating lower rank, but extreme-scale timing is simulated rather than trained, results cover only language models, and low ranks degrade quality unless error feedback and rank are carefully chosen.
source_title: Dion: Distributed Orthonormalized Updates

summary: COSMOS tracks only the leading eigenspace of the gradient second moment, applies SOAP-style coordinate adaptation there, and uses a Muon matrix-sign update on the orthogonal residual, unlike either optimizer alone. LLaMA/GPT-2 tests through 1B improve perplexity with roughly 13d² state versus SOAP’s 66d² and near-Muon wall time, but there is no convergence theory, rank and mixture weights still need choices, and 1B comparisons omit SOAP because of resource limits.
source_title: COSMOS: A Hybrid Adaptive Optimizer for Memory-Efficient Training of LLMs

summary: This report makes Muon scalable by adding decoupled weight decay, shape-dependent scaling that fixes update RMS and matches AdamW’s learning-rate convention, plus a ZeRO-1-style sharded momentum implementation that gathers only the matrix being orthogonalized. Scaling-law fits estimate 52% of AdamW’s FLOPs, and Moonlight trains a 3B-active/16B-total MoE for 5.7T tokens; evidence centers on one proprietary pipeline, distributed Muon adds communication, and pretrain/finetune optimizer mismatch remains unresolved.
source_title: Muon is Scalable for LLM Training

summary: Scion chooses architecture-aware norm balls and applies layerwise linear minimization oracles—sign for vector-like groups and spectral/polar updates for matrices—optionally constraining weights, rather than learning Adam-style geometry online. Its uSCG/SCG theory gives order-optimal O(n^-1/4) stochastic nonconvex stationarity without knowing smoothness, while NanoGPT through 3B and vision tests show learning-rate transfer, large-batch robustness, and one-weight/one-gradient memory; guarantees still assume smoothness and bounded variance, and large-scale evidence is limited to a single 3B run.
source_title: Training Deep Learning Models with Norm-Constrained LMOs

summary: Muon orthogonalizes Nesterov momentum for each two-dimensional weight with five GPU-friendly Newton–Schulz steps, approximating UVᵀ and therefore spectral-norm steepest descent; embeddings, heads, and vectors stay on AdamW. The blog reports a 35% NanoGPT speedrun gain and favorable 1.5B runs with sub-1% estimated FLOP overhead, but offers no convergence proof and explicitly leaves 20B-plus/trillion-token scaling, distributed execution, finetuning, and reinforcement learning untested.
source_title: Muon: An optimizer for hidden layers in neural networks

summary: PROFIT takes temporary reference-optimizer steps from the current converged model, treats their displacement as an implicit old-task direction, projects a new-task gradient away from it when they conflict, restores the weights, then applies any main optimizer—without old data or replay. Theory gives local old-loss protection and stable-point properties, and vision/VLM/motion tests reduce forgetting, but no full convergence proof is supplied; each update needs extra batches and roughly 25% more memory in the vanilla implementation.
source_title: PROFIT: A Specialized Optimizer for Deep Fine Tuning

summary: Cautious optimizers mask coordinates where a momentum-based proposal disagrees in sign with the current gradient, then renormalize surviving coordinates, adding one line to AdamW, Lion, or MARS without retuning. Lyapunov/Hamiltonian analysis preserves base-optimizer descent guarantees, and LLM plus Mini-ImageNet experiments improve stability, but it does not prove a strictly faster global rate; after exhaustive tuning, 130M–1.2B perplexity gains are only 0.1–1%, and broader RL/continual-learning tests remain future work.
source_title: Cautious Optimizers: Improving Training with One Line of Code

summary: MARS injects a scaled STORM correction—the same-sample gradient difference between current and previous iterates—into AdamW, Lion, or Shampoo, clips the corrected estimator, and builds preconditioners from it. Under smoothness, bounded variance, and positive-definite preconditioners it proves O(log T/T^(1/3)) convergence, while GPT-2 tests through 770M improve token and wall-clock efficiency; exact MARS needs a second gradient, so headline experiments use an approximation without the same guarantee, and evidence is confined largely to GPT-2.
source_title: MARS: Unleashing the Power of Variance Reduction for Training Large Models

summary: Subset-Norm shares AdaGrad-style scale estimates across carefully chosen coordinate groups, reducing adaptive-state memory from O(d) to O(sqrt(d)), while Subspace-Momentum stores momentum only in a low-dimensional subspace and applies SGD in its complement. Both receive high-probability nonconvex guarantees; combined on LLaMA-1B, they reached Adam's perplexity in 6.8B rather than 13.1B tokens while cutting optimizer-state memory by over 80% with little extra tuning.
source_title: Lean and Mean Adaptive Optimization via Subset-Norm and Subspace-Momentum with Convergence Guarantees

summary: ADOPT breaks the harmful dependence between Adam's current gradient and current variance estimate by normalizing with the previous second moment and applying normalization before the momentum update. These small ordering changes yield the optimal O(1/sqrt(T)) nonconvex rate for any beta2 without uniformly bounded gradient noise, unlike many Adam repairs; extensive image, generative, language, and reinforcement-learning experiments also outperformed Adam-family baselines.
source_title: ADOPT: Modified Adam Can Converge with Any $β_2$ with the Optimal Rate

summary: COAT extends FP8 beyond linear-layer arithmetic to the two major remaining memory consumers: optimizer states and saved activations. Dynamic Range Expansion reshapes state distributions to use FP8's range accurately, while mixed-granularity activation quantization chooses per-tensor or per-group scaling by operator sensitivity; LLM/VLM training retained near-lossless quality while using 1.54x less end-to-end memory and running 1.43x faster than BF16, enabling larger batches or fewer GPUs.
source_title: COAT: Compressing Optimizer states and Activation for Memory-Efficient FP8 Training

summary: LDAdam performs Adam updates in rotating low-rank subspaces while still exploring the full parameter space, introducing projection-aware moment transport so statistics remain meaningful when the basis changes. Block power iteration selects each subspace, and generalized error feedback corrects compression of both gradients and optimizer states; convergence follows under standard assumptions, while language-model pretraining and fine-tuning matched full Adam closely at a fraction of its state memory.
source_title: LDAdam: Adaptive Optimization from Low-Dimensional Gradient Statistics

summary: SOAP proves that half-power Shampoo is Adafactor in Shampoo's eigenbasis, then replaces Adafactor there with Adam and continuously updates diagonal moments between infrequent basis refreshes. This prevents the degradation caused by simply making Shampoo decompositions stale and leaves only refresh frequency beyond Adam's hyperparameters; on 360M/660M language models, SOAP cut iterations by over 40% and wall time by over 35% versus AdamW, improving both metrics about 20% over Shampoo.
source_title: SOAP: Improving and Stabilizing Shampoo using Adam

summary: AdEMAMix challenges single-timescale momentum by mixing a fast EMA for recent gradients with a very slow EMA that preserves information for tens of thousands of steps, then schedules the older component into Adam's update. The added long memory both accelerates optimization and reduces forgetting: a 1.3B model trained on 101B tokens matched an AdamW model trained on 197B, showing that old gradients remain useful far longer than conventional momentum assumes.
source_title: The AdEMAMix Optimizer: Better, Faster, Older

summary: Adam-mini uses observed block structure in neural-network Hessians to replace Adam's per-parameter second moments with one adaptive rate per structurally chosen block while retaining first momentum. The analysis suggests at least 99.9% of Adam's distinct rates are redundant; across 39M–13B models, pretraining, SFT, and RLHF matched or beat AdamW with roughly 50% less optimizer memory, and Llama-2-7B throughput rose 49.6% on two A800 GPUs, saving 33% wall time.
source_title: Adam-mini: Use Fewer Learning Rates To Gain More

summary: MicroAdam sparsifies or compresses gradients before they enter Adam's moments, then controls the lost information with error feedback whose correction buffer is itself compressed—avoiding the full-size residual that would erase the memory gain. Its analysis shifts compression effects into higher-order terms and matches AMSGrad's asymptotic guarantees for smooth nonconvex and PL objectives; GPU experiments on BERT- and LLaMA-scale models remained competitive with uncompressed Adam in convergence and runtime while using less memory.
source_title: MicroAdam: Accurate Adaptive Optimization with Low Space Overhead and Provable Convergence

summary: Schedule-Free optimization derives a direct equivalence between learning-rate decay and iterate averaging, then evaluates gradients at an interpolation of running and averaged iterates so a constant-rate momentum optimizer can obtain scheduled-like behavior without knowing the stopping horizon.
